5.32.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tathānyo'sti dvijaśreṣṭhāstasminkṣetre śubhāvahe ..
saptarṣīṇāṃ suvikhyāta āśramaḥ sarvakāmadaḥ .. 1 ..
5.32.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तथान्योऽस्ति द्विजश्रेष्ठास्तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे शुभावहे ..
सप्तर्षीणां सुविख्यात आश्रमः सर्वकामदः .. 1 ..
5.32.m: Sūta said: / Likewise, O best of the twice-born, in that auspicious field there is another / well-renowned hermitage of the Seven Seers which grants all desires.

5.32.s:
tatra śrāvaṇamāsasya paṃcadaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ ..
yaḥ karoti naraḥ snānaṃ sa labhedvāṃchitaṃ phalam .. 2 ..
5.32.d:
तत्र श्रावणमासस्य पंचदश्यां समाहितः ..
यः करोति नरः स्नानं स लभेद्वांछितं फलम् .. 2 ..
5.32.m: A person who, with mind restrained, takes a ritual ablution there on the fifteenth day of the month of Śrāvaṇa, / obtains the desired fruit.

5.32.s:
kandamūlaphalaiḥ śākairyastatra śrāddhamācaret ..
sa prāpnoti phalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ .. 3 ..
5.32.d:
कन्दमूलफलैः शाकैर्यस्तत्र श्राद्धमाचरेत् ..
स प्राप्नोति फलं कृत्स्नं राजसूयाश्वमेधयोः .. 3 ..
5.32.m: Whoever performs a śrāddha there with bulbs, roots, fruits, and vegetables, / attains the entire fruit of the rājasūya and aśvamedha sacrifices.

5.32.s:
paṃcamyāṃ śuklapakṣe tu māsi bhādrapade dvijāḥ ..
yastānpūjayate bhaktyā puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ ..
vidhinānena viprendrāḥ sarvāneva yathākramam .. 4 ..
5.32.d:
पंचम्यां शुक्लपक्षे तु मासि भाद्रपदे द्विजाः ..
यस्तान्पूजयते भक्त्या पुष्पधूपानुलेपनैः ..
विधिनानेन विप्रेन्द्राः सर्वानेव यथाक्रमम् .. 4 ..
5.32.m: On the fifth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Bhādrapada, O twice-born, / whoever worships them with devotion with flowers, incense, and ointments / according to this rite, O leaders of brahmins, all of them in order:

5.32.s:
oṃ atraye namaḥ ..
oṃ vasiṣṭhāya namaḥ ..
oṃ kaśyapāya namaḥ ..
oṃ bharadvājāya namaḥ ..
oṃ gautamāya namaḥ ..
oṃ kauśikāya namaḥ ..
oṃ jamadagnaye namaḥ ..
oṃ aruṃdhatyai namaḥ ..
.. pūjāmaṃtraḥ .. ..
jahnukanyāpavitrāṃgā gṛhītajapamālikāḥ ..
gṛhṇaṃtvarghaṃ mayā dattamṛṣayaḥ sarvakāmadāḥ .. 5 ..
5.32.d:
ओं अत्रये नमः ..
ओं वसिष्ठाय नमः ..
ओं कश्यपाय नमः ..
ओं भरद्वाजाय नमः ..
ओं गौतमाय नमः ..
ओं कौशिकाय नमः ..
ओं जमदग्नये नमः ..
ओं अरुंधत्यै नमः ..
.. पूजामंत्रः .. ..
जह्नुकन्यापवित्रांगा गृहीतजपमालिकाः ..
गृह्णंत्वर्घं मया दत्तमृषयः सर्वकामदाः .. 5 ..
5.32.m: "Oṃ, homage to Atri! / Oṃ, homage to Vasiṣṭha! / Oṃ, homage to Kaśyapa! / Oṃ, homage to Bharadvāja! / Oṃ, homage to Gautama! / Oṃ, homage to Kauśika! / Oṃ, homage to Jamadagni! / Oṃ, homage to Arundhatī!" / The mantra of worship: / "May the seers, granting all desires, whose limbs are purified by the Daughter of Jahnu, holding rosaries for japa, / accept the offering of water given by me!"

5.32.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
tatra saptarṣibhistīrthaṃ kasminkāle vyavasthitam ..
vistarātsūtaja brūhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ .. 6 ..
5.32.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
तत्र सप्तर्षिभिस्तीर्थं कस्मिन्काले व्यवस्थितम् ..
विस्तरात्सूतज ब्रूहि परं कौतूहलं हि नः .. 6 ..
5.32.m: The seers said: / "At what time was the sacred ford established there by the Seven Seers? / Tell in detail, O son of Sūta, for great indeed is our curiosity."

5.32.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
anāvṛṣṭiḥ purā jātā loke dvādaśavārṣikī ..
sarvoṣadhikṣayo jātastato lokāḥ kṣayārditāḥ .. 7 ..
5.32.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अनावृष्टिः पुरा जाता लोके द्वादशवार्षिकी ..
सर्वोषधिक्षयो जातस्ततो लोकाः क्षयार्दिताः .. 7 ..
5.32.m: Sūta said: / Formerly a twelve-year drought occurred in the world; / the loss of all herbs took place, and then people were oppressed by decay.

5.32.s:
asthiśeṣā nirutsāhāstyaktadharmavratakriyāḥ ..
abhakṣyabhakṣaṇaparāstathaivāpeyapāyinaḥ .. 8 ..
5.32.d:
अस्थिशेषा निरुत्साहास्त्यक्तधर्मव्रतक्रियाः ..
अभक्ष्यभक्षणपरास्तथैवापेयपायिनः .. 8 ..
5.32.m: With only bones remaining, devoid of energy, having abandoned the rites of virtue and vows, / intent on eating uneatable food, and likewise drinking undrinkable liquids,

5.32.s:
tyajaṃti mātaraḥ putrānkalatrāṇi tathā narāḥ ..
bhṛtyānsvānapi vitteśāḥ kā kathānyasamudbhavān .. 9 ..
5.32.d:
त्यजंति मातरः पुत्रान्कलत्राणि तथा नराः ..
भृत्यान्स्वानपि वित्तेशाः का कथान्यसमुद्भवान् .. 9 ..
5.32.m: mothers abandoned sons, and men abandoned wives; / masters of wealth even [abandoned] their own servants, not to speak of those born of others!

5.32.s:
saṃtyaktānyagnihotrāṇi brāhmaṇairyājakairapi ..
vratāni vratibhirdāṃtairapi vṛddhatamairdvijāḥ .. 6.32.10 ..
5.32.d:
संत्यक्तान्यग्निहोत्राणि ब्राह्मणैर्याजकैरपि ..
व्रतानि व्रतिभिर्दांतैरपि वृद्धतमैर्द्विजाः .. 6.32.10 ..
5.32.m: The agnihotra sacrifices were abandoned by the brahmins and by sacrificers; / vows were abandoned by the observant, even by the self-controlled, even by the oldest of elders, O twice-born!

5.32.s:
dṛśyate caiva yatraiva sasyaṃ vāpi kathaṃcana ..
hriyate lajjayā hīnaistatra kṣutkṣāmakairnaraiḥ .. 11 ..
5.32.d:
दृश्यते चैव यत्रैव सस्यं वापि कथंचन ..
ह्रियते लज्जया हीनैस्तत्र क्षुत्क्षामकैर्नरैः .. 11 ..
5.32.m: And wherever grain was seen somehow, / men emaciated by hunger, devoid of shame, seized it there.

5.32.s:
evamannakṣaye jāte pīḍite dharaṇītale ..
saptarṣayaḥ kṣudhāviṣṭā babhramustatratatra ca.. 12 ..
5.32.d:
एवमन्नक्षये जाते पीडिते धरणीतले ..
सप्तर्षयः क्षुधाविष्टा बभ्रमुस्तत्रतत्र च.. 12 ..
5.32.m: When food was thus exhausted and the surface of the earth was afflicted, / the seven seers, overcome with hunger, wandered here and there:

5.32.s:
atriścaiva vasiṣṭhaśca kaśyapaḥ sumahātapāḥ ..
bharadvājastathā cānyo gautamaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ..
kauśiko jamadagniśca tathaivāruṃdhatī satī .. 13 ..
5.32.d:
अत्रिश्चैव वसिष्ठश्च कश्यपः सुमहातपाः ..
भरद्वाजस्तथा चान्यो गौतमः संशितव्रतः..
कौशिको जमदग्निश्च तथैवारुंधती सती .. 13 ..
5.32.m: Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa of great austerity, / and likewise Bharadvāja, another [being] Gautama of strict vows, / Kauśika, and Jamadagni, as well as the virtuous Arundhatī.

5.32.s:
atha teṣāṃ samastānāṃ caṃḍābhūtparicārikā ..
paśuvaktrastathā bhṛtyo vinayena samavitaḥ .. 14 ..
5.32.d:
अथ तेषां समस्तानां चंडाभूत्परिचारिका ..
पशुवक्त्रस्तथा भृत्यो विनयेन समवितः .. 14 ..
5.32.m: Now Caṇḍā was the female attendant of them all, / and Paśuvaktra was their servant, endowed with humility.

5.32.s:
tataste viṣayaṃ prāptā vṛṣādarbhimahīpateḥ ..
kṣutkṣāmā munayo'tyarthaṃ deśe cānartasaṃjñake .. 15 ..
tatra bhikṣākṛte bhrāṃtāstataścaiva gṛhādgṛham ..
na grāsamapi sasyasya prāpnuvaṃste dvijottamāḥ ...6..
5.32.d:
ततस्ते विषयं प्राप्ता वृषादर्भिमहीपतेः ..
क्षुत्क्षामा मुनयोऽत्यर्थं देशे चानर्तसंज्ञके .. 15 ..
तत्र भिक्षाकृते भ्रांतास्ततश्चैव गृहाद्गृहम् ..
न ग्रासमपि सस्यस्य प्राप्नुवंस्ते द्विजोत्तमाः ...6..
5.32.m:
Then, exceedingly emaciated by hunger, the sages arrived at the territory / of King Vṛṣādarbhi, in the country named Ānarta.
There they wandered from house to house for the sake of alms, / but those best of brahmins did not receive even a mouthful of grain.

5.32.s:
tatastaiḥ patito bhūmau dṛṣṭo mṛtakumārakaḥ ..
maṃtrayitvā mithaḥ paścādgṛhīto bhakṣaṇāya ca .. 17 ..
5.32.d:
ततस्तैः पतितो भूमौ दृष्टो मृतकुमारकः ..
मंत्रयित्वा मिथः पश्चाद्गृहीतो भक्षणाय च .. 17 ..
5.32.m: Then they saw a dead boy fallen on the ground; / having conferred together, they then picked him up to eat.

5.32.s:
apacanyāvadagnau taṃ kṣudhayā paripīḍitāḥ ..
vṛṣādarbhirnṛpaḥ prāptaḥ śrutvā teṣāṃ viceṣṭitam .. 18 ..
5.32.d:
अपचन्यावदग्नौ तं क्षुधया परिपीडिताः ..
वृषादर्भिर्नृपः प्राप्तः श्रुत्वा तेषां विचेष्टितम् .. 18 ..
5.32.m: While they, tortured by hunger, were cooking him in the fire, / King Vṛṣādarbhi arrived, having heard of their deed.

5.32.s:
.. vṛṣādarbhiruvāca .. ..
kimidaṃ garhitaṃ karma kriyate munisattamāḥ ..
rākṣasānāmayaṃ dharmo mahāmāṃsasya bhakṣaṇam .. 19 ..
5.32.d:
.. वृषादर्भिरुवाच .. ..
किमिदं गर्हितं कर्म क्रियते मुनिसत्तमाः ..
राक्षसानामयं धर्मो महामांसस्य भक्षणम् .. 19 ..
5.32.m: Vṛṣādarbhi said: / "What is this despicable deed being done, O best of sages? / This eating of human flesh is the practice of rākṣasas!

5.32.s:
so'haṃ sasyaṃ pradāsyāmi grāmānvrīhīnyavānapi..
mama vākyādasaṃdigdhaṃ tyajardhvaṃ mṛtabālakam .. 6.32.20 ..
5.32.d:
सोऽहं सस्यं प्रदास्यामि ग्रामान्व्रीहीन्यवानपि..
मम वाक्यादसंदिग्धं त्यजर्ध्वं मृतबालकम् .. 6.32.20 ..
5.32.m: I shall give you grain, villages, rice, and barley; / at my word, without hesitation, abandon the dead child!"

5.32.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
prāyaścittaṃ samādiṣṭaṃ mahāmāṃsasya bhakṣaṇāt ..
pratigrahasya bhūpālā dāpatkāle'pi no nṛpa .. 21 ..
5.32.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
प्रायश्चित्तं समादिष्टं महामांसस्य भक्षणात् ..
प्रतिग्रहस्य भूपाला दापत्कालेऽपि नो नृप .. 21 ..
5.32.m: The seers said: / "An expiation is prescribed for eating human flesh, / but never for accepting gifts from kings, even in times of distress, O king!

5.32.s:
paścāttapaścariṣyāmo mahāmāṃsasamudbhavam ..
pātakaṃ nāśayiṣyāmo bhakṣayāmo vayaṃ tataḥ .. 22 ..
5.32.d:
पश्चात्तपश्चरिष्यामो महामांससमुद्भवम् ..
पातकं नाशयिष्यामो भक्षयामो वयं ततः .. 22 ..
5.32.m: Afterwards we shall perform penance arising from [eating] human flesh, / and destroy the sin; therefore we shall eat it."

5.32.s:
.. vṛṣādarbhi ruvāca .. ..
pratigraho dvijātīnāṃ proktā vṛttiraniṃditā ..
grāhyo mattastataḥ sarvairnātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 23 ..
5.32.d:
.. वृषादर्भि रुवाच .. ..
प्रतिग्रहो द्विजातीनां प्रोक्ता वृत्तिरनिंदिता ..
ग्राह्यो मत्तस्ततः सर्वैर्नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 23 ..
5.32.m: Vṛṣādarbhi said: / "Accepting gifts is declared to be the blameless livelihood of the twice-born; / therefore it should be taken from me by all; no doubt should be made here."

5.32.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
rāja pratigraho ghoro madhvāsvādo viṣopamaḥ ..
sa dūrādbrāhmaṇaistyājyo viśeṣātkṛtibhirnṛpa .. 24 ..
5.32.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
राज प्रतिग्रहो घोरो मध्वास्वादो विषोपमः ..
स दूराद्ब्राह्मणैस्त्याज्यो विशेषात्कृतिभिर्नृप .. 24 ..
5.32.m: The seers said: / "Accepting gifts from a king is dreadful, sweet to taste but like poison; / it should be avoided from afar by brahmins, especially by men of virtue, O king!

5.32.s:
daśasūnāsamaścakrī daśacakrisamo dhvajī ..
daśa dhvajisamā veśyā daśaveśyāsamo nṛpaḥ .. 25 ..
5.32.d:
दशसूनासमश्चक्री दशचक्रिसमो ध्वजी ..
दश ध्वजिसमा वेश्या दशवेश्यासमो नृपः .. 25 ..
5.32.m: An oil-presser is equal to ten slaughterhouses; an owner of a liquor-flag is equal to ten oil-pressers; / a courtesan is equal to ten owners of liquor-flags; a king is equal to ten courtesans.

5.32.s:
daśasūnāsahasreṇa tulyo rājapratigrahaḥ ..
kastasya pratigṛhṇāti lobhāḍhyo brāhmaṇo yathā .. 26 ..
5.32.d:
दशसूनासहस्रेण तुल्यो राजप्रतिग्रहः ..
कस्तस्य प्रतिगृह्णाति लोभाढ्यो ब्राह्मणो यथा .. 26 ..
5.32.m: Accepting a gift from a king is equal to ten thousand slaughterhouses. / Who would accept it, like a greedy brahmin?

5.32.s:
rauravādiṣu sarveṣu narakeṣu sa pacyate ..
tasmādgaccha gṛhe bhūpa svasti te'stu sadaiva hi .. 27 ..
5.32.d:
रौरवादिषु सर्वेषु नरकेषु स पच्यते ..
तस्माद्गच्छ गृहे भूप स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु सदैव हि .. 27 ..
5.32.m: He cooks in all the hells, such as Raurava. / Therefore go home, O king; may there always be welfare for you!

5.32.s:
vayamanyatra yāsyāmo grahīṣyāmo na te dhanam ..
evamuktvātha te sarve munayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ .. 28 ..
5.32.d:
वयमन्यत्र यास्यामो ग्रहीष्यामो न ते धनम् ..
एवमुक्त्वाथ ते सर्वे मुनयः शंसितव्रताः .. 28 ..
5.32.m: We will go elsewhere; we will not take your wealth." / Having spoken thus, all those sages of praiseworthy vows,

5.32.s:
parityajya kumāraṃ taṃ mṛtaṃ tamapi bhūmipam ..
camatkārapuraṃ kṣetraṃ samuddiśya tato yayuḥ .. 29 ..
5.32.d:
परित्यज्य कुमारं तं मृतं तमपि भूमिपम् ..
चमत्कारपुरं क्षेत्रं समुद्दिश्य ततो ययुः .. 29 ..
5.32.m: abandoning that dead boy as well as that king, / then set out toward the sacred field of Camatkārapura.

5.32.s:
so'pi rājā tatastaistu bhartsito'tiruṣānvitaḥ ..
jijñāsārthaṃ tatasteṣāṃ cakre karma dvijottamāḥ .. 6.32.30 ..
5.32.d:
सोऽपि राजा ततस्तैस्तु भर्त्सितोऽतिरुषान्वितः ..
जिज्ञासार्थं ततस्तेषां चक्रे कर्म द्विजोत्तमाः .. 6.32.30 ..
5.32.m: Then that king also, rebuked by them and filled with great anger, / performed an act to test them, O best of brahmins:

5.32.s:
tataḥ suvarṇapūrṇāni vidhāyodumbarāṇi ca ..
teṣāṃ mārgāgrato bhūmau samaṃtādatha cākṣipat .. 31 ..
5.32.d:
ततः सुवर्णपूर्णानि विधायोदुम्बराणि च ..
तेषां मार्गाग्रतो भूमौ समंतादथ चाक्षिपत् .. 31 ..
5.32.m: Having filled udumbara fruits with gold, / he then scattered them all around on the ground in front of their path.

5.32.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atha te munayo dṛṣṭvā patitāni dharātale ..
udumbarāṇi saṃdṛṣṭvā jagṛhuḥ kṣudhayārditāḥ .. 32 ..
5.32.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अथ ते मुनयो दृष्ट्वा पतितानि धरातले ..
उदुम्बराणि संदृष्ट्वा जगृहुः क्षुधयार्दिताः .. 32 ..
5.32.m: Sūta said: / Then those sages, seeing the udumbara fruits / fallen on the earth, took them, afflicted as they were with hunger.

5.32.s:
atha tāni samālakṣya gurūṇi munisattamāḥ ..
atrirekaṃ parisphoṭya suvarṇaṃ vīkṣya cābravīt..33.. ..
5.32.d:
अथ तानि समालक्ष्य गुरूणि मुनिसत्तमाः ..
अत्रिरेकं परिस्फोट्य सुवर्णं वीक्ष्य चाब्रवीत्..33.. ..
5.32.m: Then, observing them to be heavy, O best of sages, / Atri split one open, saw the gold, and said:

5.32.s:
.. atriruvāca .. ..
nāsmākaṃ munayo'jñānaṃ nāsmākaṃ gṛhabuddhayaḥ ..
haimānimānvijānaṃto grahīṣyāma udumbarān .. 34 ..
5.32.d:
.. अत्रिरुवाच .. ..
नास्माकं मुनयोऽज्ञानं नास्माकं गृहबुद्धयः ..
हैमानिमान्विजानंतो ग्रहीष्याम उदुम्बरान् .. 34 ..
5.32.m: Atri said: / "O sages, we are not ignorant, nor are our minds fixed on household life. / Knowing these udumbara fruits to be filled with gold, shall we take them?

5.32.s:
tasmādetāni saṃtyajya hemagarbhāṇi dūrataḥ ..
udumbarāṇi yāsyāmaḥ phalāni vigataspṛhāḥ .. 35 ..
5.32.d:
तस्मादेतानि संत्यज्य हेमगर्भाणि दूरतः ..
उदुम्बराणि यास्यामः फलानि विगतस्पृहाः .. 35 ..
5.32.m: Therefore, casting these gold-filled udumbara fruits / far away, free from desire we shall go on.

5.32.s:
sārvabhaumo mahīpāla eko'nyaśca nirīhakaḥ ..
subhagastu tayornityaṃ bhūyādbhūyo nirīhakaḥ .. 36 ..
5.32.d:
सार्वभौमो महीपाल एकोऽन्यश्च निरीहकः ..
सुभगस्तु तयोर्नित्यं भूयाद्भूयो निरीहकः .. 36 ..
5.32.m: One is an emperor over the earth, and the other is a man without desires; / but between the two, the desireless one is always far more fortunate.

5.32.s:
dharmārthamapi viprāṇāṃ saṃcayo'rthasya garhitaḥ ..
prakṣālanāddhi paṃkasya dūrādasparśanaṃ varam .. .. 37 ..
5.32.d:
धर्मार्थमपि विप्राणां संचयोऽर्थस्य गर्हितः ..
प्रक्षालनाद्धि पंकस्य दूरादस्पर्शनं वरम् .. .. 37 ..
5.32.m: Even for the sake of dharma, the accumulation of wealth is despised for brahmins; / for rather than washing off mud, it is better not to touch it from afar.

5.32.s:
tyajataḥ saṃcayānsarvānyāṃti hānimupadravāḥ ..
na hi sarvārthavānkaściddṛśyate nirupadravaḥ .. 38 ..
5.32.d:
त्यजतः संचयान्सर्वान्यांति हानिमुपद्रवाः ..
न हि सर्वार्थवान्कश्चिद्दृश्यते निरुपद्रवः .. 38 ..
5.32.m: For one who renounces all accumulations, afflictions come to an end; / indeed, no one who possesses all kinds of wealth is seen free from affliction.

5.32.s:
nirdhanatvaṃ tathā rājyaṃ tulāyāṃ dhārayedbudhaḥ ..
akiṃcanatvamadhikaṃ jāyate saṃmatirmama .. 39 ..
5.32.d:
निर्धनत्वं तथा राज्यं तुलायां धारयेद्बुधः ..
अकिंचनत्वमधिकं जायते संमतिर्मम .. 39 ..
5.32.m: A wise man should place poverty and kingship on a balance; / possessionlessness outweighs it—this is my conviction."

5.32.s:
.. kaśyapa uvāca .. ..
anartho'yaṃ mune prāpto yadarthasya parigrahaḥ ..
arthaiśvaryavimūḍhātmā śreyasā mucyate hi saḥ .. 6.32.40 ..
5.32.d:
.. कश्यप उवाच .. ..
अनर्थोऽयं मुने प्राप्तो यदर्थस्य परिग्रहः ..
अर्थैश्वर्यविमूढात्मा श्रेयसा मुच्यते हि सः .. 6.32.40 ..
5.32.m: Kaśyapa said: / "A calamity has arrived, O sage, since this acceptance of wealth has occurred! / For he whose mind is deluded by wealth and power is separated from the highest good.

5.32.s:
arthasaṃpadvimohāya vimoho narakāya ca ..
tasmādarthaṃ prayatnena śreyo'rthī dūratastyajet .. ..41 ..
5.32.d:
अर्थसंपद्विमोहाय विमोहो नरकाय च ..
तस्मादर्थं प्रयत्नेन श्रेयोऽर्थी दूरतस्त्यजेत् .. ..41 ..
5.32.m: Abundance of wealth leads to delusion, and delusion leads to hell; / therefore, one seeking the highest good should diligently abandon wealth from afar.

5.32.s:
yorthena sādhyate dharmaḥ kṣayiṣṇuḥ sa prakīrtitaḥ ..
yaḥ punastapasā sādhyaḥ sa mokṣāyeti me matiḥ .. 42 ..
5.32.d:
योर्थेन साध्यते धर्मः क्षयिष्णुः स प्रकीर्तितः ..
यः पुनस्तपसा साध्यः स मोक्षायेति मे मतिः .. 42 ..
5.32.m: Dharma which is accomplished through wealth is proclaimed to be perishable; / that, however, which is accomplished through austerity leads to liberation; this is my view."

5.32.s:
.. bharadvāja uvāca .. ..
jīryaṃti jīryataḥ keśā daṃtā jīryaṃti jīryataḥ ..
cakṣuḥ śrotre tathā puṃsastṛṣṇaikā taruṇāyate .. 43 ..
5.32.d:
.. भरद्वाज उवाच .. ..
जीर्यंति जीर्यतः केशा दंता जीर्यंति जीर्यतः ..
चक्षुः श्रोत्रे तथा पुंसस्तृष्णैका तरुणायते .. 43 ..
5.32.m: Bharadvāja said: / "The hairs of an aging man age, the teeth of an aging man decay; / the eyes and ears of a man decay likewise; craving alone remains youthful.

5.32.s:
sūcyā sūtraṃ yathā vastraṃ saṃcārayati sūcikā ..
tadvatsaṃsārasūtraṃ ca vāṃchayātmā nayatyasau ... 44 ..
5.32.d:
सूच्या सूत्रं यथा वस्त्रं संचारयति सूचिका ..
तद्वत्संसारसूत्रं च वांछयात्मा नयत्यसौ ... 44 ..
5.32.m: Just as a seamstress passes the thread through cloth with a needle, / so this soul leads the thread of saṃsāra through desire.

5.32.s:
yathā śṛṃgaṃ hi kāyena varddhamānena vardhate.
tadvattṛṣṇāpi vittena varddhamānena varddhate..45..
5.32.d:
यथा शृंगं हि कायेन वर्द्धमानेन वर्धते.
तद्वत्तृष्णापि वित्तेन वर्द्धमानेन वर्द्धते..45..
5.32.m: Just as a horn grows as the body grows, / so craving grows as wealth grows.

5.32.s:
anaṃtapārā duṣpūrā tṛṣṇā duḥkhaśatāvahā..
adharmabahulā caiva tasmāttāṃ parivarjayet..46..
5.32.d:
अनंतपारा दुष्पूरा तृष्णा दुःखशतावहा..
अधर्मबहुला चैव तस्मात्तां परिवर्जयेत्..46..
5.32.m: Craving is endless, insatiable, the bringer of hundreds of sorrows, / and full of unrighteousness; therefore one should abandon it."

5.32.s:
gautama uvāca..
saṃtuṣṭaḥ kena cālyo'sti phalairapi vivarjitaḥ..
sarvopīndriyalaulyena saṃkaṭe bhramati dvijāḥ..47..
5.32.d:
गौतम उवाच..
संतुष्टः केन चाल्योऽस्ति फलैरपि विवर्जितः..
सर्वोपीन्द्रियलौल्येन संकटे भ्रमति द्विजाः..47..
5.32.m: Gautama said: / "By what can a contented man be shaken, even when destitute of fruits? / The whole world wanders in distress due to greed of the senses, O brahmins.

5.32.s:
sarvatra saṃpadastasya saṃtuṣṭaṃ yasya mānasam..
upānadgūḍhapādasya nanu carmāstṛteva bhūḥ..48..
5.32.d:
सर्वत्र संपदस्तस्य संतुष्टं यस्य मानसम्..
उपानद्गूढपादस्य ननु चर्मास्तृतेव भूः..48..
5.32.m: Wealth is everywhere for him whose mind is contented; / for one whose foot is covered with a shoe, is not the earth as if spread with leather?

5.32.s:
saṃtoṣāmṛtatṛptānāṃ yatsukhaṃ śāṃtacetasām ..
kutastaddhanalubdhānāmitaścetaśca dhāvatām .. 49 ..
5.32.d:
संतोषामृततृप्तानां यत्सुखं शांतचेतसाम् ..
कुतस्तद्धनलुब्धानामितश्चेतश्च धावताम् .. 49 ..
5.32.m: That happiness belonging to the peaceful-minded who are satiated with the nectar of contentment, / whence could it belong to those greedy for wealth, running this way and that?

5.32.s:
asaṃtoṣaḥ paraṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃtoṣaḥ paramaṃ sukham ..
sukhārthī puruṣastasmātsaṃtuṣṭaḥ satataṃ bhavet .. 6.32.50 ..
5.32.d:
असंतोषः परं दुःखं संतोषः परमं सुखम् ..
सुखार्थी पुरुषस्तस्मात्संतुष्टः सततं भवेत् .. 6.32.50 ..
5.32.m: Discontent is supreme sorrow; contentment is supreme happiness. / Therefore, a person seeking happiness should always remain contented."

5.32.s:
.. viśvāmitra uvāca .. ..
kāmaṃ kāmayamānasya yadi kāmaḥ sa sidhyati ..
tathānyo jāyate puṃsastatkṣaṇādeva kalpitaḥ .. 51 ..
5.32.d:
.. विश्वामित्र उवाच .. ..
कामं कामयमानस्य यदि कामः स सिध्यति ..
तथान्यो जायते पुंसस्तत्क्षणादेव कल्पितः .. 51 ..
5.32.m: Viśvāmitra said: / "If that desire of a desiring man is fulfilled, / then another desire is conceived for that man at that very instant.

5.32.s:
na jātu kāmī kāmānāṃ sahasrairapi tuṣyati ..
haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva vāṃchā tasya vivardhate .. ..52 ..
5.32.d:
न जातु कामी कामानां सहस्रैरपि तुष्यति ..
हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव वांछा तस्य विवर्धते .. ..52 ..
5.32.m: Never is a lustful man satisfied even by thousands of desires; / his craving increases like a fire fed with clarified butter."

5.32.s:
kāmānabhilaṣanmohānna naraḥ sukhamāpnuyāt ..
śyenālayatarucchāyāṃ vrajanniva kapiñjalaḥ .. 53 ..
5.32.d:
कामानभिलषन्मोहान्न नरः सुखमाप्नुयात् ..
श्येनालयतरुच्छायां व्रजन्निव कपिञ्जलः .. 53 ..
5.32.m: Craving desires out of delusion, a man cannot attain happiness, / like a francolin going into the shade of a falcon's roosting-tree. 53

5.32.s:
nityaṃ sāgaraparyantāṃ yo bhuṅkte pṛthivīmimām ..
tulyāśmakāścanaścaiva sa kṛtārtho mahīpateḥ .. 54 ..
5.32.d:
नित्यं सागरपर्यन्तां यो भुङ्क्ते पृथिवीमिमाम् ..
तुल्याश्मकाश्चनश्चैव स कृतार्थो महीपतेः .. 54 ..
5.32.m: He who continually enjoys this earth as far as the ocean, / and regards a clod and gold as equal, is fulfilled [like the greatest] of kings. 54

5.32.s:
.. jamadagniruvāca .. ..
yo'rthaṃ prāpyādhamo vipraḥ śocitavyepi hṛṣyati ..
na ca paśyati mandātmā narakaṃ cā kutobhayaḥ.. 55 ..
5.32.d:
.. जमदग्निरुवाच .. ..
योऽर्थं प्राप्याधमो विप्रः शोचितव्येपि हृष्यति ..
न च पश्यति मन्दात्मा नरकं चा कुतोभयः.. 55 ..
5.32.m: Jamadagni said: / A base brahmin who, having obtained wealth, rejoices when he ought to grieve, / and, dull-minded, does not see hell—from what does he fear nothing? 55

5.32.s:
pratigrahasamarthānāṃ nivṛttānāṃ pratigrahāt ..
ya eva dadatāṃ lokāsta evāpratigṛhṇatām..56..
5.32.d:
प्रतिग्रहसमर्थानां निवृत्तानां प्रतिग्रहात् ..
य एव ददतां लोकास्त एवाप्रतिगृह्णताम्..56..
5.32.m: For those who are capable of accepting gifts, but refrain from accepting them, / the same worlds that belong to the givers belong to those who do not accept. 56

5.32.s:
arundhatyuvāca..
bisataṃturyathā'nanto nālamāsādya saṃsthitaḥ..
tṛṣṇā caivamanādyantā sthitā dehe śarīriṇām..57..
5.32.d:
अरुन्धत्युवाच..
बिसतंतुर्यथाऽनन्तो नालमासाद्य संस्थितः..
तृष्णा चैवमनाद्यन्ता स्थिता देहे शरीरिणाम्..57..
5.32.m: Arundhatī said: / Just as the lotus fiber, endless, remains having reached into the stalk, / even so desire, without beginning or end, remains in the body of embodied beings. 57

5.32.s:
yā dustyajā durmatibhiryā na jīryati jīryataḥ..
yā'sau prāṇāntiko rogastāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham..58..
caṇḍovāca..
sarpādivaddhanādyasmādbibhyatīme mameśvarāḥ ..
yatastato viśeṣeṇa kasmāttasmādbhayaṃ mama ..56.. ..
5.32.d:
या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः..
याऽसौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम्..58..
चण्डोवाच..
सर्पादिवद्धनाद्यस्माद्बिभ्यतीमे ममेश्वराः ..
यतस्ततो विशेषेण कस्मात्तस्माद्भयं मम ..56.. ..
5.32.m:
That which is hard to abandon by the wicked-minded, which does not age as one ages, / which is a fatal disease—giving up that desire brings happiness. 58
Caṇḍā said: / Since these masters of mine fear wealth as they would a serpent, / for what reason should I not fear it even more? 59

5.32.s:
paśumukha uvāca..
yadācaranti vidvāṃsaḥ sadā dharmaparāyaṇāḥ..
tadeva viduṣā kāryamātmano hitamicchatā..6.32.60..
sūta uvāca..
ityuktvā hemagarbhāṇi tyaktvā tāni phalāni ca..
ṛṣayo jagmuranyatra sarva eva dṛḍhavratāḥ ..6...
5.32.d:
पशुमुख उवाच..
यदाचरन्ति विद्वांसः सदा धर्मपरायणाः..
तदेव विदुषा कार्यमात्मनो हितमिच्छता..6.32.60..
सूत उवाच..
इत्युक्त्वा हेमगर्भाणि त्यक्त्वा तानि फलानि च..
ऋषयो जग्मुरन्यत्र सर्व एव दृढव्रताः ..6...
5.32.m:
Paśumukha said: / Whatever the wise, ever devoted to dharma, practice, / that alone should be done by an intelligent person who desires his own welfare. 60
Sūta said: / Having spoken thus and abandoned those gold-bearing fruits, / all the seers of firm vows went elsewhere. 61

5.32.s:
camatkārapurekṣetre viviśuste tataḥ param ..
dadṛśuḥ sahasā prāptaṃ parivrājaṃ śunomukham .. 62 ..
5.32.d:
चमत्कारपुरेक्षेत्रे विविशुस्ते ततः परम् ..
ददृशुः सहसा प्राप्तं परिव्राजं शुनोमुखम् .. 62 ..
5.32.m: Then they entered the sacred field of Camatkārapura; / suddenly they saw a mendicant with the face of a dog who had arrived there. 62

5.32.s:
tenaiva sahitāstatra gatvā kiñcidvanāntaram..
dṛṣṭavantastato hṛdyaṃ saraḥ paṃkajaśobhitam .. 63 ..
5.32.d:
तेनैव सहितास्तत्र गत्वा किञ्चिद्वनान्तरम्..
दृष्टवन्तस्ततो हृद्यं सरः पंकजशोभितम् .. 63 ..
5.32.m: Having gone with him to another forest there, / they then saw a lovely lake adorned with lotuses. 63

5.32.s:
tato bubhukṣayāviṣṭā bisānyādāya bhūriśaḥ ..
tīre nikṣipya sarasaścakruḥ puṇyāṃ jala kriyām .. 64 ..
5.32.d:
ततो बुभुक्षयाविष्टा बिसान्यादाय भूरिशः ..
तीरे निक्षिप्य सरसश्चक्रुः पुण्यां जल क्रियाम् .. 64 ..
5.32.m: Then, seized by hunger, they gathered abundant lotus roots, / laid them on the shore of the lake, and performed their sacred water rite. 64

5.32.s:
athottīryajalātsarve te sametya parasparam ..
bisāni tānyapaśyanta idaṃ vacanamabruvan .. 65 ..
5.32.d:
अथोत्तीर्यजलात्सर्वे ते समेत्य परस्परम् ..
बिसानि तान्यपश्यन्त इदं वचनमब्रुवन् .. 65 ..
5.32.m: Then, having emerged from the water, they all assembled together, / and, not seeing those lotus roots, spoke these words: 65

5.32.s:
..ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kena kṣudhābhitaptānāmasmākaṃ nirdayātmanā ..
mṛṇālāni samastāni sthānādasmāddhṛtāni ca .. 66 ..
5.32.d:
..ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
केन क्षुधाभितप्तानामस्माकं निर्दयात्मना ..
मृणालानि समस्तानि स्थानादस्माद्धृतानि च .. 66 ..
5.32.m: The seers said: / By what pitiless person have all the lotus roots / been taken from this spot while we were tormented by hunger? 66

5.32.s:
te śaṃkamānā anyonyamṛṣayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ ..
pracakruḥ śapathānraudrānātmanaḥ praviśuddhaye .. 67 ..
5.32.d:
ते शंकमाना अन्योन्यमृषयः शंसितव्रताः ..
प्रचक्रुः शपथान्रौद्रानात्मनः प्रविशुद्धये .. 67 ..
5.32.m: Suspecting one another, the seers of celebrated vows / uttered fierce oaths for the sake of their own purification: 67

5.32.s:
.. kaśyapa uvāca .. ..
sarvabhakṣaḥ sadā so'stu nyāsalobhaṃ karotu vā ..
kūṭasākṣitvamabhye tu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 68 ..
5.32.d:
.. कश्यप उवाच .. ..
सर्वभक्षः सदा सोऽस्तु न्यासलोभं करोतु वा ..
कूटसाक्षित्वमभ्ये तु बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 68 ..
5.32.m: Kaśyapa said: / May he who steals the lotus roots always eat anything, / or let him crave a trust deposit, or incur the state of a false witness! 68

5.32.s:
dharmaṃ karotu daṃbhena rājānaṃ copasevatām ..
madhumāṃsaṃ sadāśnātu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 69 . ..
.. vasiṣṭha uvāca .. ..
anṛtau maithunaṃ yātu divā vāpyatha parvaṇi ..
atithiḥ syāttato'nyonyaṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 6.32.70 .. ..
5.32.d:
धर्मं करोतु दंभेन राजानं चोपसेवताम् ..
मधुमांसं सदाश्नातु बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 69 . ..
.. वसिष्ठ उवाच .. ..
अनृतौ मैथुनं यातु दिवा वाप्यथ पर्वणि ..
अतिथिः स्यात्ततोऽन्योन्यं बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 6.32.70 .. ..
5.32.m: May he perform dharma out of deceit, and let him attend upon a king; / may he always eat honey and meat—he who steals the lotus roots! 69 / Vasiṣṭha said: / May he have sexual intercourse out of season, by day, or on a forbidden day; / and may he then be an unwelcome guest to another—he who steals the lotus roots! 70

5.32.s:
.. bharadvāja uvāca .. ..
yodhigamya guroḥ śāstraṃ niṣkrayaṃ na prayacchati ..
tasyainasā sa yuktostu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 71 ..
5.32.d:
.. भरद्वाज उवाच .. ..
योधिगम्य गुरोः शास्त्रं निष्क्रयं न प्रयच्छति ..
तस्यैनसा स युक्तोस्तु बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 71 ..
5.32.m: Bharadvāja said: / May he who steals the lotus roots be burdened with the sin / of one who, having received teaching from a guru, does not give the fee! 71

5.32.s:
nṛśaṃso'stu sa sarvatra samṛddhyā cāpyahaṃkṛtaḥ ..
matsarī piśunaścaiva bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 72 ..
5.32.d:
नृशंसोऽस्तु स सर्वत्र समृद्ध्या चाप्यहंकृतः ..
मत्सरी पिशुनश्चैव बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 72 ..
5.32.m: May he be cruel in all matters, conceited on account of wealth, / envious, and a slanderer—he who steals the lotus roots! 72

5.32.s:
.. viśvāmitra uvāca .. ..
ekākī mṛṣṭama śnātu praśaṃsyādatha cātmanaḥ ..
vedavikrayakartāstu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 73 ..
5.32.d:
.. विश्वामित्र उवाच .. ..
एकाकी मृष्टम श्नातु प्रशंस्यादथ चात्मनः ..
वेदविक्रयकर्तास्तु बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 73 ..
5.32.m: Viśvāmitra said: / May he eat sweet delicacies alone, praise himself, / and be a seller of the Veda—he who steals the lotus roots! 73

5.32.s:
.. jamadagniruvāca .. ..
kanyāṃ yacchatu vṛddhāya sa bhūyādvṛṣalī patiḥ ..
astu vārdhuṣiko nityaṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 74
5.32.d:
.. जमदग्निरुवाच .. ..
कन्यां यच्छतु वृद्धाय स भूयाद्वृषली पतिः ..
अस्तु वार्धुषिको नित्यं बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 74
5.32.m: Jamadagni said: / Let him give his daughter to an old man, may he become the husband of a Śūdra woman, / or may he always be a usurer—he who steals the lotus roots! 74

5.32.s:
.. gautama uvāca .. ..
sa gṛhṇātvavikādānaṃ karotu hayavikrayam..
prakaro tu gurorniṃdāṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ ..75 ..
5.32.d:
.. गौतम उवाच .. ..
स गृह्णात्वविकादानं करोतु हयविक्रयम्..
प्रकरो तु गुरोर्निंदां बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः ..75 ..
5.32.m: Gautama said: / May he accept gifts of sheep, engage in selling horses, / and utter revilement of his guru—he who steals the lotus roots! 75

5.32.s:
.. atriruvāca .. ..
mātaraṃ pitaraṃ nityaṃ durmatiḥ so'vamanyatām ..
śūdraṃ pṛcchatu dharmārthaṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 76 ..
5.32.d:
.. अत्रिरुवाच .. ..
मातरं पितरं नित्यं दुर्मतिः सोऽवमन्यताम् ..
शूद्रं पृच्छतु धर्मार्थं बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 76 ..
5.32.m: Atri said: / Wicked-minded, may he continually despise his mother and father; / let him ask a Śūdra for instruction in dharma—he who steals the lotus roots! 76

5.32.s:
pratiśrutya na yo dadyādbrāhmaṇāya gavādikam ..
tasyainasā sa yujyeta bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ ..-77 ..
.. aruṃdhatyuvāca .. ..
karotu patyuḥ pūrvaṃ sā bhojanaṃ śayanaṃ tathā ..
nārī duṣṭasamācārā bisastainyaṃ karoti yā .. 78 ..
5.32.d:
प्रतिश्रुत्य न यो दद्याद्ब्राह्मणाय गवादिकम् ..
तस्यैनसा स युज्येत बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः ..-77 ..
.. अरुंधत्युवाच .. ..
करोतु पत्युः पूर्वं सा भोजनं शयनं तथा ..
नारी दुष्टसमाचारा बिसस्तैन्यं करोति या .. 78 ..
5.32.m: May he who steals the lotus roots be burdened with the sin / of one who, having promised cattle and the like to a brahmin, does not give them! 77 / Arundhatī said: / May she eat before her husband, and likewise sleep before him, / a woman of wicked conduct—she who steals the lotus roots! 78

5.32.s:
.. caṇḍovāca .. ..
svāminaḥ pratikūlāstu dharmadveṣaṃ karotu ca..
sādhudveṣaparā caiva bisastainyaṃ karoti yā .. 79 ..
5.32.d:
.. चण्डोवाच .. ..
स्वामिनः प्रतिकूलास्तु धर्मद्वेषं करोतु च..
साधुद्वेषपरा चैव बिसस्तैन्यं करोति या .. 79 ..
5.32.m: Caṇḍā said: / May she be contrary to her master, bear hatred toward dharma, / and be intent on hating the virtuous—she who steals the lotus roots! 79

5.32.s:
paśumukha uvāca .. ..
svāmidroharato nityaṃ sa bhūyātpāpakṛnnaraḥ ..
sādhu dveṣaparaścaiva bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 6.32.80 ..
5.32.d:
पशुमुख उवाच .. ..
स्वामिद्रोहरतो नित्यं स भूयात्पापकृन्नरः ..
साधु द्वेषपरश्चैव बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 6.32.80 ..
5.32.m: Paśumukha said: / May that sinful man always be devoted to betraying his master, / and intent on hating the virtuous—he who steals the lotus roots! 80

5.32.s:
.. śunomukha uvāca .. ..
vedānsa paṭhatu nyāyādgṛhasthaḥ syātpriyātithiḥ ..
satyaṃ vadatu cājasraṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 81 ..
5.32.d:
.. शुनोमुख उवाच .. ..
वेदान्स पठतु न्यायाद्गृहस्थः स्यात्प्रियातिथिः ..
सत्यं वदतु चाजस्रं बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 81 ..
5.32.m: Śunomukha said: / May he study the Vedas properly, be a householder fond of guests, / and constantly speak the truth—he who steals the lotus roots! 81

5.32.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
iṣṭa eva dvijātīnāṃ yastvayā śapathaḥ kṛtaḥ ..
bisastainyaṃ hi cāsmākaṃ tannūnaṃ bhavatā kṛtam .. 82 ..
5.32.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
इष्ट एव द्विजातीनां यस्त्वया शपथः कृतः ..
बिसस्तैन्यं हि चास्माकं तन्नूनं भवता कृतम् .. 82 ..
5.32.m: The seers said: / The oath sworn by you is entirely desirable for the twice-born; / surely, then, the theft of our lotus roots was done by you! 82

5.32.s:
.. śunomukha uvāca .. ..
mayā hṛtāni sarveṣāṃ bisānīmāni vo dvijāḥ ..
dharmānvai śrotukāmena māṃ jānīta puraṃdaram .. 83 ..
5.32.d:
.. शुनोमुख उवाच .. ..
मया हृतानि सर्वेषां बिसानीमानि वो द्विजाः ..
धर्मान्वै श्रोतुकामेन मां जानीत पुरंदरम् .. 83 ..
5.32.m: Śunomukha said: / These lotus roots of yours were taken by me, O twice-born, / out of a desire to hear righteous duties; know me to be Purandara. 83

5.32.s:
yuṣmākaṃ parituṣṭo'smi lobhābhāvāddvijottamāḥ ..
tasmātsvargaṃ mayā sārddhaṃ śīghramāgamyatāmiti .ā 84 ..
5.32.d:
युष्माकं परितुष्टोऽस्मि लोभाभावाद्द्विजोत्तमाः ..
तस्मात्स्वर्गं मया सार्द्धं शीघ्रमागम्यतामिति .आ 84 ..
5.32.m: I am well-pleased with you, O best of the twice-born, because of your absence of greed; / therefore, come quickly with me to heaven! 84

5.32.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
mokṣamārgaṃ samāsaktā na vayaṃ svargalipsavaḥ ..
tasmāttapaścariṣyāmaḥ sarasīha vimuktaye .. 85 ..
5.32.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
मोक्षमार्गं समासक्ता न वयं स्वर्गलिप्सवः ..
तस्मात्तपश्चरिष्यामः सरसीह विमुक्तये .. 85 ..
5.32.m: The seers said: / Dedicated to the path of liberation, we do not desire heaven; / therefore, we shall perform austerity here at the lake for final liberation. 85

5.32.s:
pūrṇā sāgaraparyaṃtāṃ caritvā pṛthivī mimām ..
prāṇayātrāṃ prakurvāṇā mṛṇālairmunisattamāḥ ..
tasmādgaccha tava śreyo bhūyādasmātsamāgamāt .. 86 ..
5.32.d:
पूर्णा सागरपर्यंतां चरित्वा पृथिवी मिमाम् ..
प्राणयात्रां प्रकुर्वाणा मृणालैर्मुनिसत्तमाः ..
तस्माद्गच्छ तव श्रेयो भूयादस्मात्समागमात् .. 86 ..
5.32.m: We have wandered all over this earth up to the ocean, / sustaining our lives on lotus roots, O best of sages; / therefore depart; may good fortune come to you from this meeting with us. 86

5.32.s:
.. śakra uvāca .. ..
na vṛthā darśanaṃ me syātkadācidapi suvratāḥ ..
tasmādgṛhṇīta yaccitte sadābhīṣṭaṃ vyavasthitam .. 87 ..
5.32.d:
.. शक्र उवाच .. ..
न वृथा दर्शनं मे स्यात्कदाचिदपि सुव्रताः ..
तस्माद्गृह्णीत यच्चित्ते सदाभीष्टं व्यवस्थितम् .. 87 ..
5.32.m: Śakra said: / My sight can never be in vain, O men of noble vows; / therefore, choose whatever is constantly desired in your hearts. 87

5.32.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. .. ,
āśramo'yaṃ suvikhyāto bhūyācchakra mahītale ..
nāmnāsmākaṃ tathā nṛṇāṃ sarvapātakanāśanaḥ .. 88 ..
5.32.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. .. ,
आश्रमोऽयं सुविख्यातो भूयाच्छक्र महीतले ..
नाम्नास्माकं तथा नृणां सर्वपातकनाशनः .. 88 ..
5.32.m: The seers said: / O Śakra, may this hermitage become very famous on earth / by our name, destroying all sins for mankind. 88

5.32.s:
vayaṃ sthāsyāmahe nityamatraiva surasattama ..
tapo'rthaṃ bhāvitātmāno yāvanmokṣagatirdhruvā .. 89 ..
5.32.d:
वयं स्थास्यामहे नित्यमत्रैव सुरसत्तम ..
तपोऽर्थं भावितात्मानो यावन्मोक्षगतिर्ध्रुवा .. 89 ..
5.32.m: We shall remain forever right here, O best of gods, / with purified minds for the sake of austerity, until our attainment of liberation is secure. 89

5.32.s:
.. indra uvāca .. ..
trailokye'pi suvikhyāta āśramo vo bhaviṣyati ..
tathā kāmapradaścaiva lokānāṃ saṃbhaviṣyati .. 6.32.90 ..
5.32.d:
.. इन्द्र उवाच .. ..
त्रैलोक्येऽपि सुविख्यात आश्रमो वो भविष्यति ..
तथा कामप्रदश्चैव लोकानां संभविष्यति .. 6.32.90 ..
5.32.m: Indra said: / Your hermitage will be well-renowned even in the three worlds, / and it shall likewise grant the desires of people. 90

5.32.s:
yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya śrāddhamatra kariṣyati ..
śrāvaṇe paurṇamāsyāṃ ca sa taṃ sarvamavā psyati .. 91 ..
5.32.d:
यो यं काममभिध्याय श्राद्धमत्र करिष्यति ..
श्रावणे पौर्णमास्यां च स तं सर्वमवा प्स्यति .. 91 ..
5.32.m: Whoever performs an ancestral rite here on the full-moon day in the month of Śrāvaṇa, / intending any desire, shall obtain all of it. 91

5.32.s:
niṣkāmo vā naro yastu śrāddhaṃ dānamathāpi vā ..
prakariṣyati mokṣaṃ sa samavāpsyatyasaṃśayam .. 92 ..
5.32.d:
निष्कामो वा नरो यस्तु श्राद्धं दानमथापि वा ..
प्रकरिष्यति मोक्षं स समवाप्स्यत्यसंशयम् .. 92 ..
5.32.m:
Or whatever desireless person performs a śrāddha or gives gifts,
he shall attain liberation, without a doubt.

5.32.s:
ye cātra dehaṃ tyakṣyaṃti yuṣmākaṃ cāśrame śubhe ..
api pāpasamāyuktāste yāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim .. 93 ..
5.32.d:
ये चात्र देहं त्यक्ष्यंति युष्माकं चाश्रमे शुभे ..
अपि पापसमायुक्तास्ते यास्यंति परां गतिम् .. 93 ..
5.32.m:
And those who cast off their bodies here in your auspicious hermitage,
even though joined with sins, shall attain the highest state.

5.32.s:
iṃgudairbadarairvāpi bilvairbhallātakairapi ..
pitṝnuddiśya yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kariṣyati samāhitaḥ .. 94 ..
5.32.d:
इंगुदैर्बदरैर्वापि बिल्वैर्भल्लातकैरपि ..
पितॄनुद्दिश्य यः श्राद्धं करिष्यति समाहितः .. 94 ..
5.32.m:
With inguda, jujube, bilva, or bhallātaka fruits,
whoever, being concentrated, performs a śrāddha dedicated to the ancestors

5.32.s:
sa yāsyati parāṃ siddhiṃ durlabhāṃ tridaśairapi ..
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ stūyamānaśca kiṃnaraiḥ .. 95 .. ..
5.32.d:
स यास्यति परां सिद्धिं दुर्लभां त्रिदशैरपि ..
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः स्तूयमानश्च किंनरैः .. 95 .. ..
5.32.m:
shall attain the highest perfection, difficult to obtain even by the gods,
freed from all sins and praised by kimnaras.”

5.32.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamuktvā sahasrākṣastaiḥ sarvairabhinaṃditaḥ 0.
jagāmādarśanaṃ te'pi sthitāstatra dvijottamāḥ .. 96 ..
5.32.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा सहस्राक्षस्तैः सर्वैरभिनंदितः 0.
जगामादर्शनं तेऽपि स्थितास्तत्र द्विजोत्तमाः .. 96 ..
5.32.m:
Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the thousand-eyed [Indra], congratulated by them all,
vanished from sight; and those best of twice-born remained there.

5.32.s:
tataḥ kāle gate te'pi kṛtvā tīvraṃ mahattapaḥ ..
saṃprāptāḥ paramaṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam .. 97 ..
5.32.d:
ततः काले गते तेऽपि कृत्वा तीव्रं महत्तपः ..
संप्राप्ताः परमं स्थानं जरामरणवर्जितम् .. 97 ..
5.32.m:
Then, as time passed, having performed severe and great austerity,
they reached the supreme realm, devoid of old age and death.

5.32.s:
taistatra sthāpitaṃ liṅgaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ ..
tasya saṃdarśanādeva naraḥ pāpādvimucyate .. 98 ..
5.32.d:
तैस्तत्र स्थापितं लिङ्गं देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ..
तस्य संदर्शनादेव नरः पापाद्विमुच्यते .. 98 ..
5.32.m:
A liṅga of the god of gods, the trident-bearer, was established there by them;
merely by the sight of it, a man is freed from sin.

5.32.s:
yastalliṃgaṃ punarbhaktyā puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ ..
arcayetsa dhruvaṃ muktiṃ prāpnoti dvijasattamāḥ .. 99 ..
5.32.d:
यस्तल्लिंगं पुनर्भक्त्या पुष्पधूपानुलेपनैः ..
अर्चयेत्स ध्रुवं मुक्तिं प्राप्नोति द्विजसत्तमाः .. 99 ..
5.32.m:
Moreover, whoever worships that liṅga with devotion, through flowers, incense, and unguents,
surely attains liberation, O best of twice-born.

5.32.s:
etatpavitra māyuṣyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam..
saptarṣoṇāṃ samākhyātamāśramasyānukīrtanam .. 6.32.100 ..
iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye saptarṣyāśramamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma dvātriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 32 .. .. cha ..
5.32.d:
एतत्पवित्र मायुष्यं सर्वपातकनाशनम्..
सप्तर्षोणां समाख्यातमाश्रमस्यानुकीर्तनम् .. 6.32.100 ..
इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये सप्तर्ष्याश्रममाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम द्वात्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 32 .. .. छ ..
5.32.m:
This holy, life-promoting, all-sin-destroying
recitation of the hermitage of the Seven Seers has been proclaimed.
Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, named "Description of the Greatness of the Hermitage of the Seven Seers," in the Greatness of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skanda Purāṇa.

5.33.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
agastyasyāśramo'nyosti tathā tatra dvijottamāḥ ..
yatra tiṣṭhati viśvātmā svayaṃ devo maheśvaraḥ .. 1 ..
5.33.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अगस्त्यस्याश्रमोऽन्योस्ति तथा तत्र द्विजोत्तमाः ..
यत्र तिष्ठति विश्वात्मा स्वयं देवो महेश्वरः .. 1 ..
5.33.m:
Sūta said: / There is another hermitage of Agastya there, O best of twice-born,
where the Self of all, God Maheśvara himself, resides.

5.33.s:
śuklapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ caitramāse divākaraḥ ..
svayamabhyetya deveśaṃ pūjayatyeva śaṃkaram .. 2 ..
5.33.d:
शुक्लपक्षे चतुर्दश्यां चैत्रमासे दिवाकरः ..
स्वयमभ्येत्य देवेशं पूजयत्येव शंकरम् .. 2 ..
5.33.m:
On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Caitra, the sun,
coming in person, worships Śaṃkara, the lord of gods.

5.33.s:
tasmādanyo'pi yastasyāṃ bhaktyā cāgatya śaṃkaram ..
tameva pūjayedbhaktyā sa yāti devamandiram .. .. 3 ..
5.33.d:
तस्मादन्योऽपि यस्तस्यां भक्त्या चागत्य शंकरम् ..
तमेव पूजयेद्भक्त्या स याति देवमन्दिरम् .. .. 3 ..
5.33.m:
Therefore, whatever other person also goes there on that day and worships Śaṃkara
with devotion, he goes to the abode of the gods.

5.33.s:
yastatra kurute śrāddhaṃ samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ ..
pitarastasya tṛpyaṃte pitṛmedhe kṛte yathā .. 4 ..
5.33.d:
यस्तत्र कुरुते श्राद्धं सम्यक्छ्रद्धासमन्वितः ..
पितरस्तस्य तृप्यंते पितृमेधे कृते यथा .. 4 ..
5.33.m:
Whoever performs a śrāddha there, endowed with complete faith,
his ancestors are satisfied, just as when a pitṛmedha sacrifice is performed.

5.33.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
agastyasyāśramaṃ prāpya kasmāddevo divākaraḥ ..
pradakṣiṇāṃ prakurute vadaitanme suvistaram .. 5 ..
5.33.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
अगस्त्यस्याश्रमं प्राप्य कस्माद्देवो दिवाकरः ..
प्रदक्षिणां प्रकुरुते वदैतन्मे सुविस्तरम् .. 5 ..
5.33.m:
The seers said: / Having arrived at the hermitage of Agastya, why does the divine sun
circumambulate it? Tell me this in full detail.

5.33.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
kathayāmi kathāmetāṃ śṛṇuta dvija sattamāḥ ..
asti viṃdhya iti khyātaḥ parvataḥ pṛthivītale .. 6 ..
5.33.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
कथयामि कथामेतां शृणुत द्विज सत्तमाः ..
अस्ति विंध्य इति ख्यातः पर्वतः पृथिवीतले .. 6 ..
5.33.m:
Sūta said: / I shall relate this narrative; listen, O best of twice-born:
There is a mountain renowned as Vindhya on the surface of the earth.

5.33.s:
yasya vṛkṣāgraśākhāyāṃ saṃlagnāstaraṇeḥ karāḥ ..
puṣpapūgā ivādhaḥsthairlakṣyaṃte mugdhasi ddhakaiḥ .. 7 ..
5.33.d:
यस्य वृक्षाग्रशाखायां संलग्नास्तरणेः कराः ..
पुष्पपूगा इवाधःस्थैर्लक्ष्यंते मुग्धसि द्धकैः .. 7 ..
5.33.m:
On whose treetop branches the clinging rays of the sun
are perceived by innocent young siddhas below as clusters of flowers.

5.33.s:
anabhijñāstamisrasya yasya sānunivāsinaḥ ..
ratnaprabhāpraṇunnasya kṛṣṇapakṣaniśāsvapi .. 8 ..
5.33.d:
अनभिज्ञास्तमिस्रस्य यस्य सानुनिवासिनः ..
रत्नप्रभाप्रणुन्नस्य कृष्णपक्षनिशास्वपि .. 8 ..
5.33.m:
The dwellers on its slopes are unaware of darkness
dispelled by the radiance of jewels, even on the nights of the dark fortnight.

5.33.s:
yasya sānuṣu muṃcaṃto bhāṃti puṣpāṇi pādapāḥ ..
vāyuvegavaśānnūnaṃ nīraugha nīradā iva .. 9 ..
5.33.d:
यस्य सानुषु मुंचंतो भांति पुष्पाणि पादपाः ..
वायुवेगवशान्नूनं नीरौघ नीरदा इव .. 9 ..
5.33.m:
On whose slopes the trees shedding flowers appear splendid,
verily like clouds shedding torrents of water under the force of the wind.

5.33.s:
yasminnānāmṛgā bhāṃti dhāvamānā itastataḥ ..
kalatraputrapuṣṭyarthaṃ lobhārthaṃ mānavā iva .. .. 6.33.10 ..
5.33.d:
यस्मिन्नानामृगा भांति धावमाना इतस्ततः ..
कलत्रपुत्रपुष्ट्यर्थं लोभार्थं मानवा इव .. .. 6.33.10 ..
5.33.m:
Upon which various animals are seen running to and fro,
like humans driven by greed for the nourishment of wives and sons.

5.33.s:
niryāsacchadmanā bāṣpaṃ vāsitāśeṣadiṅmukham ..
muñcaṃti taravo yatra dantidantakṣatatvacaḥ.. 11 ..
5.33.d:
निर्यासच्छद्मना बाष्पं वासिताशेषदिङ्मुखम् ..
मुञ्चंति तरवो यत्र दन्तिदन्तक्षतत्वचः.. 11 ..
5.33.m:
Where trees whose bark has been wounded by elephants’ tusks shed tears
under the guise of resin, perfuming all the quarters of the sky.

5.33.s:
cīrikāvirutairdīrghai rudaṃta iva cāpare ..
hastihastahatā vṛkṣā manyante yasya sānuṣu .. 12 ..
5.33.d:
चीरिकाविरुतैर्दीर्घै रुदंत इव चापरे ..
हस्तिहस्तहता वृक्षा मन्यन्ते यस्य सानुषु .. 12 ..
5.33.m:
And other trees on its ridges, struck by elephants' trunks,
are thought to be weeping through the prolonged chirping of crickets.

5.33.s:
itaścetaśca gacchadbhirnirjharāṃbhobhirāvṛtaḥ ..
śuśubhe sitavastrāḍhyaiḥ pumāniva vibhūṣitaḥ .. .. 13 ..
5.33.d:
इतश्चेतश्च गच्छद्भिर्निर्झरांभोभिरावृतः ..
शुशुभे सितवस्त्राढ्यैः पुमानिव विभूषितः .. .. 13 ..
5.33.m:
Surrounded by cascade waters flowing here and there,
it shone like a man adorned with opulent white garments.

5.33.s:
yasya sparddhā samutpannā pūrvaṃ saha sumeruṇā ..
tataḥ prāha sahasrāṃśuṃ gatvā sa krodhamūrcchitaḥ .. 14 ..
5.33.d:
यस्य स्पर्द्धा समुत्पन्ना पूर्वं सह सुमेरुणा ..
ततः प्राह सहस्रांशुं गत्वा स क्रोधमूर्च्छितः .. 14 ..
5.33.m:
Formerly, a rivalry arose between it and Sumeru;
then, swooning with rage, it approached the thousand-rayed [sun] and spoke:

5.33.s:
kasmādbhāskara merostvaṃ prakaroṣi pradakṣiṇām ..
kulaparvatasaṃjñe'pi na karoṣi kathaṃ mayi .. 15 ..
5.33.d:
कस्माद्भास्कर मेरोस्त्वं प्रकरोषि प्रदक्षिणाम् ..
कुलपर्वतसंज्ञेऽपि न करोषि कथं मयि .. 15 ..
5.33.m:
“Why, O Bhāskara, do you circumambulate Meru?
Why do you not circumambulate me, though I am also designated a clan mountain?”

5.33.s:
.. bhāskara uvāca .. ..
na vayaṃ śraddhayā tasya gireḥ kurmaḥ pradakṣiṇām ..
eṣa me vihitaḥ panthā yenedaṃ vihitaṃ jagat .. 16 ..
5.33.d:
.. भास्कर उवाच .. ..
न वयं श्रद्धया तस्य गिरेः कुर्मः प्रदक्षिणाम् ..
एष मे विहितः पन्था येनेदं विहितं जगत् .. 16 ..
5.33.m:
Bhāskara said: / “We do not circumambulate that mountain out of devotion;
this is my path ordained by the One by whom this world was ordained.

5.33.s:
tasya tuṃgāni śṛṃgāṇi vyāpya khaṃ saṃśritāni ca ..
tena saṃjāyate tasya balādeva prada kṣiṇā .. 17 ..
5.33.d:
तस्य तुंगानि शृंगाणि व्याप्य खं संश्रितानि च ..
तेन संजायते तस्य बलादेव प्रद क्षिणा .. 17 ..
5.33.m:
Its towering peaks pervade and reach into the sky;
therefore, circumambulating it happens by necessity alone.”

5.33.s:
etacchrutvā viśeṣeṇa saṃkruddho viṃdhyaparvataḥ ..
provāca paśya bhāno tvaṃ tarhi tuṃgatvamadya me ..
rurodhātha nabhomārgaṃ yena gacchati bhāskaraḥ .. 18 ..
5.33.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा विशेषेण संक्रुद्धो विंध्यपर्वतः ..
प्रोवाच पश्य भानो त्वं तर्हि तुंगत्वमद्य मे ..
रुरोधाथ नभोमार्गं येन गच्छति भास्करः .. 18 ..
5.33.m: Hearing this, the Vindhya mountain became especially enraged / and said: “See then my height today, O Sun!” / And forthwith it blocked the pathway of the sky by which the sun travels.

5.33.s:
atha ruddhaṃ samālokya mārgaṃ vāsaranāyakaḥ ..
cintayāmāsa citte sve sāṃprataṃ kiṃ karomyaham .. 19 ..
5.33.d:
अथ रुद्धं समालोक्य मार्गं वासरनायकः ..
चिन्तयामास चित्ते स्वे सांप्रतं किं करोम्यहम् .. 19 ..
5.33.m:
Then, seeing the path blocked, the lord of day
thought in his heart: “What shall I do now?

5.33.s:
karomi yadyahaṃ cāsya parvatasya pradakṣiṇām ..
tadbhaviṣyati kālasya calanaṃ bhuvanatraye .. 6.33.20 ..
5.33.d:
करोमि यद्यहं चास्य पर्वतस्य प्रदक्षिणाम् ..
तद्भविष्यति कालस्य चलनं भुवनत्रये .. 6.33.20 ..
5.33.m:
If I perform a circumambulation of this mountain,
there will be a disruption of time in the three worlds.

5.33.s:
māsartubhuvanānāṃ ca tathā bhāvī viparyayaḥ ..
agniṣṭomādikāḥ sarvāḥ kriyā yāsyaṃti saṃkṣayam ..
naṣṭayajñotsave loke devānāṃ syānmahāvyathā .. 21 ..
5.33.d:
मासर्तुभुवनानां च तथा भावी विपर्ययः ..
अग्निष्टोमादिकाः सर्वाः क्रिया यास्यंति संक्षयम् ..
नष्टयज्ञोत्सवे लोके देवानां स्यान्महाव्यथा .. 21 ..
5.33.m:
And likewise a confusion of months, seasons, and realms will occur;
all rites such as the agniṣṭoma will meet with destruction; / when the festivals of sacrifice are destroyed in the world, great distress will befall the gods.”

5.33.s:
evaṃ saṃcintya cittena bahudhā tīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ ..
jagāma manasā bhītaḥ so'gastyaṃ munipuṃgavam .. 22 ..
5.33.d:
एवं संचिन्त्य चित्तेन बहुधा तीक्ष्णदीधितिः ..
जगाम मनसा भीतः सोऽगस्त्यं मुनिपुंगवम् .. 22 ..
5.33.m:
Having reflected thus in many ways within his mind, the hot-rayed [sun],
afraid, went in thought to Agastya, the bull among sages.

5.33.s:
nānyosti vāraṇe śakto viṃdhasyāsya hi taṃ vinā ..
agastyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhaṃ mitrāvaruṇasaṃbhavam .. 23 ..
5.33.d:
नान्योस्ति वारणे शक्तो विंधस्यास्य हि तं विना ..
अगस्त्यं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठं मित्रावरुणसंभवम् .. 23 ..
5.33.m:
“Indeed, there is no other capable of stopping this Vindhya except him,
Agastya, the best of brahmins, born from Mitra and Varuṇa.”

5.33.s:
tato dvijamayaṃ rūpaṃ sa kṛtvā tīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ ..
camatkārapurakṣetre tasyāśramapadaṃ yayau .. 24 ..
5.33.d:
ततो द्विजमयं रूपं स कृत्वा तीक्ष्णदीधितिः ..
चमत्कारपुरक्षेत्रे तस्याश्रमपदं ययौ .. 24 ..
5.33.m:
Then, assuming the form of a twice-born, the hot-rayed [sun]
went to the precincts of his hermitage in the sacred field of Camatkārapura.

5.33.s:
tatastu vaiśvadevāṃte vedoccāraparāyaṇaḥ ..
provāca so'tithiḥ prāptastavāhaṃ munisattama .. 25 ..
5.33.d:
ततस्तु वैश्वदेवांते वेदोच्चारपरायणः ..
प्रोवाच सोऽतिथिः प्राप्तस्तवाहं मुनिसत्तम .. 25 ..
5.33.m:
Then, at the conclusion of the Vaiśvadeva rite, devoted to chanting the Veda,
he spoke: “I, a guest, have arrived, O best of sages.”

5.33.s:
tato'gastyaḥ kṛtānandaḥ svāgataṃ te mahāmune ..
manoratha ivādhyāto yo'gnikāryāṃta āgataḥ .. 26 ..
5.33.d:
ततोऽगस्त्यः कृतानन्दः स्वागतं ते महामुने ..
मनोरथ इवाध्यातो योऽग्निकार्यांत आगतः .. 26 ..
5.33.m:
Then Agastya, filled with joy, [said]: “Welcome to you, O great sage,
who have arrived at the end of the fire ritual, like a cherished desire thought upon!

5.33.s:
tattvaṃ brūhi muniśreṣṭha yaddadāmi tavepsitam ..
adeyaṃ nāsti me kiñcitkāle'sminprārthitasya ca .. 27 ..
5.33.d:
तत्त्वं ब्रूहि मुनिश्रेष्ठ यद्ददामि तवेप्सितम् ..
अदेयं नास्ति मे किञ्चित्कालेऽस्मिन्प्रार्थितस्य च .. 27 ..
5.33.m:
Speak the truth, O best of sages, that I may grant your desire;
there is nothing that cannot be given by me when asked for at this time.”

5.33.s:
.. bhāskara uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ bhāskara āyāto viprarūpeṇa sanmune ..
sarvakāryakṣamaṃ matvā tvāmekaṃ bhuvanatraye .. 28 ..
5.33.d:
.. भास्कर उवाच .. ..
अहं भास्कर आयातो विप्ररूपेण सन्मुने ..
सर्वकार्यक्षमं मत्वा त्वामेकं भुवनत्रये .. 28 ..
5.33.m:
Bhāskara said: / “I, Bhāskara, have come in the form of a brahmin, O noble sage,
considering you the only one capable of all deeds in the three worlds.

5.33.s:
tvayā pūrvaṃ surārthāya prapītaḥ payasāṃnidhiḥ ..
vātāpiśca tathā daityo bhakṣito dvijakaṇṭakaḥ .. 29 ..
5.33.d:
त्वया पूर्वं सुरार्थाय प्रपीतः पयसांनिधिः ..
वातापिश्च तथा दैत्यो भक्षितो द्विजकण्टकः .. 29 ..
5.33.m:
Formerly, the ocean of waters was drunk dry by you for the sake of the gods,
and likewise the Daitya Vātāpi, the tormentor of the twice-born, was devoured.

5.33.s:
tasmādgatirbhavāsmākaṃ sāṃprataṃ munisattama ..
devānāmiha varṇānāṃ tvameva śaraṇaṃ yataḥ .. 6.33.30 ..
5.33.d:
तस्माद्गतिर्भवास्माकं सांप्रतं मुनिसत्तम ..
देवानामिह वर्णानां त्वमेव शरणं यतः .. 6.33.30 ..
5.33.m:
Therefore, be our refuge now, O best of sages,
since you alone are the protector of the gods and the castes here.”

5.33.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tacchrutvā sa munirviprā viśeṣeṇa praharṣitaḥ ..
arghyaṃ dattvā dineśāya tataḥ provāca sādaram .. 31 ..
5.33.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा स मुनिर्विप्रा विशेषेण प्रहर्षितः ..
अर्घ्यं दत्त्वा दिनेशाय ततः प्रोवाच सादरम् .. 31 ..
5.33.m:
Sūta said: / Hearing that, O brahmins, that sage was exceedingly delighted;
having offered the respectful water offering to the lord of day, he then said with respect:

5.33.s:
dhanyo'smyanugṛhītosmi yanme tvaṃ gṛhamāgataḥ ..
tasmādbrūhi kariṣyāmi tava vākyamakhaṃḍitam .. 32 ..
5.33.d:
धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोस्मि यन्मे त्वं गृहमागतः ..
तस्माद्ब्रूहि करिष्यामि तव वाक्यमखंडितम् .. 32 ..
5.33.m: "I am blessed, I am graced, that you have come to my home. / Therefore speak, and I shall carry out your word without fail."

5.33.s:
.. bhāskara uvāca .. ..
eṣa viṃdhyācalo'smākaṃ mārgamāvṛtya saṃsthitaḥ .. .
sparddhayā girimukhyasya sumerormunisatama .. 33 ..
5.33.d:
.. भास्कर उवाच .. ..
एष विंध्याचलोऽस्माकं मार्गमावृत्य संस्थितः .. .
स्पर्द्धया गिरिमुख्यस्य सुमेरोर्मुनिसतम .. 33 ..
5.33.m: Bhāskara said: / "This Vindhya mountain stands blocking our path, / out of rivalry with the foremost of mountains, Sumeru, O best of sages.

5.33.s:
sāmādyairvividhopāyaistasmādenaṃ nivāraya ..
kālātyayo yathā na syādgaterbhaṃgastathā kuru .. 34 ... ..
5.33.d:
सामाद्यैर्विविधोपायैस्तस्मादेनं निवारय ..
कालात्ययो यथा न स्याद्गतेर्भंगस्तथा कुरु .. 34 ... ..
5.33.m: Restrain it, therefore, by various means such as conciliation and the rest; / act so that there is no passing of time, so that the course is not obstructed."

5.33.s:
.. agastya uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ te vārayiṣyāmi vardhamānaṃ kulācalam ..
svasthānaṃ gaccha tasmāttvaṃ sukhībhava divākara .. 35 ..
5.33.d:
.. अगस्त्य उवाच .. ..
अहं ते वारयिष्यामि वर्धमानं कुलाचलम् ..
स्वस्थानं गच्छ तस्मात्त्वं सुखीभव दिवाकर .. 35 ..
5.33.m: Agastya said: / "I shall restrain for you this growing clan mountain. / Therefore go to your own place, O maker of day, and be at ease."

5.33.s:
tataḥ sa preṣitaste na bhāskarastīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ ..
svaṃ sthānaṃ prayayau hṛṣṭastamāmaṃtrya munīśvaram .. 36 ..
5.33.d:
ततः स प्रेषितस्ते न भास्करस्तीक्ष्णदीधितिः ..
स्वं स्थानं प्रययौ हृष्टस्तमामंत्र्य मुनीश्वरम् .. 36 ..
5.33.m: Then Bhāskara of sharp rays, dismissed by him, / took leave of that lord of sages and went to his own place, rejoicing.

5.33.s:
agastyo'pi drutaṃ gatvā viṃdhyaṃ provāca sādaram ..
nyūnatāṃ vraja madvākyācchīghraṃ parvatasattama ..37..
5.33.d:
अगस्त्योऽपि द्रुतं गत्वा विंध्यं प्रोवाच सादरम् ..
न्यूनतां व्रज मद्वाक्याच्छीघ्रं पर्वतसत्तम ..37..
5.33.m: Agastya also went quickly and spoke respectfully to the Vindhya: / 'Descend to a low state at my word, swiftly, O best of mountains!

5.33.s:
dākṣiṇātyeṣu tīrtheṣu snāne jātādya me matiḥ ..
tavāyattā gire saiva tatkuruṣva yathocitam .. 38 ..
5.33.d:
दाक्षिणात्येषु तीर्थेषु स्नाने जाताद्य मे मतिः ..
तवायत्ता गिरे सैव तत्कुरुष्व यथोचितम् .. 38 ..
5.33.m: Today the thought has arisen in me to bathe in the southern tīrthas; / that depends on you, O mountain, so act as is fitting.'

5.33.s:
sa tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā viṃdhyaḥ parvatasattamaḥ ..
abhajannimnatāṃ sadyo vinayena samanvitaḥ..39..
5.33.d:
स तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा विंध्यः पर्वतसत्तमः ..
अभजन्निम्नतां सद्यो विनयेन समन्वितः..39..
5.33.m: Hearing his word, the Vindhya, best of mountains, / immediately assumed a low level, filled with humility.

5.33.s:
agastyo'pi samāsādya tasyāṃtaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ dvijāḥ..
tvayaivaṃ saṃsthitenātha() sthātavyamityuvāca tam .. 6.33.40 ..
yāvadāgamanaṃ mahyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
no cecchāpaṃ pradāsyāmi yena saṃyāsyasi kṣayam ..4...
5.33.d:
अगस्त्योऽपि समासाद्य तस्यांतं दक्षिणं द्विजाः..
त्वयैवं संस्थितेनाथ() स्थातव्यमित्युवाच तम् .. 6.33.40 ..
यावदागमनं मह्यं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..
नो चेच्छापं प्रदास्यामि येन संयास्यसि क्षयम् ..4...
5.33.m:
Agastya, having reached its southern border, O twice-born, / said to it: 'You must remain standing just as you are,
until my return; let there be no doubt here. / Otherwise I will pronounce a curse, by which you will meet destruction.'

5.33.s:
sa tatheti pratijñāya śāpādbhīto nagottamaḥ..
na jagāma punarvṛddhiṃ tasyāgamanavāṃchayā..42..
5.33.d:
स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय शापाद्भीतो नगोत्तमः..
न जगाम पुनर्वृद्धिं तस्यागमनवांछया..42..
5.33.m: Promising 'So be it', terrified of the curse, the best of mountains / did not grow again, desiring his return.

5.33.s:
so'pi tenaivamārgeṇa nivṛttiṃ na karoti ca..
yāvadadyāpi vipreṃdrā dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāśrita taḥ ..43..
5.33.d:
सोऽपि तेनैवमार्गेण निवृत्तिं न करोति च..
यावदद्यापि विप्रेंद्रा दक्षिणां दिशमाश्रित तः ..43..
5.33.m: And he [Agastya] did not turn back by that path; / even today, O leaders of brahmins, he remains residing in the southern region.

5.33.s:
atha tatraiva cānīya lopāmudrāṃ munīśvaraḥ ..
samāhūya sahasrāṃśuṃ tataḥ provāca sādaram .. 44 ..
5.33.d:
अथ तत्रैव चानीय लोपामुद्रां मुनीश्वरः ..
समाहूय सहस्रांशुं ततः प्रोवाच सादरम् .. 44 ..
5.33.m: Then, bringing Lopāmudrā there, the lord of sages / summoned the thousand-rayed [sun] and spoke respectfully to him:

5.33.s:
tava vākyānmayā tyaktaḥ svāśramastīkṣṇadī dhite ..
tavārthe ca na gaṃtavyaṃ bhūyastatra kathaṃcana .. 45 ..
5.33.d:
तव वाक्यान्मया त्यक्तः स्वाश्रमस्तीक्ष्णदी धिते ..
तवार्थे च न गंतव्यं भूयस्तत्र कथंचन .. 45 ..
5.33.m: "At your word, O one of sharp rays, I abandoned my own hermitage; / and for your sake, I must by no means go back there again.

5.33.s:
tasmānmadvacanādbhāno caturdaśyāṃ madhau site ..
yanmayā sthāpitaṃ tatra liṃgaṃ pūjyaṃ hi tattva yā .. 46 ..
5.33.d:
तस्मान्मद्वचनाद्भानो चतुर्दश्यां मधौ सिते ..
यन्मया स्थापितं तत्र लिंगं पूज्यं हि तत्त्व या .. 46 ..
5.33.m: Therefore, at my word, O Sun, on the bright fourteenth of Madhu, / that liṅga installed by me there must certainly be worshipped by you."

5.33.s:
.. bhāskara uvāca .. ..
evaṃ mune kariṣyāmi tava vākyādasaṃśayam ..
pūjayiṣyāmi talliṃgaṃ varṣāṃte svayameva hi .. 47 ..
5.33.d:
.. भास्कर उवाच .. ..
एवं मुने करिष्यामि तव वाक्यादसंशयम् ..
पूजयिष्यामि तल्लिंगं वर्षांते स्वयमेव हि .. 47 ..
5.33.m: Bhāskara said: / "O sage, at your word I will certainly do so without doubt. / I myself shall worship that liṅga at the end of the year.

5.33.s:
yo'nyo hi taddine liṃgaṃ pūjayiṣyati mānavaḥ ..
mama lokaṃ samāsādya sa bhaviṣyati muktibhāk .. 48..
5.33.d:
योऽन्यो हि तद्दिने लिंगं पूजयिष्यति मानवः ..
मम लोकं समासाद्य स भविष्यति मुक्तिभाक् .. 48..
5.33.m: Whatever other human being worships that liṅga on that day / shall reach my world and attain liberation."

5.33.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
etasmātkāraṇāttatra bhagavāṃstīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ ..
caitraśuklacaturdaśyāṃ sāṃnidhyaṃ kurute sadā .. 49 ..
5.33.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एतस्मात्कारणात्तत्र भगवांस्तीक्ष्णदीधितिः ..
चैत्रशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां सांनिध्यं कुरुते सदा .. 49 ..
5.33.m: Sūta said: / For this reason the blessed one of sharp rays / always manifests his presence there on the fourteenth of the bright half of Caitra.

5.33.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭosmi dvijottamāḥ ..
bhūyo vadata vai kaścitsaṃdehaśce ddhṛdi sthitaḥ .. 6.33.50 ..
iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye 'gastyāśramamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma trayastriṃśattamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 33 .. cha ..
5.33.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं यत्पृष्टोस्मि द्विजोत्तमाः ..
भूयो वदत वै कश्चित्संदेहश्चे द्धृदि स्थितः .. 6.33.50 ..
इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये ऽगस्त्याश्रममाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम त्रयस्त्रिंशत्तमोऽध्यायः .. 33 .. छ ..
5.33.m:
All this which I was asked has been told to you, O best of the twice-born; / speak again if any doubt remains in your hearts.
Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Agastya's Hermitage,' in the glory of the Hāṭakeśvara field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the auspicious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.34.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ taṃ muniṃ prati sūtaja ..
tvayā purā surārthāya prapītaḥ payasāṃnidhiḥ .. 1 ..
5.34.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
यदेतद्भवता प्रोक्तं तं मुनिं प्रति सूतज ..
त्वया पुरा सुरार्थाय प्रपीतः पयसांनिधिः .. 1 ..
5.34.m: The seers said: / "As for that which was mentioned by you concerning that sage, O son of Sūta: / 'Long ago, for the sake of the gods, the ocean of water was drunk up by you'—

5.34.s:
tattvaṃ sūtaja no brūhi vistareṇa mahāmate ..
yathā tena purā pīto muninā payasāṃnidhiḥ .. 2 ..
5.34.d:
तत्त्वं सूतज नो ब्रूहि विस्तरेण महामते ..
यथा तेन पुरा पीतो मुनिना पयसांनिधिः .. 2 ..
5.34.m: Tell us that in detail, O wise son of Sūta, / how formerly the ocean of water was drunk up by that sage."

5.34.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
kāleyā iti vikhyātāḥ purā dānavasattamāḥ ..
saṃbhūtāḥ sarvadevānāṃ vīryotsāhapraṇāśakāḥ .. 3 ..
5.34.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
कालेया इति विख्याताः पुरा दानवसत्तमाः ..
संभूताः सर्वदेवानां वीर्योत्साहप्रणाशकाः .. 3 ..
5.34.m: Sūta said: / Formerly there arose the foremost Dānavas known as the Kāleyas, / who destroyed the strength and enthusiasm of all the gods.

5.34.s:
tatastaiḥ pīḍitaṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā ..
trailokyaṃ śaktiyogena prokto devo maheśvaraḥ ..4..
5.34.d:
ततस्तैः पीडितं दृष्ट्वा विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ..
त्रैलोक्यं शक्तियोगेन प्रोक्तो देवो महेश्वरः ..4..
5.34.m: Then, seeing the three worlds oppressed by them, the mighty Viṣṇu / spoke through the power of his yoga to the god Maheśvara:

5.34.s:
etadīśāna daiteyaistrailokyaṃ paripīḍitam..
kālikeyairmahāvīryestasmātkāryo mahāhavaḥ..
adyaiva taiḥ samaṃ deva samāsādya dharātalam.. 5 ..
5.34.d:
एतदीशान दैतेयैस्त्रैलोक्यं परिपीडितम्..
कालिकेयैर्महावीर्येस्तस्मात्कार्यो महाहवः..
अद्यैव तैः समं देव समासाद्य धरातलम्.. 5 ..
5.34.m: "O Īśāna, the three worlds are utterly tormented by the Daiteyas, / the Kālikeyas of great valor; therefore a great battle must be fought / with them this very day, O god, descending upon the earth's surface."

5.34.s:
tato viṣṇuśca rudraśca sahasrākṣaḥ suraiḥ saha ..
śitaśastradharāḥ sarve saṃprāptā dharaṇītalam .. 6 ..
5.34.d:
ततो विष्णुश्च रुद्रश्च सहस्राक्षः सुरैः सह ..
शितशस्त्रधराः सर्वे संप्राप्ता धरणीतलम् .. 6 ..
5.34.m: Then Viṣṇu, Rudra, and the thousand-eyed [Indra] along with the gods, / all bearing sharpened weapons, arrived on the surface of the earth.

5.34.s:
atha te dānavāḥ sarve śrutvā devānsa- māgatān ..
yuddhārthaṃ sahasā jagmuḥ saṃmukhāḥ kopasaṃyutāḥ .. 7 ..
5.34.d:
अथ ते दानवाः सर्वे श्रुत्वा देवान्स- मागतान् ..
युद्धार्थं सहसा जग्मुः संमुखाः कोपसंयुताः .. 7 ..
5.34.m: Then all those Dānavas, hearing that the gods had assembled, / quickly advanced to meet them, filled with rage, to fight.

5.34.s:
tato'bhavanmahāyuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha ..
trailokyaṃ kaṃpitaṃ yena samastaṃ bhaya vihvalam.. 8 ..
5.34.d:
ततोऽभवन्महायुद्धं देवानां दानवैः सह ..
त्रैलोक्यं कंपितं येन समस्तं भय विह्वलम्.. 8 ..
5.34.m: Then a great battle took place between the gods and the Dānavas, / by which all the three worlds were shaken, overcome with fear.

5.34.s:
atha kālaprabhonāma dānavo balagarvitaḥ ..
sa śakraṃ purato dṛṣṭvā vajrocchritakaraṃ sthitam..
provāca prahasanvākyaṃ meghagambhīraniḥsvanaḥ .. 9 ..
5.34.d:
अथ कालप्रभोनाम दानवो बलगर्वितः ..
स शक्रं पुरतो दृष्ट्वा वज्रोच्छ्रितकरं स्थितम्..
प्रोवाच प्रहसन्वाक्यं मेघगम्भीरनिःस्वनः .. 9 ..
5.34.m: Then the Dānava named Kālaprabha, proud of his strength, / seeing Śakra standing before him with the thunderbolt raised in his hand, / laughed and spoke with a voice deep as a thundercloud:

5.34.s:
muṃca vajra sahasrākṣa paśyāmi tava pauruṣam ..
cirātprāpto'si me dṛṣṭiṃ diṣṭyā tvaṃ tridiveśvaraḥ .. 6.34.10 ..
5.34.d:
मुंच वज्र सहस्राक्ष पश्यामि तव पौरुषम् ..
चिरात्प्राप्तोऽसि मे दृष्टिं दिष्ट्या त्वं त्रिदिवेश्वरः .. 6.34.10 ..
5.34.m: "Release your thunderbolt, O thousand-eyed one! Let me see your manly strength! / By good fortune, after a long time, you, the lord of heaven, have come within my sight!"

5.34.s:
tataścikṣepa saṃkruddhastasya vajraṃ śatakratuḥ ..
so'pi tallīlayā dhṛtvā jagṛhe savyapāṇinā .. 11 ..
5.34.d:
ततश्चिक्षेप संक्रुद्धस्तस्य वज्रं शतक्रतुः ..
सोऽपि तल्लीलया धृत्वा जगृहे सव्यपाणिना .. 11 ..
5.34.m: Then Śatakratu, deeply enraged, hurled his thunderbolt at him; / but he caught it playfully and seized it with his left hand.

5.34.s:
tataḥ śakraṃ samuddiśya gadāṃ gurvīṃ mumoca saḥ ..
sarvāyasamayīṃ raudrāṃ yamajihvāmivāparām .. 12 ..
5.34.d:
ततः शक्रं समुद्दिश्य गदां गुर्वीं मुमोच सः ..
सर्वायसमयीं रौद्रां यमजिह्वामिवापराम् .. 12 ..
5.34.m: Then, aiming at Śakra, he hurled a heavy mace / made entirely of iron, dreadful, like a second tongue of Yama.

5.34.s:
tayā hataḥ sahasrākṣo visaṃjño rudhiraplutaḥ ..
dhvajayaṣṭiṃ samāśritya saṃniviṣṭo rathopari .. 13 ..
5.34.d:
तया हतः सहस्राक्षो विसंज्ञो रुधिरप्लुतः ..
ध्वजयष्टिं समाश्रित्य संनिविष्टो रथोपरि .. 13 ..
5.34.m: Struck by it, the thousand-eyed [Indra] lost consciousness, bathed in blood; / leaning against the flagpole, he collapsed upon the chariot.

5.34.s:
atha taṃ mātalirdṛṣṭvā visaṃjñaṃ valaghātinam..
prāṅmukhaṃ ca rathaṃ cakre saṃsmaransārathernayam .. 14 ..
5.34.d:
अथ तं मातलिर्दृष्ट्वा विसंज्ञं वलघातिनम्..
प्राङ्मुखं च रथं चक्रे संस्मरन्सारथेर्नयम् .. 14 ..
5.34.m: Then Mātali, seeing that slayer of Vala unconscious / and recalling the duty of a charioteer, turned the chariot eastward.

5.34.s:
tataḥ parāṅmukhībhūte rathe śakrasya saṃgare ..
dudruvurbhayasaṃtrastāḥ sarve devāḥ samaṃtataḥ .. 15 ..
5.34.d:
ततः पराङ्मुखीभूते रथे शक्रस्य संगरे ..
दुद्रुवुर्भयसंत्रस्ताः सर्वे देवाः समंततः .. 15 ..
5.34.m: Then, when Śakra's chariot turned away in the battle, / all the gods fled in all directions, terrified with fear.

5.34.s:
ādityā vasavo rudrā viśvedevā marudgaṇāḥ ..
vrīḍāṃ vihāya vidhvastāḥ pṛṣṭhadeśe śitaiḥ śaraiḥ .. 16 ..
5.34.d:
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा विश्वेदेवा मरुद्गणाः ..
व्रीडां विहाय विध्वस्ताः पृष्ठदेशे शितैः शरैः .. 16 ..
5.34.m: The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Viśvedevas, and troops of Maruts, / casting aside shame, were shattered in the rear by sharp arrows.

5.34.s:
atha bhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā dānavairmadhusūdanaḥ ..
āruhya garuḍaṃ tūrṇaṃ kālaprabhamupādravat .. 17 ..
tataste dānavāḥ sarve parivārya śitaiḥ śaraiḥ ..
samyagācchādayāmāsurgarjamānā muhurmuhuḥ...8 ..
5.34.d:
अथ भग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा दानवैर्मधुसूदनः ..
आरुह्य गरुडं तूर्णं कालप्रभमुपाद्रवत् .. 17 ..
ततस्ते दानवाः सर्वे परिवार्य शितैः शरैः ..
सम्यगाच्छादयामासुर्गर्जमाना मुहुर्मुहुः...8 ..
5.34.m:
Then Madhusūdana, seeing the army broken by the Dānavas, / mounted Garuḍa and swiftly rushed upon Kālaprabha.
Then all those Dānavas surrounded [him] and covered him completely / with sharp arrows, roaring again and again.

5.34.s:
sa tairācchādito viṣṇuḥ śuśubhe ca samaṃtataḥ ..
samyakpulakitāṃgaśca raktācala ivāparaḥ .. 19 ..
5.34.d:
स तैराच्छादितो विष्णुः शुशुभे च समंततः ..
सम्यक्पुलकितांगश्च रक्ताचल इवापरः .. 19 ..
5.34.m: Covered by them, Viṣṇu shone on all sides, / with his limbs thoroughly bristling [with arrows], like another mountain of blood.

5.34.s:
tataḥ śārṅgavinirmuktaiḥ śaraiḥ kaṃkapatatribhiḥ ..
chedayitveṣujālāni daiteyānnijaghāna saḥ .. 6.34.20 ..
5.34.d:
ततः शार्ङ्गविनिर्मुक्तैः शरैः कंकपतत्रिभिः ..
छेदयित्वेषुजालानि दैतेयान्निजघान सः .. 6.34.20 ..
5.34.m: Then, having severed the nets of arrows with heron-feathered arrows / shot from the Śārṅga bow, he struck down the Daiteyas.

5.34.s:
tato daityagaṇāḥ sarve hanyamānā surāriṇā ..
trātāraṃ nābhyagacchaṃta mṛgāḥ siṃhārditā iva .. 21 ..
5.34.d:
ततो दैत्यगणाः सर्वे हन्यमाना सुरारिणा ..
त्रातारं नाभ्यगच्छंत मृगाः सिंहार्दिता इव .. 21 ..
5.34.m: Then all the hosts of Daityas, being struck down by the enemy of the asuras, / found no protector, like deer harassed by a lion.

5.34.s:
etasminnaṃtare daityaḥ kālakhaṃja iti smṛtaḥ..
sa kopavaśamāpanno vāsudevamupādravat .. 22 ..
5.34.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे दैत्यः कालखंज इति स्मृतः..
स कोपवशमापन्नो वासुदेवमुपाद्रवत् .. 22 ..
5.34.m: In the meantime, a Daitya known as Kālakhañja, / overcome with fury, rushed against Vāsudeva.

5.34.s:
sa hatvā pañcabhirbāṇairvāsudevaṃ śilā śitaiḥ ..
jaghāna garuḍaṃ kruddho daśabhirnataparvabhiḥ..23..
5.34.d:
स हत्वा पञ्चभिर्बाणैर्वासुदेवं शिला शितैः ..
जघान गरुडं क्रुद्धो दशभिर्नतपर्वभिः..23..
5.34.m: Striking Vāsudeva with five stone-sharpened arrows, / enraged, he struck Garuḍa with ten straight-jointed shafts.

5.34.s:
tataḥ sudarśanaṃ cakraṃ tasya daityasya mādhavaḥ .]
pramumoca vadhārthāya jvālāmālāsamāvṛtam ..24..
5.34.d:
ततः सुदर्शनं चक्रं तस्य दैत्यस्य माधवः .]
प्रमुमोच वधार्थाय ज्वालामालासमावृतम् ..24..
5.34.m: Then, to slay that Daitya, Mādhava released / the Sudarśana discus surrounded by garlands of flames.

5.34.s:
so'pi taccakramālokya vāsudevakarāccyutam ..
āgacchaṃtaṃ prasāryāsyaṃ grastuṃ tatsaṃmukho yayau .. 25 ..
5.34.d:
सोऽपि तच्चक्रमालोक्य वासुदेवकराच्च्युतम् ..
आगच्छंतं प्रसार्यास्यं ग्रस्तुं तत्संमुखो ययौ .. 25 ..
5.34.m: Seeing that discus loosed from Vāsudeva's hand, / he opened his mouth and went before it to swallow it as it approached.

5.34.s:
agrasacca mahādaityastiṣṭhatiṣṭheti cābravīt ..
vāsudevaṃ samuddiśya tataścikṣepa sāyakān .. 26 ..
5.34.d:
अग्रसच्च महादैत्यस्तिष्ठतिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत् ..
वासुदेवं समुद्दिश्य ततश्चिक्षेप सायकान् .. 26 ..
5.34.m: The great Daitya swallowed it and shouted, "Halt, halt!" / Addressing Vāsudeva, he then shot arrows [at him].

5.34.s:
tataścakrī sa daityena grastacakreṇa tāḍitaḥ ..
suparṇena samāyukto jagāma viṣamāṃ vyathām .. 27 ..
5.34.d:
ततश्चक्री स दैत्येन ग्रस्तचक्रेण ताडितः ..
सुपर्णेन समायुक्तो जगाम विषमां व्यथाम् .. 27 ..
5.34.m: Then the discus-wielder, struck by that Daitya who had swallowed his discus, / along with Garuḍa, fell into acute distress.

5.34.s:
etasminnaṃtare kruddho bhagavāṃstripurāṃtakaḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā hariṃ tathābhūtaṃ śakraṃ cāpi parāṅmukham .. 28 ..
5.34.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे क्रुद्धो भगवांस्त्रिपुरांतकः ..
दृष्ट्वा हरिं तथाभूतं शक्रं चापि पराङ्मुखम् .. 28 ..
5.34.m: In the meantime, the blessed destroyer of Tripura, enraged / upon seeing Hari in such a state and Śakra also turning back,

5.34.s:
tataḥ śūlaprahāreṇa taṃ nihatya danoḥ sutam ..
śaraiḥ pinākanirmuktairjaghānoccaistathā parān .. 29 ..
5.34.d:
ततः शूलप्रहारेण तं निहत्य दनोः सुतम् ..
शरैः पिनाकनिर्मुक्तैर्जघानोच्चैस्तथा परान् .. 29 ..
5.34.m: then killed that son of Danu with a blow of his trident / and struck down others in great numbers with arrows shot from Pināka.

5.34.s:
kālaprabhaṃ prakālaṃ ca kālāsyaṃ kālavigraham ..
jaghāna bhagavāñchaṃbhustathānyānapi nāyakān ..6.34.30..
5.34.d:
कालप्रभं प्रकालं च कालास्यं कालविग्रहम् ..
जघान भगवाञ्छंभुस्तथान्यानपि नायकान् ..6.34.30..
5.34.m: The blessed Śambhu struck down Kālaprabha, Prakāla, / Kālāsya, and Kālavigraha, as well as other leaders.

5.34.s:
tataḥ pradhānāste sarve dānavā apidāruṇāḥ ..
palāyanaparā jātā nirutsāhā dviṣajjaye .. 31 ..
5.34.d:
ततः प्रधानास्ते सर्वे दानवा अपिदारुणाः ..
पलायनपरा जाता निरुत्साहा द्विषज्जये .. 31 ..
5.34.m: Then all those chief Dānavas, though fierce, / took to flight, devoid of enthusiasm for conquering their enemies.

5.34.s:
tataḥ śakraśca viṣṇuśca labdhasaṃjñau dhṛtāyudhau ..
ślāghayaṃtau mahādevaṃ saṃsthitau raṇamūrdhani .. 32 ..
5.34.d:
ततः शक्रश्च विष्णुश्च लब्धसंज्ञौ धृतायुधौ ..
श्लाघयंतौ महादेवं संस्थितौ रणमूर्धनि .. 32 ..
5.34.m: Then Śakra and Viṣṇu, having regained consciousness and seizing their weapons, / stood at the forefront of the battle, praising Mahādeva.

5.34.s:
etasminnaṃtare bhagnānsamudvīkṣya danoḥ sutān ..
jaghnuḥ śaraśataiḥ śastraiḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ .. 33 ..
5.34.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे भग्नान्समुद्वीक्ष्य दनोः सुतान् ..
जघ्नुः शरशतैः शस्त्रैः सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः .. 33 ..
5.34.m: In the meantime, seeing the sons of Danu broken, / all the gods along with Indra struck them down with hundreds of arrows and weapons.

5.34.s:
atha te hatabhūyiṣṭhā dānavā balavattarāḥ ..
hanyamānāḥ śitairbāṇaistridaśairjitakāśibhiḥ .. 34 ..
5.34.d:
अथ ते हतभूयिष्ठा दानवा बलवत्तराः ..
हन्यमानाः शितैर्बाणैस्त्रिदशैर्जितकाशिभिः .. 34 ..
5.34.m: Then those mighty Dānavas, mostly slaughtered, / being struck with sharp arrows by the gods appearing victorious,

5.34.s:
agamyaṃ manasā teṣāṃ praviṣṭā varuṇālayam ..
śastraiśca kṣatasarvāṃgā hatanāthāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ .. 35 ..
iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramā hātmye'gastyāśramamāhātmye'gastyakṛtasamudraprāśanavṛttānte devāsurasaṃgrāmavarṇanaṃnāma catustriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 34 .. .. cha ..
5.34.d:
अगम्यं मनसा तेषां प्रविष्टा वरुणालयम् ..
शस्त्रैश्च क्षतसर्वांगा हतनाथाः सुदुःखिताः .. 35 ..
इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमा हात्म्येऽगस्त्याश्रममाहात्म्येऽगस्त्यकृतसमुद्रप्राशनवृत्तान्ते देवासुरसंग्रामवर्णनंनाम चतुस्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 34 .. .. छ ..
5.34.m:
entered the abode of Varuṇa, which was unapproachable even in thought by them, / all their limbs wounded by weapons, their leaders slain, in great misery.
Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, named 'Description of the Battle between the Gods and Asuras' in the account of the drinking of the ocean by Agastya, in the māhātmya of Agastya's Hermitage, in the māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.35.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ teṣu prabhagneṣu hateṣu ca surottamāḥ ..
prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve stutvā devaṃ maheśvaram .. 1 ..
5.35.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं तेषु प्रभग्नेषु हतेषु च सुरोत्तमाः ..
प्रहृष्टमनसः सर्वे स्तुत्वा देवं महेश्वरम् .. 1 ..
5.35.m: Sūta said: / When they were broken and slain in this way, the foremost gods, / all rejoicing in heart, praised the god Maheśvara.

5.35.s:
tenaiva cātha nirmuktāḥ praṇamya ca muhurmuhuḥ ..
svaṃsvaṃ sthānamathājagmuḥ śakraviṣṇupuraḥsarāḥ .. 2 ..
5.35.d:
तेनैव चाथ निर्मुक्ताः प्रणम्य च मुहुर्मुहुः ..
स्वंस्वं स्थानमथाजग्मुः शक्रविष्णुपुरःसराः .. 2 ..
5.35.m: Then, dismissed by him, bowing repeatedly, / led by Śakra and Viṣṇu, they departed each to their own abode.

5.35.s:
te'pi dānavaśārdūlā hatāśāśca surottamaiḥ ..
maṃtraṃ pracakrire sarve nāśāya tridivaukasām .. 3 ..
5.35.d:
तेऽपि दानवशार्दूला हताशाश्च सुरोत्तमैः ..
मंत्रं प्रचक्रिरे सर्वे नाशाय त्रिदिवौकसाम् .. 3 ..
5.35.m: Those foremost Dānavas as well, their hopes shattered by the highest gods, / all held counsel for the destruction of the heaven-dwellers.

5.35.s:
teṣāṃ maṃtrayatāmeṣa niścayaḥ samapadyata ..
nānyatra dharmavidhvaṃsāddevānāṃ jāyate kṣayaḥ .. 4 ..
5.35.d:
तेषां मंत्रयतामेष निश्चयः समपद्यत ..
नान्यत्र धर्मविध्वंसाद्देवानां जायते क्षयः .. 4 ..
5.35.m: As they deliberated, this decision was reached: / "Except through the destruction of dharma, the ruin of the gods does not occur.

5.35.s:
tasmāttapasvino yai ca ye ca yajñaparāyaṇāḥ ..
tathānye niratā dharme nihantavyā niśāgame .. 5 ..
5.35.d:
तस्मात्तपस्विनो यै च ये च यज्ञपरायणाः ..
तथान्ये निरता धर्मे निहन्तव्या निशागमे .. 5 ..
5.35.m: Therefore, the ascetics, those devoted to sacrifice, / and others engaged in dharma are to be slaughtered when night arrives."

5.35.s:
evaṃ te niścayaṃ kṛtvā niṣkramya varuṇālayāt ..
rātrau sadaiva nighnaṃti janāndharmaparāyaṇān .. 6 ..
5.35.d:
एवं ते निश्चयं कृत्वा निष्क्रम्य वरुणालयात् ..
रात्रौ सदैव निघ्नंति जनान्धर्मपरायणान् .. 6 ..
5.35.m: Having thus made their decision, emerging from the abode of Varuṇa, / they continually slaughter people devoted to dharma at night.

5.35.s:
yatra yatra bhavedyajñaḥ satraṃ 'pyutsavo'thavā ..
tatra gatvā niśāyoge prakurvaṃti janakṣayam .. 7 ..
5.35.d:
यत्र यत्र भवेद्यज्ञः सत्रं ऽप्युत्सवोऽथवा ..
तत्र गत्वा निशायोगे प्रकुर्वंति जनक्षयम् .. 7 ..
5.35.m: Wherever there was a sacrifice, an oblation-session, or a festival, / going there at nightfall, they brought about the destruction of people.

5.35.s:
taiḥ prasūtā makhā dhvastā dīkṣitā vinipātitāḥ ..
ṛtvijaśca tathānye'pi sāmānyā dvijasattamāḥ .. 8- ..
āśrame munimukhyasya śāṃḍilyasya mahātmanaḥ ..
sahasraṃ brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ bhakṣitaṃ tairdurātmabhiḥ. .. 9 ..
5.35.d:
तैः प्रसूता मखा ध्वस्ता दीक्षिता विनिपातिताः ..
ऋत्विजश्च तथान्येऽपि सामान्या द्विजसत्तमाः .. 8- ..
आश्रमे मुनिमुख्यस्य शांडिल्यस्य महात्मनः ..
सहस्रं ब्राह्मणेंद्राणां भक्षितं तैर्दुरात्मभिः. .. 9 ..
5.35.m: By them sacrifices commenced were ruined; the consecrated were struck down, / as were priests and other ordinary foremost twice-born ones. / In the hermitage of the noble Śāṇḍilya, foremost among sages, / a thousand chief brahmins were devoured by those evil-minded ones.

5.35.s:
śatāni ca sahasrāṇi nihatāni dvijanmanām ..
viśvāmitrasya pañcaiva saptātreścaiva dhīmataḥ .. 6.35.10 ..
5.35.d:
शतानि च सहस्राणि निहतानि द्विजन्मनाम् ..
विश्वामित्रस्य पञ्चैव सप्तात्रेश्चैव धीमतः .. 6.35.10 ..
5.35.m: And hundreds of thousands of twice-born ones were killed: / five [thousand] of Viśvāmitra, and seven of the wise Atri.

5.35.s:
etasminneva kāle tu samastaṃ dharaṇītalam ..
naṣṭayajñotsavaṃ jātaṃ kāleyabhayapīḍitam .. 11 ..
5.35.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु समस्तं धरणीतलम् ..
नष्टयज्ञोत्सवं जातं कालेयभयपीडितम् .. 11 ..
5.35.m: At that very time, the entire surface of the earth, / with its sacrificial festivals destroyed, was afflicted by the dread of the Kāleyas.

5.35.s:
na kaścicchayanaṃ rātrau prakaroti mahī tale ..
dhṛtāyudhā janāḥ sarve tiṣṭhaṃti saha tāpasaiḥ .. 12 ..
5.35.d:
न कश्चिच्छयनं रात्रौ प्रकरोति मही तले ..
धृतायुधा जनाः सर्वे तिष्ठंति सह तापसैः .. 12 ..
5.35.m: No one slept at night on the surface of the earth; / all people stood, weapons in hand, along with the ascetics.

5.35.s:
rātrau svapaṃti ye kecidviśvastā dharmabhājanāḥ ..
teṣāmasthīni dṛśyaṃte prātareva hi kevalam .. 13 ..
5.35.d:
रात्रौ स्वपंति ये केचिद्विश्वस्ता धर्मभाजनाः ..
तेषामस्थीनि दृश्यंते प्रातरेव हि केवलम् .. 13 ..
5.35.m: Whichever confident performers of dharma slept at night, / only their bones were to be seen in the morning.

5.35.s:
atha devagaṇāḥ sarve yajñabhāgavinākṛtāḥ ..
prajagmuḥ paramāmārti brahmaviṣṇupurassarāḥ .. 14 ..
5.35.d:
अथ देवगणाः सर्वे यज्ञभागविनाकृताः ..
प्रजग्मुः परमामार्ति ब्रह्मविष्णुपुरस्सराः .. 14 ..
5.35.m: Then all the hosts of gods, deprived of their shares in sacrifices, / fell into extreme distress, with Brahmā and Viṣṇu at their head.

5.35.s:
tato gatvā samudrāṃtaṃ vadhāya suravidviṣām ..
na śekurviṣamasthāṃstānmanasāpi pradharṣitum .. 15 ..
5.35.d:
ततो गत्वा समुद्रांतं वधाय सुरविद्विषाम् ..
न शेकुर्विषमस्थांस्तान्मनसापि प्रधर्षितुम् .. 15 ..
5.35.m: Then, having gone to the edge of the ocean to slay the enemies of the gods, / they were unable even in thought to overpower them established in that difficult place.

5.35.s:
tataḥ samudranāśāya maṃtraṃ cakruḥ suduḥkhitāḥ ..
tasminnaṣṭe bhavantyeva vadhyā dānavasattamāḥ ..16..
5.35.d:
ततः समुद्रनाशाय मंत्रं चक्रुः सुदुःखिताः ..
तस्मिन्नष्टे भवन्त्येव वध्या दानवसत्तमाः ..16..
5.35.m: Then, deeply grieved, they took counsel for the destruction of the ocean: / "Once that is destroyed, the foremost Dānavas will indeed be liable to be slain.

5.35.s:
agastyena vinā naiṣa śoṣaṃ yāsyati sāgaraḥ ..
tasmātsaṃprārthayāmotra kṛtye gatvā munīśvaram ..17..
5.35.d:
अगस्त्येन विना नैष शोषं यास्यति सागरः ..
तस्मात्संप्रार्थयामोत्र कृत्ये गत्वा मुनीश्वरम् ..17..
5.35.m: Without Agastya, this ocean will not dry up; / therefore, let us go and entreat the lord of sages for this deed.

5.35.s:
camatkārapure kṣetre sa tiṣṭhati ca sanmuniḥ ..
tasmāttatraiva gacchāmo yena gacchati satvaram ..18..
5.35.d:
चमत्कारपुरे क्षेत्रे स तिष्ठति च सन्मुनिः ..
तस्मात्तत्रैव गच्छामो येन गच्छति सत्वरम् ..18..
5.35.m: That noble sage resides in the Camatkārapura sacred field; / therefore, let us go right there so that he may set out quickly."

5.35.s:
evaṃ niścitya te sarve tridaśāstasya cāśramam ..
saṃprāptā munimukhyasya mitrāvaruṇa janmanaḥ .. 19 ..
5.35.d:
एवं निश्चित्य ते सर्वे त्रिदशास्तस्य चाश्रमम् ..
संप्राप्ता मुनिमुख्यस्य मित्रावरुण जन्मनः .. 19 ..
5.35.m: Having resolved thus, all those gods reached the hermitage / of that foremost among sages born of Mitra and Varuṇa.

5.35.s:
so'pi sarvānsamālokya saṃprāptānsurasattamān ..
prahṛṣṭaḥ sammukhastūrṇaṃ jagāmātīva sanmuniḥ .. 6.35.20 ..
5.35.d:
सोऽपि सर्वान्समालोक्य संप्राप्तान्सुरसत्तमान् ..
प्रहृष्टः सम्मुखस्तूर्णं जगामातीव सन्मुनिः .. 6.35.20 ..
5.35.m: Seeing all the foremost gods who had arrived, / that noble sage, exceedingly delighted, went swiftly to meet them.

5.35.s:
provāca prāṃjalirvākyaṃ harṣa gadgadayā girā ..
brahmādīṃstānsurāndṛṣṭvā vismayotphullalocanaḥ .. 21 ..
5.35.d:
प्रोवाच प्रांजलिर्वाक्यं हर्ष गद्गदया गिरा ..
ब्रह्मादींस्तान्सुरान्दृष्ट्वा विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनः .. 21 ..
5.35.m: With folded hands, he spoke with a voice trembling with joy, / his eyes wide open with wonder upon seeing those gods led by Brahmā:

5.35.s:
camatkārapuraṃ kṣetrametanmedhyamapi sthitam ..
bhūyo medhyataraṃ jātaṃ yuṣmākaṃ hi samāśrayāt.. 22 ..
5.35.d:
चमत्कारपुरं क्षेत्रमेतन्मेध्यमपि स्थितम् ..
भूयो मेध्यतरं जातं युष्माकं हि समाश्रयात्.. 22 ..
5.35.m: "This Camatkārapura sacred field, though already pure, / has become even purer indeed through your refuge.

5.35.s:
tasmādvadata yatkṛtyaṃ mayā saṃsiddhyate'dhunā ..
tatsarvaṃ prakariṣyāmi yadyapi syātsuduṣkaram.. 23 ..
5.35.d:
तस्माद्वदत यत्कृत्यं मया संसिद्ध्यतेऽधुना ..
तत्सर्वं प्रकरिष्यामि यद्यपि स्यात्सुदुष्करम्.. 23 ..
5.35.m: Therefore, speak what task may be accomplished by me now; / I will perform all of it, even if it be very difficult to do."

5.35.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
kāleyā iti daityā ye hataśeṣāḥ suraiḥ kṛtāḥ ..
te samudraṃ samāśritya nighnaṃti śubhakāriṇaḥ .. 24 ..
5.35.d:
.. देवा ऊचुः .. ..
कालेया इति दैत्या ये हतशेषाः सुरैः कृताः ..
ते समुद्रं समाश्रित्य निघ्नंति शुभकारिणः .. 24 ..
5.35.m: The gods said: / "Those Daityas known as the Kāleyas, who were left over after being struck down by the gods, / taking shelter in the ocean, are slaughtering those who perform good deeds.

5.35.s:
śubhe nāśamanuprāpte dhruvaṃ nāśo divaukasām ..
tasmātteṣāṃ vadhārthāya tvaṃ śoṣaya mahārṇavam .. 25 ..
5.35.d:
शुभे नाशमनुप्राप्ते ध्रुवं नाशो दिवौकसाम् ..
