तस्मात्तेषां वधार्थाय त्वं शोषय महार्णवम् .. 25 ..
5.35.m: When goodness meets with destruction, the destruction of the heaven-dwellers is certain. / Therefore, dry up the great ocean for their slaughter,

5.35.s:
yena te gocaraṃ prāptā dṛṣṭerdānavasattamāḥ ..
badhyaṃte vibudhaiḥ sarve jāyaṃte ca makhā iha .. 26 .. ..
5.35.d:
येन ते गोचरं प्राप्ता दृष्टेर्दानवसत्तमाः ..
बध्यंते विबुधैः सर्वे जायंते च मखा इह .. 26 .. ..
5.35.m: so that, brought within the range of sight, all those foremost Dānavas / may be slain by the gods, and sacrifices may take place here."

5.35.s:
.. agastya uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ saṃvatsarasyāṃte śoṣayiṣyāmi sāgaram ..
vidyābalaṃ samāśritya yoginīnāṃ surottamāḥ .. 27 ..
5.35.d:
.. अगस्त्य उवाच .. ..
अहं संवत्सरस्यांते शोषयिष्यामि सागरम् ..
विद्याबलं समाश्रित्य योगिनीनां सुरोत्तमाः .. 27 ..
5.35.m: Agastya said: / "At the end of a year I will dry up the ocean, / relying on the power of the magical knowledge of the yoginīs, O foremost gods."

5.35.s:
tasmādvrajata harmyāṇi yūyaṃ yāti hi vatsaram ..
yāvadbhūyo'pi varṣāṃte kāryamāgamanaṃ dhruvam .. 28 ..
5.35.d:
तस्माद्व्रजत हर्म्याणि यूयं याति हि वत्सरम् ..
यावद्भूयोऽपि वर्षांते कार्यमागमनं ध्रुवम् .. 28 ..
5.35.m: "Therefore go to your mansions; for a year is passing. / When the year has ended, you must certainly return here again.

5.35.s:
tato mayā samaṃ gatvā śoṣite varuṇālaye ..
haṃtavyā dānavā duṣṭā hanta yaiḥ pīḍyate jagat .. 29 ..
5.35.d:
ततो मया समं गत्वा शोषिते वरुणालये ..
हंतव्या दानवा दुष्टा हन्त यैः पीड्यते जगत् .. 29 ..
5.35.m: Then, having gone together with me once the abode of Varuṇa is dried up, / the wicked Dānavas must be slain—alas, by whom the world is tormented!"

5.35.s:
tato devagaṇāḥ sarve gatāḥ svesve niketane ..
agastyo'pi samudyogaṃ cakre vidyāsamudbhavam .. 6.35.30 ..
5.35.d:
ततो देवगणाः सर्वे गताः स्वेस्वे निकेतने ..
अगस्त्योऽपि समुद्योगं चक्रे विद्यासमुद्भवम् .. 6.35.30 ..
5.35.m: Then all the hosts of gods went to their respective abodes. / Agastya too made energetic effort born of the vidyā.

5.35.s:
tataḥ sarvāṇi pīṭhāni yāni saṃti dharātale ..
tāni tatrānayāmāsa maṃtraśaktyā mahāmuniḥ .. 31 ..
5.35.d:
ततः सर्वाणि पीठानि यानि संति धरातले ..
तानि तत्रानयामास मंत्रशक्त्या महामुनिः .. 31 ..
5.35.m: Then all the sacred seats that exist upon the surface of the earth, / those the great sage brought there through the power of mantras.

5.35.s:
aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ teṣu saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ ..
yoginīnāṃ ca vṛndāni kanyakānāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 32 ..
5.35.d:
अष्टम्यां च चतुर्दश्यां तेषु संपूज्य भक्तितः ..
योगिनीनां च वृन्दानि कन्यकानां विशेषतः .. 32 ..
5.35.m: And having worshipped with devotion on the eighth and fourteenth days upon them / the multitudes of yoginīs, and especially the young maidens,

5.35.s:
vidyāṃ viśoṣiṇīnāma samārādhayata dvijaḥ ..
pūjayitvā diśāṃ pālānkṣetrapālānapi dvijaḥ ..
ākāśacāriṇīṃ caiva devatāṃ śraddhayā dvijaḥ .. 33 ..
5.35.d:
विद्यां विशोषिणीनाम समाराधयत द्विजः ..
पूजयित्वा दिशां पालान्क्षेत्रपालानपि द्विजः ..
आकाशचारिणीं चैव देवतां श्रद्धया द्विजः .. 33 ..
5.35.m: the twice-born worshipped the vidyā named Viśoṣiṇī. / Having worshipped the guardians of the directions and the guardians of the field, / and with faith the goddess who moves through the sky, the twice-born [invoked her].

5.35.s:
tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte prasannā tasya devatā ..
provāca vada yatkṛtyaṃ siddhāhaṃ tava sanmune .. .. 34 ..
5.35.d:
ततः संवत्सरस्यांते प्रसन्ना तस्य देवता ..
प्रोवाच वद यत्कृत्यं सिद्धाहं तव सन्मुने .. .. 34 ..
5.35.m: Then at the end of the year the pleased goddess / said to him: "Speak what is to be done; I have been mastered by you, O good sage!"

5.35.s:
.. agastya uvāca .. ..
yadi devi prasannā me tadāsyaṃ viśa satvaram ..
yena saṃśoṣayāmyāśu samudraṃ devi vāgyataḥ .. 35 ..
5.35.d:
.. अगस्त्य उवाच .. ..
यदि देवि प्रसन्ना मे तदास्यं विश सत्वरम् ..
येन संशोषयाम्याशु समुद्रं देवि वाग्यतः .. 35 ..
5.35.m: Agastya said: / "If you are pleased with me, O goddess, enter my mouth swiftly, / so that by holding my speech I may quickly dry up the ocean, O goddess."

5.35.s:
sā tatheti pratijñāya praviṣṭā satvaraṃ mukhe ..
saṃśoṣaṇī mahāvidyā tasyarṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ .. 36 ..
5.35.d:
सा तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय प्रविष्टा सत्वरं मुखे ..
संशोषणी महाविद्या तस्यर्षेर्भावितात्मनः .. 36 ..
5.35.m: She assented with "So be it," and swiftly entered the mouth / of that sage of cultivated soul, [she] the great vidyā Saṃśoṣaṇī.

5.35.s:
etasminnaṃtare prāptāḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ ..
dhṛtāyudhakarā hṛṣṭāḥ saṃnaddhā yuddhahetave .. 37 ..
5.35.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्ताः सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ..
धृतायुधकरा हृष्टाः संनद्धा युद्धहेतवे .. 37 ..
5.35.m: In the meantime, all the gods arrived together with Indra, / weapons held in their hands, rejoicing, armed and ready for the purpose of battle.

5.35.s:
tataḥ saṃprasthito vipro devaiḥ sarvaiḥ samāhitaḥ ..
vārirāśiṃ samuddiśya saṃśuṣkavadanastadā .. 38 ..
5.35.d:
ततः संप्रस्थितो विप्रो देवैः सर्वैः समाहितः ..
वारिराशिं समुद्दिश्य संशुष्कवदनस्तदा .. 38 ..
5.35.m: Then the brahmin set forth, accompanied by all the gods, / heading towards the mass of waters, his face then completely parched.

5.35.s:
atha gatvā samudrāṃtaṃ stūyamāno divālayaiḥ ..
pipāsākulito'tīva sarvāndevānuvāca ha .. 39 ..
5.35.d:
अथ गत्वा समुद्रांतं स्तूयमानो दिवालयैः ..
पिपासाकुलितोऽतीव सर्वान्देवानुवाच ह .. 39 ..
5.35.m: Then, having gone to the edge of the ocean while being praised by the dwellers of heaven, / being exceedingly overcome by thirst, he spoke indeed to all the gods:

5.35.s:
eṣo'haṃ sāgaraṃ sadyaḥ śoṣayiṣyāmi sāṃpratam ..
yūyaṃ bhavata sodyogā vadhāya suravidviṣām .. 6.35.40 ..
5.35.d:
एषोऽहं सागरं सद्यः शोषयिष्यामि सांप्रतम् ..
यूयं भवत सोद्योगा वधाय सुरविद्विषाम् .. 6.35.40 ..
5.35.m: "Here, I will immediately dry up the ocean right now. / You must be ready with effort for the slaughter of the enemies of the gods."

5.35.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamuktvā muniḥ so'tha matsyakacchapasaṃkulam..
helayā prapapau kṛtsnaṃ grāhaiḥ kīrṇaṃ mahārṇavam .. 41 ..
5.35.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा मुनिः सोऽथ मत्स्यकच्छपसंकुलम्..
हेलया प्रपपौ कृत्स्नं ग्राहैः कीर्णं महार्णवम् .. 41 ..
5.35.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, that sage then, with ease, completely drank / the great ocean, crowded with fish and turtles and strewn with sea-monsters.

5.35.s:
tataḥ sthalopame jāte te daityāḥ surasattamaiḥ ..
vadhyante niśitairbāṇaiḥ samantādvijigīṣubhiḥ .. 42 ..
5.35.d:
ततः स्थलोपमे जाते ते दैत्याः सुरसत्तमैः ..
वध्यन्ते निशितैर्बाणैः समन्ताद्विजिगीषुभिः .. 42 ..
5.35.m: Then, when it had become like dry land, those Daityas were slain / by the excellent gods with sharp arrows on all sides, wishing for victory.

5.35.s:
atha kṛtvā mahadyuddhaṃ yathā śaktyātidāruṇam ..
hatabhūyiṣṭhaśeṣā ye bhittvā bhūmiṃ gatā adhaḥ..43..
5.35.d:
अथ कृत्वा महद्युद्धं यथा शक्त्यातिदारुणम् ..
हतभूयिष्ठशेषा ये भित्त्वा भूमिं गता अधः..43..
5.35.m: Then, having fought a great and exceedingly terrible battle according to their strength, / those who remained after most were killed split the earth and went below.

5.35.s:
tataḥ procuḥ surāḥ sarve stutvā taṃ munisattamam ..
parityaja jalaṃ bhūyaḥ pūraṇārthaṃ mahodadheḥ .. 44 ..
5.35.d:
ततः प्रोचुः सुराः सर्वे स्तुत्वा तं मुनिसत्तमम् ..
परित्यज जलं भूयः पूरणार्थं महोदधेः .. 44 ..
5.35.m: Then all the gods, having praised that best of sages, said: / "Discharge the water once more for the sake of refilling the great ocean.

5.35.s:
naiṣā vasumatī vipra samudreṇa vinākṛtā ..
rājate vastusaṃtyaktā yathā nārī vibhūṣitā .. 45 ..
5.35.d:
नैषा वसुमती विप्र समुद्रेण विनाकृता ..
राजते वस्तुसंत्यक्ता यथा नारी विभूषिता .. 45 ..
5.35.m: Deprived of the ocean, O brahmin, this earth / does not look splendid, just as an adorned woman devoid of clothing [does not look splendid]."

5.35.s:
.. agastya uvāca .. ...
yā mayā''rādhitā vidyā varṣaṃyāvatpraśoṣaṇī ..
tayā pītamidaṃ toyaṃ pariṇāmagataṃ tathā .. 46 ..
5.35.d:
.. अगस्त्य उवाच .. ...
या मया'ऽराधिता विद्या वर्षंयावत्प्रशोषणी ..
तया पीतमिदं तोयं परिणामगतं तथा .. 46 ..
5.35.m: Agastya said: / "The desiccating vidyā which was worshipped by me for the course of a year, / by her this water was drunk, and it has also been digested.

5.35.s:
eṣa yāsyati vai pūrtiṃ bhūyo'pi varuṇālayaḥ ..
khātaścāgādhatāṃ prāpto gaṃgātoyaiḥ sunirmalaiḥ .. 47 ..
5.35.d:
एष यास्यति वै पूर्तिं भूयोऽपि वरुणालयः ..
खातश्चागाधतां प्राप्तो गंगातोयैः सुनिर्मलैः .. 47 ..
5.35.m: This abode of Varuṇa will indeed attain fullness once again; / dug out and having reached bottomlessness, [it will be filled] by the pure waters of the Gaṅgā.

5.35.s:
sagaronāma bhūpālo bhaviṣyati mahītale ..
tatputrāḥ ṣaṣṭisāhasrāḥ khaniṣyaṃti na saṃśayaḥ .. 48 ..
5.35.d:
सगरोनाम भूपालो भविष्यति महीतले ..
तत्पुत्राः षष्टिसाहस्राः खनिष्यंति न संशयः .. 48 ..
5.35.m: There will be a king named Sagara upon the surface of the earth. / His sixty thousand sons will dig it out; there is no doubt.

5.35.s:
tasyaivānvayavānrājā bhaviṣyati bhagīrathaḥ ..
sa jñātikāraṇādgaṃgāṃ brahmāṃḍādānayiṣyati .. 49 ..
5.35.d:
तस्यैवान्वयवान्राजा भविष्यति भगीरथः ..
स ज्ञातिकारणाद्गंगां ब्रह्मांडादानयिष्यति .. 49 ..
5.35.m: Belonging to his very lineage, there will be a king named Bhagīratha. / For the sake of his kinsmen, he will bring the Gaṅgā from the cosmic egg.

5.35.s:
pravāheṇa tatastasyāḥ samaṃtādaṃbhasāṃnidhiḥ ..
bhaviṣyati susaṃpūrṇaḥ satyametanmayoditam .. 6.35.50 ..
5.35.d:
प्रवाहेण ततस्तस्याः समंतादंभसांनिधिः ..
भविष्यति सुसंपूर्णः सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् .. 6.35.50 ..
5.35.m: Then, by her flow on all sides, the ocean / will become fully filled; this that I have spoken is true."

5.35.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
devakṛtyaṃ muniśreṣṭha bhavatā hyupapāditam ..
tasmātprārthaya cittasthaṃ varaṃ sarvaṃ munīśvara .. 51 ..
5.35.d:
.. देवा ऊचुः .. ..
देवकृत्यं मुनिश्रेष्ठ भवता ह्युपपादितम् ..
तस्मात्प्रार्थय चित्तस्थं वरं सर्वं मुनीश्वर .. 51 ..
5.35.m: The gods said: / "The task of the gods has indeed been accomplished by you, O best of sages! / Therefore ask, O lord of sages, every boon that resides in your mind."

5.35.s:
.. agastya uvāca .. ..
camatkārapure kṣetre mayā pīṭhānyaśeṣataḥ ..
ānītāni prabhāvena maṃtrāṇāṃ surasattamāḥ .. 52 ..
5.35.d:
.. अगस्त्य उवाच .. ..
चमत्कारपुरे क्षेत्रे मया पीठान्यशेषतः ..
आनीतानि प्रभावेन मंत्राणां सुरसत्तमाः .. 52 ..
5.35.m: Agastya said: / "In the sacred field of Camatkārapura all the sacred seats without remainder / have been brought by me by the power of mantras, O best of gods.

5.35.s:
tasmātteṣāṃ sadā vāsastatraivāstu prabhāvataḥ ..
sarvāsāṃ yoginīnāṃ ca mātṝṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .. 53 ..
5.35.d:
तस्मात्तेषां सदा वासस्तत्रैवास्तु प्रभावतः ..
सर्वासां योगिनीनां च मातॄणां च विशेषतः .. 53 ..
5.35.m: Therefore, by [your] power, let their dwelling be always right there, / and [the dwelling] of all the yoginīs, and especially of the Mothers.

5.35.s:
aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ tāni yaḥ śraddhayā'nvitaḥ ..
pūjayiṣyati tasya syātsamastaṃ manasepsitam .. 54 ..
5.35.d:
अष्टम्यां च चतुर्दश्यां तानि यः श्रद्धयाऽन्वितः ..
पूजयिष्यति तस्य स्यात्समस्तं मनसेप्सितम् .. 54 ..
5.35.m: And whoever, endowed with faith, worships them on the eighth and fourteenth days, / all that is desired in his mind shall come to be."

5.35.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
yasmāccitrāṇi pīṭhāni tvayānītāni tatra hi ..
tasmāccitreśvaraṃ nāma pīṭhamekaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 55 ..
5.35.d:
.. देवा ऊचुः .. ..
यस्माच्चित्राणि पीठानि त्वयानीतानि तत्र हि ..
तस्माच्चित्रेश्वरं नाम पीठमेकं भविष्यति .. 55 ..
5.35.m: The gods said: / "Since diverse sacred seats were brought there by you, / therefore there shall be one sacred seat named Citreśvara.

5.35.s:
yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya tatra pūjāṃ kariṣyati ..
yoginīnāṃ ca vidyānāṃ mātṝṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .. 56 ..
5.35.d:
यो यं काममभिध्याय तत्र पूजां करिष्यति ..
योगिनीनां च विद्यानां मातॄणां च विशेषतः .. 56 ..
5.35.m: Whichever desire a person meditates upon and performs worship there, / of the yoginīs, the vidyās, and especially of the Mothers,

5.35.s:
taṃtaṃ kāmaṃ naraḥ śīghraṃ saṃprāpsyati mahāmune ..
asmākaṃ varadānena yadyapi syātsupāpakṛt.. 57 ..
5.35.d:
तंतं कामं नरः शीघ्रं संप्राप्स्यति महामुने ..
अस्माकं वरदानेन यद्यपि स्यात्सुपापकृत्.. 57 ..
5.35.m: that very desire the mortal shall quickly obtain, O great sage, / by the granting of our boon, even if he were a great doer of evil."

5.35.s:
evamuktvā surāḥ sarve tamāmantrya munīśvaram ..
gatāstriviṣṭapaṃ hṛṣṭāḥ so'pyagastyaḥ svamāśramam .. 58 ..
5.35.d:
एवमुक्त्वा सुराः सर्वे तमामन्त्र्य मुनीश्वरम् ..
गतास्त्रिविष्टपं हृष्टाः सोऽप्यगस्त्यः स्वमाश्रमम् .. 58 ..
5.35.m: Having spoken thus, all the gods, having bidden farewell to that lord of sages, / went joyfully to heaven; and Agastya too [went] to his own hermitage.

5.35.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yathā sa payasāṃnidhiḥ ..
agastyena purā pīto devakāryaprasiddhaye .. 59 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye'gastyakṛtasamudra prāśanavṛttāṃte'gastyāhūtapīṭhasamūhasya devaiścitreśvarapīṭhanāmapūrvakavarapradānavarṇanaṃnāma pañcatriṃśattamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 35 .. ..9..
5.35.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं यथा स पयसांनिधिः ..
अगस्त्येन पुरा पीतो देवकार्यप्रसिद्धये .. 59 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्येऽगस्त्यकृतसमुद्र प्राशनवृत्तांतेऽगस्त्याहूतपीठसमूहस्य देवैश्चित्रेश्वरपीठनामपूर्वकवरप्रदानवर्णनंनाम पञ्चत्रिंशत्तमोऽध्यायः .. 35 .. ..9..
5.35.m:
Sūta said: / All this has been narrated to you: how that ocean / was drunk of old by Agastya for the accomplishment of the purpose of the gods.
Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Granting of the Boon Named the Sacred Seat of Citreśvara by the Gods to the Assemblage of Sacred Seats Summoned by Agastya, in the Narrative of the Drinking of the Ocean by Agastya', in the Māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvarakṣetra, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection in the glorious Skandapurāṇa.

5.36.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
citreśvaramidaṃ pīṭhamagastyamuninirmitam ..
yatpramāṇaṃ yatprabhāvaṃ tadasmākaṃ prakīrtaya .. 1 ..
5.36.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
चित्रेश्वरमिदं पीठमगस्त्यमुनिनिर्मितम् ..
यत्प्रमाणं यत्प्रभावं तदस्माकं प्रकीर्तय .. 1 ..
5.36.m: The seers said: / "This sacred seat of Citreśvara was created by the sage Agastya. / Proclaim to us its extent and its power!"

5.36.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tasya pīṭhasya māhātmyaṃ vaktuṃ no śakyate dvijāḥ ..
sahasreṇāpi varṣāṇāṃ mukhānāmayutairapi .. 2 ..
5.36.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तस्य पीठस्य माहात्म्यं वक्तुं नो शक्यते द्विजाः ..
सहस्रेणापि वर्षाणां मुखानामयुतैरपि .. 2 ..
5.36.m: Sūta said: / "The māhātmya of that sacred seat cannot be spoken, O twice-born ones, / even in a thousand years, or even with tens of thousands of mouths.

5.36.s:
tatra siddhimanuprāptāḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
anudhyānasamāyuktā yoginaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ .. 3 ..
5.36.d:
तत्र सिद्धिमनुप्राप्ताः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ..
अनुध्यानसमायुक्ता योगिनः शंसितव्रताः .. 3 ..
5.36.m: There yogins of praised vows, absorbed in deep meditation, / have attained perfection by hundreds and by thousands.

5.36.s:
anyapīṭheṣu yā siddhirvarṣānuṣṭhānato bhavet ..
dinenaikena tāṃ siddhiṃ labhaṃte yogino dhruvam .. 4 ..
5.36.d:
अन्यपीठेषु या सिद्धिर्वर्षानुष्ठानतो भवेत् ..
दिनेनैकेन तां सिद्धिं लभंते योगिनो ध्रुवम् .. 4 ..
5.36.m: Whatever perfection might arise in other sacred seats from a year of ritual practice, / that perfection yogins certainly obtain there in a single day.

5.36.s:
yastatrātha rvaṇānmaṃtrāñjapecchraddhāsamanvitaḥ ..
teṣāmarthodbhavaṃ kṛtsnaṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti sa dhruvam .. 5 ..
5.36.d:
यस्तत्राथ र्वणान्मंत्राञ्जपेच्छ्रद्धासमन्वितः ..
तेषामर्थोद्भवं कृत्स्नं फलं प्राप्नोति स ध्रुवम् .. 5 ..
5.36.m: Whoever recites the Ātharvaṇa mantras there, endowed with faith, / he certainly obtains the entire fruit born of their purpose.

5.36.s:
putrakāmo narastatra puṃliṃgānyo japennaraḥ ..
sa labhetepsitānputrānyadyapi syājjarānvitaḥ .. 6 ..
5.36.d:
पुत्रकामो नरस्तत्र पुंलिंगान्यो जपेन्नरः ..
स लभेतेप्सितान्पुत्रान्यद्यपि स्याज्जरान्वितः .. 6 ..
5.36.m: A man desiring a son who recites the masculine names there, / he would obtain desired sons, even if he were advanced in old age.

5.36.s:
garbhopaniṣadaṃ tatra putrakāmo japennaraḥ ..
api vandhyāprasaṃgena syātsa putrasamanvitaḥ .. 7 ..
5.36.d:
गर्भोपनिषदं तत्र पुत्रकामो जपेन्नरः ..
अपि वन्ध्याप्रसंगेन स्यात्स पुत्रसमन्वितः .. 7 ..
5.36.m: A man desiring a son who recites the Garbha Upaniṣad there, / even through union with a barren woman he would be endowed with a son."

5.36.s:
śatrulokavināśāya yo japecchatarudriyam ..
tasminpīṭhe'rayastasya sadyo gacchaṃti saṃkṣayam 0. 8 ..
5.36.d:
शत्रुलोकविनाशाय यो जपेच्छतरुद्रियम् ..
तस्मिन्पीठेऽरयस्तस्य सद्यो गच्छंति संक्षयम् 0. 8 ..
5.36.m: A person who recites the Śatarudrīya for the destruction of enemies / at that seat sees his foes immediately perish. (8)

5.36.s:
bhūtapretapiśācādirakṣārthaṃ tatra mānavaḥ ..
yo japedvāmadevyaṃ ca sa syāddhi nirupadravaḥ .. 9 ..
5.36.d:
भूतप्रेतपिशाचादिरक्षार्थं तत्र मानवः ..
यो जपेद्वामदेव्यं च स स्याद्धि निरुपद्रवः .. 9 ..
5.36.m: For protection from spirits, ghosts, piśācas, and the like, a man there / who recites the Vāmadevya [hymn] indeed becomes free from affliction. (9)

5.36.s:
ko'dāditi narastatra kanyārthaṃ yo japedṛcam ..
yāṃ kanyāṃ dhyāyamānastu sa tāṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 6.36.10 ..
5.36.d:
कोऽदादिति नरस्तत्र कन्यार्थं यो जपेदृचम् ..
यां कन्यां ध्यायमानस्तु स तां प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् .. 6.36.10 ..
5.36.m: A man there who recites the verse ‘Who gave?’ (ko 'dāt) desiring a maiden, / attains without a doubt that maiden upon whom he meditates. (10)

5.36.s:
yo bhūpālaprasādārthamimaṃ devā niśaṃ japet ..
nirargalaḥ prasādaḥ syāttasya pārthivasaṃbhavaḥ .. 11 ..
5.36.d:
यो भूपालप्रसादार्थमिमं देवा निशं जपेत् ..
निरर्गलः प्रसादः स्यात्तस्य पार्थिवसंभवः .. 11 ..
5.36.m: He who recites ‘These gods’ (imaṃ devāḥ) day and night to win the favor of a king / attains unhindered favor issuing from that monarch. (11)

5.36.s:
svastrīsnehakṛteyastu taṃ patnībhiriti dvijāḥ ...
japedbhāryā bhavetsādhvī tasya sā snehavatsalā .. 12 ..
5.36.d:
स्वस्त्रीस्नेहकृतेयस्तु तं पत्नीभिरिति द्विजाः ...
जपेद्भार्या भवेत्साध्वी तस्य सा स्नेहवत्सला .. 12 ..
5.36.m: He who recites ‘Together with the wives’ (taṃ patnībhiḥ), O brahmins, to secure his wife's affection / finds that his wife becomes virtuous, devoted, and loving. (12)

5.36.s:
yo lokānugrahārthāya japedaditirityapi ..
tasya lokānurāgaḥ syātsalābhaśca viśeṣataḥ .. .. 13 ..
5.36.d:
यो लोकानुग्रहार्थाय जपेददितिरित्यपि ..
तस्य लोकानुरागः स्यात्सलाभश्च विशेषतः .. .. 13 ..
5.36.m: He who recites ‘Aditi’ (aditiḥ) to win the favor of people / secures the affection of the world and especially profit. (13)

5.36.s:
vittārthī yo japettatra śrīsūktaṃ manujo dvijāḥ ..
sarvatastasya vittāni samāgacchaṃtyanekaśaḥ .. 14 .
bhūmīti yo japetsāma bhūmyarthaṃ tatra mānavaḥ ..
sa bhavedbhūpatirnūnaṃ nīcajātirapi dhruvam ...5..
5.36.d:
वित्तार्थी यो जपेत्तत्र श्रीसूक्तं मनुजो द्विजाः ..
सर्वतस्तस्य वित्तानि समागच्छंत्यनेकशः .. 14 .
भूमीति यो जपेत्साम भूम्यर्थं तत्र मानवः ..
स भवेद्भूपतिर्नूनं नीचजातिरपि ध्रुवम् ...5..
5.36.m:
A man seeking wealth who recites the Śrīsūkta there, O brahmins, / receives wealth from every quarter in many ways. (14)
A man who recites the Sāman ‘Earth’ (bhūmi) there for the sake of land / truly becomes a ruler of the earth, even if born of low caste, without fail. (15)

5.36.s:
japedrathaṃtaraṃ sāma yānārthaṃ tatra yo naraḥ ..
sa prāpnoti hi yānāni śīghragāni śubhāni ca .. 16 ..
5.36.d:
जपेद्रथंतरं साम यानार्थं तत्र यो नरः ..
स प्राप्नोति हि यानानि शीघ्रगानि शुभानि च .. 16 ..
5.36.m: A man there who recites the Rathaṃtara Sāman for the sake of vehicles / indeed obtains fast and auspicious conveyances. (16)

5.36.s:
gajārthī yo japettatra gaṇānāṃ dvijasattamāḥ ..
sa prāpnoti gajānmartyo madaplāvitabhūtalān .. 17 ..
5.36.d:
गजार्थी यो जपेत्तत्र गणानां द्विजसत्तमाः ..
स प्राप्नोति गजान्मर्त्यो मदप्लावितभूतलान् .. 17 ..
5.36.m: He who desires elephants and recites ‘Of the hosts’ (gaṇānām) there, O best of brahmins, / obtains elephants that flood the ground with rut. (17)

5.36.s:
na tadrakṣeti yo mantraṃ japedra kṣākṛte naraḥ ..
tasya syātsarvato rakṣā sameṣu viṣameṣu ca .. 18 ..
5.36.d:
न तद्रक्षेति यो मन्त्रं जपेद्र क्षाकृते नरः ..
तस्य स्यात्सर्वतो रक्षा समेषु विषमेषु च .. 18 ..
5.36.m: A man who recites the mantra ‘Not that protection’ (na tadrakṣā) for the sake of safety / enjoys protection from all sides, through level and rough ways. (18)

5.36.s:
saptarṣaya iti śreṣṭhāṃ yo japettu samāhitaḥ ..
ṛcaṃ rogavināśāya sa rogaiḥ pari mucyate .. 19 ..
5.36.d:
सप्तर्षय इति श्रेष्ठां यो जपेत्तु समाहितः ..
ऋचं रोगविनाशाय स रोगैः परि मुच्यते .. 19 ..
5.36.m: He who, composed in mind, recites the excellent verse / ‘The Seven Seers’ (saptarṣayaḥ) for the eradication of diseases is released from diseases. (19)

5.36.s:
yadubhī yo japettatra grahapīḍārdito janaḥ ..
sānukūlā grahāstasya prabhavaṃti na saṃśayaḥ .. 6.36.20 ..
5.36.d:
यदुभी यो जपेत्तत्र ग्रहपीडार्दितो जनः ..
सानुकूला ग्रहास्तस्य प्रभवंति न संशयः .. 6.36.20 ..
5.36.m: A person tormented by the affliction of planets who recites ‘By Yadū’ (yadubhīḥ) there / finds the planets becoming favorable to him, without a doubt. (20)

5.36.s:
bhūtapīḍārdito yaśca bṛhatsāma japennaraḥ ..
pitṛvajjāyate tasya sa bhūto'pyaṃtako'pi cet .. 21 ..
5.36.d:
भूतपीडार्दितो यश्च बृहत्साम जपेन्नरः ..
पितृवज्जायते तस्य स भूतोऽप्यंतकोऽपि चेत् .. 21 ..
5.36.m: And a man afflicted by spirit-possession who recites the Bṛhat Sāman / finds that spirit becoming like a father to him, even were it the God of Death. (21)

5.36.s:
yātrāsiddhikṛte yaśca japetsūktaṃ ca śākunam ..
tasya saṃsidhyate yātrā yadyapi syādakiṃcanaḥ .. 22 ..
5.36.d:
यात्रासिद्धिकृते यश्च जपेत्सूक्तं च शाकुनम् ..
तस्य संसिध्यते यात्रा यद्यपि स्यादकिंचनः .. 22 ..
5.36.m: And he who recites the Śākunam Sūkta for success on a journey / achieves success in his journey, even if he possesses nothing. (22)

5.36.s:
sarpanāśāya yastatra sārpasūktaṃ japennaraḥ ..
na tasya maṃdire sarpāḥ praviśaṃti kathaṃcana .. 23 ..
5.36.d:
सर्पनाशाय यस्तत्र सार्पसूक्तं जपेन्नरः ..
न तस्य मंदिरे सर्पाः प्रविशंति कथंचन .. 23 ..
5.36.m: A man who recites the hymn to serpents (Sārpasūkta) there for the destruction of snakes / finds snakes never entering his dwelling under any circumstance. (23)

5.36.s:
viṣanāśāya yastatra japecchra ddhāsamanvitaḥ ..
uttiṣṭheti viṣaṃ sadyastasya nāśaṃ prayāsyati .. 24 ..
5.36.d:
विषनाशाय यस्तत्र जपेच्छ्र द्धासमन्वितः ..
उत्तिष्ठेति विषं सद्यस्तस्य नाशं प्रयास्यति .. 24 ..
5.36.m: He who recites ‘Arise!’ (uttiṣṭha) there endowed with faith / to destroy poison immediately brings about the destruction of the venom. (24)

5.36.s:
sthāvarajagamaṃ vāpi kṛtrimaṃ yadi vā viṣam ..
tasya nāmnā viniryāti tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā .. 25 ..
5.36.d:
स्थावरजगमं वापि कृत्रिमं यदि वा विषम् ..
तस्य नाम्ना विनिर्याति तमः सूर्योदये यथा .. 25 ..
5.36.m: Be it vegetable, animal, or artificial poison, / it departs at its name, like darkness at sunrise. (25)

5.36.s:
vyāghrasāma japedyastu tatra śraddhāsamanvitaḥ ..
tasya vyāghrādayo vyālā jāyaṃte saumyacetasaḥ .. 26 ..
5.36.d:
व्याघ्रसाम जपेद्यस्तु तत्र श्रद्धासमन्वितः ..
तस्य व्याघ्रादयो व्याला जायंते सौम्यचेतसः .. 26 ..
5.36.m: He who recites the Vyāghrasāman there endowed with faith / finds tigers and other ferocious beasts becoming gentle-minded toward him. (26)

5.36.s:
kṛṣikarmaprasi ddhyarthaṃ yo japellāṃgalāni ca ..
vṛṣṭihīne'pi loke'sminkṛṣistasya prasidhyati .. 27 ..
5.36.d:
कृषिकर्मप्रसि द्ध्यर्थं यो जपेल्लांगलानि च ..
वृष्टिहीनेऽपि लोकेऽस्मिन्कृषिस्तस्य प्रसिध्यति .. 27 ..
5.36.m: He who recites ‘The plows’ (lāṅgalāni) for the success of agricultural work / finds his farming flourish, even in this world devoid of rain. (27)

5.36.s:
ītināśāya tatraiva japeddevavrataṃ naraḥ ..
tataḥ saṃkīrttanā deva ītayo yāṃti saṃkṣayam .. 28 ..
5.36.d:
ईतिनाशाय तत्रैव जपेद्देवव्रतं नरः ..
ततः संकीर्त्तना देव ईतयो यांति संक्षयम् .. 28 ..
5.36.m: A man should recite the Devavrata hymn right there for the elimination of calamities; / through that utterance alone, calamities come to an end. (28)

5.36.s:
anāvṛṣṭihate loke paṃceṃdraṃ tatra yo japet ..
tasya hastakṛte home tanmaṃtraiḥ syājjalāgamaḥ .. 29 ..
5.36.d:
अनावृष्टिहते लोके पंचेंद्रं तत्र यो जपेत् ..
तस्य हस्तकृते होमे तन्मंत्रैः स्याज्जलागमः .. 29 ..
5.36.m: When the world is stricken by drought, he who recites the Pañcendra hymn there / brings about the arrival of water through an oblation offered with his hands using those mantras. (29)

5.36.s:
daṃṣṭrābhyā miti yastatra naraścaurārditaḥ paṭhet ..
nopadravo bhavettasya kadāciccaurasaṃbhavaḥ .. 6.36.30 ..
5.36.d:
दंष्ट्राभ्या मिति यस्तत्र नरश्चौरार्दितः पठेत् ..
नोपद्रवो भवेत्तस्य कदाचिच्चौरसंभवः .. 6.36.30 ..
5.36.m: A man tormented by thieves who reads ‘By the two tusks’ (daṃṣṭrābhyām) there / never suffers any trouble arising from thieves. (30)

5.36.s:
vivādārthaṃ japedyastu saṃsṛṣṭamiti tatra ca ..
vivāde vijaya stasya pāpasyāpi prajāyate .. 31 ..
5.36.d:
विवादार्थं जपेद्यस्तु संसृष्टमिति तत्र च ..
विवादे विजय स्तस्य पापस्यापि प्रजायते .. 31 ..
5.36.m: And he who recites ‘Connected’ (saṃsṛṣṭam) there for the sake of a dispute / attains victory in the dispute, even if he be in the wrong. (31)

5.36.s:
yo ripūccāṭanārthāya naro rudraśiro japet ..
tasya te ripavo yāṃti deśaṃ tyaktvā kubuddhitaḥ .. 32 ..
5.36.d:
यो रिपूच्चाटनार्थाय नरो रुद्रशिरो जपेत् ..
तस्य ते रिपवो यांति देशं त्यक्त्वा कुबुद्धितः .. 32 ..
5.36.m: A man who recites the Rudraśiras hymn to drive away his enemies / finds his enemies leaving the region due to their corrupted intellects. (32)

5.36.s:
mohanāya ripūṇāṃ ca yo japedviṣṇusaṃhitām ..
tasya mohābhibhūtāste jāyaṃte ripavo dhruvam .. 33 ..
5.36.d:
मोहनाय रिपूणां च यो जपेद्विष्णुसंहिताम् ..
तस्य मोहाभिभूतास्ते जायंते रिपवो ध्रुवम् .. 33 ..
5.36.m: And he who recites the Viṣṇusaṃhitā to stupefy his enemies / sees those enemies become overcome by delusion, certainly. (33)

5.36.s:
vaśīkaraṇahetoryaḥ kūṣmāṃḍīḥ prajapennaraḥ ..
śatravo'pi vaśe tasya kiṃ punaḥ pramadādayaḥ .. 34 ..
5.36.d:
वशीकरणहेतोर्यः कूष्मांडीः प्रजपेन्नरः ..
शत्रवोऽपि वशे तस्य किं पुनः प्रमदादयः .. 34 ..
5.36.m: A man who recites the Kūṣmāṇḍa mantras for subjugation / brings even his enemies under control, not to mention women and others. (34)

5.36.s:
yaḥ staṃbhāya ripūṇāṃ vai prājāpatyaṃ ca vāruṇam ..
maṃtraṃ japeddvijaśreṣṭhāḥ samyakchraddhāparāyaṇaḥ ..
maṃtrasaṃstaṃbhitāstasya jāyaṃte sarvaśatravaḥ .. 35 ..
5.36.d:
यः स्तंभाय रिपूणां वै प्राजापत्यं च वारुणम् ..
मंत्रं जपेद्द्विजश्रेष्ठाः सम्यक्छ्रद्धापरायणः ..
मंत्रसंस्तंभितास्तस्य जायंते सर्वशत्रवः .. 35 ..
5.36.m: He who, devoted to right faith, O best of brahmins, recites the Prājāpatya and Vāruṇa mantras / for paralyzing his enemies / sees all his foes become paralyzed by the mantra. (35)

5.36.s:
japetkālī karālīti yaḥ śoṣāya naro dvijāḥ ..
sa śoṣayati tatkṛtsnaṃ yaccitte dhārayennaraḥ .. 36 ..
5.36.d:
जपेत्काली करालीति यः शोषाय नरो द्विजाः ..
स शोषयति तत्कृत्स्नं यच्चित्ते धारयेन्नरः .. 36 ..
5.36.m: A man who recites ‘Kālī, Karālī’, O brahmins, to dry up [something] / completely dries up whatever he holds in his mind. (36)

5.36.s:
eṣa maṃtrastadā japto hyagastyena mahātmanā..
yatprabhāvānnadīnāthastena saṃśoṣito dhruvam .. 37 ..
5.36.d:
एष मंत्रस्तदा जप्तो ह्यगस्त्येन महात्मना..
यत्प्रभावान्नदीनाथस्तेन संशोषितो ध्रुवम् .. 37 ..
5.36.m: This mantra was recited then by the great-souled Agastya, / by whose power the lord of rivers [the ocean] was certainly dried up by him. (37)

5.36.s:
etatprabhāvaṃ yatpīṭhaṃ maṃtrāṇāṃ siddhikārakam..
aihikānāṃ phalānāṃ ca tanmayā vaḥ prakīrtitam .. 38 ..
5.36.d:
एतत्प्रभावं यत्पीठं मंत्राणां सिद्धिकारकम्..
ऐहिकानां फलानां च तन्मया वः प्रकीर्तितम् .. 38 ..
5.36.m: The power of this seat which effects the accomplishment of mantras / and earthly fruits has thus been proclaimed by me to you. (38)

5.36.s:
yo vāṃchati punaḥ svargaṃ sa tatra dvijasattamāḥ ..
snānaṃ karotu dānaṃ ca śrāddhaṃ cāpi viśeṣataḥ .. 39 ..
5.36.d:
यो वांछति पुनः स्वर्गं स तत्र द्विजसत्तमाः ..
स्नानं करोतु दानं च श्राद्धं चापि विशेषतः .. 39 ..
5.36.m: Moreover, he who desires heaven, O best of brahmins, / should perform ritual ablution, charitable gifts, and especially ancestral rites (śrāddha) there. (39)

5.36.s:
atha vāṃchati yo mokṣaṃ virakto bhavasāgarāt ..
niṣkāmastatra saṃtuṣṭastapastapyetsubuddhimān .. 6.36.40 ..
5.36.d:
अथ वांछति यो मोक्षं विरक्तो भवसागरात् ..
निष्कामस्तत्र संतुष्टस्तपस्तप्येत्सुबुद्धिमान् .. 6.36.40 ..
5.36.m: Or, if someone desires liberation, having grown detached from the ocean of worldly existence, / let that wise person, desireless and contented, practice austerity there. (40)

5.36.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
maṃtrajāpyasya māhātmyaṃ yattvayā naḥ prakīrtitam..
tatkathaṃ siddhimāyāti maṃtrajāpyaṃ hi sūtaja .. 41 ..
5.36.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
मंत्रजाप्यस्य माहात्म्यं यत्त्वया नः प्रकीर्तितम्..
तत्कथं सिद्धिमायाति मंत्रजाप्यं हि सूतज .. 41 ..
5.36.m: The seers said: / The māhātmya of mantra recitation that has been proclaimed by you to us— / how does that mantra recitation attain perfection, O son of Sūta? (41)

5.36.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atra tatkathayiṣyāmi yanmayā pitṛtaḥ śrutam ..
vadato brāhmaṇeṃdrasya purā durvāsaso muneḥ .. 42 ..
5.36.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अत्र तत्कथयिष्यामि यन्मया पितृतः श्रुतम् ..
वदतो ब्राह्मणेंद्रस्य पुरा दुर्वाससो मुनेः .. 42 ..
5.36.m: Sūta said: / Here I shall relate that which was heard by me from my father, / as it was spoken in ancient times by the eminent brahmin, the sage Durvāsas. (42)

5.36.s:
tena pūrvaṃ pitā'smākaṃ pṛṣṭo durvāsasā dvijāḥ ..
maṃtravādakṛte yacca śṛṇudhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ .. 43 .. ..
5.36.d:
तेन पूर्वं पिताऽस्माकं पृष्टो दुर्वाससा द्विजाः ..
मंत्रवादकृते यच्च शृणुध्वं सुसमाहिताः .. 43 .. ..
5.36.m: Formerly, our father was questioned by that Durvāsas, O brahmins, / regarding the practice of mantras; listen with attentive minds: (43)

5.36.s:
.. durvāsā uvāca .. ..
sādhayiṣyāmyahaṃ mantramabhīṣṭaṃ kamapi vratī ..
tasya siddhikṛte brūhi vidhānaṃ śāstrasaṃbhavam .. 44 ..
5.36.d:
.. दुर्वासा उवाच .. ..
साधयिष्याम्यहं मन्त्रमभीष्टं कमपि व्रती ..
तस्य सिद्धिकृते ब्रूहि विधानं शास्त्रसंभवम् .. 44 ..
5.36.m: Durvāsas said: / Observing vows, I wish to master a certain desired mantra. / Tell me the procedure derived from the scriptures for its accomplishment. (44)

5.36.s:
.. lomaharṣaṇa uvāca .. ..
maṃtrāṇāṃ sādhanaṃ kaṣṭaṃ sarveṣāmapi sanmune ..
pratyavāyasamopetaṃ bahucchidrasamākulam..45..
5.36.d:
.. लोमहर्षण उवाच .. ..
मंत्राणां साधनं कष्टं सर्वेषामपि सन्मुने ..
प्रत्यवायसमोपेतं बहुच्छिद्रसमाकुलम्..45..
5.36.m: Romaharṣaṇa said: / The accomplishment of all mantras is difficult, O noble sage; / it is accompanied by transgressions and full of many flaws. (45)

5.36.s:
tasmānmaṃtrakṛte siddhiṃ yadi tvaṃ vāṃchasi dvija..
camatkārapure kṣetre tatra tvaṃ gaṃtumarhasi .. 46 ..
5.36.d:
तस्मान्मंत्रकृते सिद्धिं यदि त्वं वांछसि द्विज..
चमत्कारपुरे क्षेत्रे तत्र त्वं गंतुमर्हसि .. 46 ..
5.36.m: Therefore, if you desire accomplishment through mantra, O brahmin, / you ought to go to that sacred field in Camatkārapura. (46)

5.36.s:
tatra citreśvarīpīṭhamagastyena vinirmitam ..
sadyaḥ siddhikaraṃ proktaṃ mantrāṇāṃ hṛdi vartinām ..47 ..
5.36.d:
तत्र चित्रेश्वरीपीठमगस्त्येन विनिर्मितम् ..
सद्यः सिद्धिकरं प्रोक्तं मन्त्राणां हृदि वर्तिनाम् ..47 ..
5.36.m: There is the Citreśvarī seat established by Agastya, / said to instantly grant the accomplishment of mantras held in one's heart. (47)

5.36.s:
na tatra jāyate chidraṃ pratyavāyo na ca dvija ..
nāsiddhirvaradānena sarveṣāṃ tridivaukasām .. 48 ..
5.36.d:
न तत्र जायते छिद्रं प्रत्यवायो न च द्विज ..
नासिद्धिर्वरदानेन सर्वेषां त्रिदिवौकसाम् .. 48 ..
5.36.m: There no defect arises, nor any transgression, O brahmin, / nor failure, due to the boon granted by all the denizens of heaven. (48)

5.36.s:
cāturyuṃgyaṃ hi tatpīṭhaṃ sthitānāṃ siddhimāha ret ..
yugānurūpataḥ sadyastato vakṣyāmyahaṃ dvija .. 49 ..
5.36.d:
चातुर्युंग्यं हि तत्पीठं स्थितानां सिद्धिमाह रेत् ..
युगानुरूपतः सद्यस्ततो वक्ष्याम्यहं द्विज .. 49 ..
5.36.m: For that seat bestows accomplishment across the four ages / immediately upon those residing there, according to the age; therefore I shall explain, O brahmin. (49)

5.36.s:
yo yaṃ sādhayituṃ mantramicchati dvijasattama ..
sa tasya pūrvamevātha lakṣamekaṃ japennaraḥ .. .. 6.36.50 ..
5.36.d:
यो यं साधयितुं मन्त्रमिच्छति द्विजसत्तम ..
स तस्य पूर्वमेवाथ लक्षमेकं जपेन्नरः .. .. 6.36.50 ..
5.36.m: Whichever mantra a person wishes to master, O best of brahmins, / that man should first recite it one hundred thousand times.

5.36.s:
tato bhavati saṃsiddho maṃtrārhaḥ sa naraḥ śuciḥ ..
japedbrāhmaṇaśārdūla tato lakṣacatuṣṭayam ..
daśāṃśena tu homaḥ syātsusamiddhe hutāśane .. .. 51 ..
5.36.d:
ततो भवति संसिद्धो मंत्रार्हः स नरः शुचिः ..
जपेद्ब्राह्मणशार्दूल ततो लक्षचतुष्टयम् ..
दशांशेन तु होमः स्यात्सुसमिद्धे हुताशने .. .. 51 ..
5.36.m: Then, purified, that man becomes accomplished and worthy of the mantra. / Then he should recite it four hundred thousand times, O tiger among brahmins; / and one-tenth of that should be an oblation offered into a well-kindled fire.

5.36.s:
tatastu jāyate siddhirnūnaṃ tanmaṃtrasaṃbhavā ..
tatra saumyeṣu kṛtyeṣu homaḥ siddhārthakaiḥ sitaiḥ .. 52 ..
jātīpuṣpaiśca viprendra smṛto brāhmaṇa bhojanaiḥ ..
tathā raudreṣu kṛtyeṣu raktapuṣpaiḥ saguggulaiḥ 0..
5.36.d:
ततस्तु जायते सिद्धिर्नूनं तन्मंत्रसंभवा ..
तत्र सौम्येषु कृत्येषु होमः सिद्धार्थकैः सितैः .. 52 ..
जातीपुष्पैश्च विप्रेन्द्र स्मृतो ब्राह्मण भोजनैः ..
तथा रौद्रेषु कृत्येषु रक्तपुष्पैः सगुग्गुलैः 0..
5.36.m:
Thereupon, accomplishment certainly arises from that mantra. / In benevolent rites, the oblation is performed there with white mustard seeds
and jasmine flowers, O best of brahmins, and is accompanied by feeding brahmins; / likewise, in fierce rites, with red flowers and bdellium,

5.36.s: tarpaṇaiḥ kanyakānāṃ ca homaḥ syātsa phalapradaḥ .. 53 ..
5.36.d: तर्पणैः कन्यकानां च होमः स्यात्स फलप्रदः .. 53 ..
5.36.m: and with satisfactions offered to young maidens; such an oblation yields results.

5.36.s:
etatkṛtayuge proktaṃ maṃtrasādhanamutta mam ..
sarveṣāṃ sādhakānāṃ ca mayā proktaṃ dvijottama .. 54 ..
5.36.d:
एतत्कृतयुगे प्रोक्तं मंत्रसाधनमुत्त मम् ..
सर्वेषां साधकानां च मया प्रोक्तं द्विजोत्तम .. 54 ..
5.36.m: This excellent method of mastering mantras was proclaimed for the Kṛta age; / it has been spoken by me for all practitioners, O best of brahmins.

5.36.s:
etattretāyuge proktaṃ pādonaṃ mantrasādhanam ..
yugmārdhaṃ dvāpare kāryaṃ caturthāṃśaṃ kalau yuge .. 55 ..
5.36.d:
एतत्त्रेतायुगे प्रोक्तं पादोनं मन्त्रसाधनम् ..
युग्मार्धं द्वापरे कार्यं चतुर्थांशं कलौ युगे .. 55 ..
5.36.m: In the Tretā age, this mastery of mantras is said to be reduced by one-quarter; / half of the pair is to be done in the Dvāpara age, and one-quarter in the Kali age.

5.36.s:
evaṃ tatra samāsādya siddhiṃ maṃtrasamudbhavām ..
tatra pīṭhe tataḥ kṛtyaṃ sādhayetsvecchayā naraḥ .. 56 ..
5.36.d:
एवं तत्र समासाद्य सिद्धिं मंत्रसमुद्भवाम् ..
तत्र पीठे ततः कृत्यं साधयेत्स्वेच्छया नरः .. 56 ..
5.36.m: Thus having attained there the perfection born of the mantra / at that sacred seat, a person may then accomplish his objective at will.

5.36.s:
śāpānugrahasāmarthyasaṃyutasteja sā'nvitaḥ ..
ajeyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sādhūnāṃ saṃmatastathā .. 57 ..
5.36.d:
शापानुग्रहसामर्थ्यसंयुतस्तेज साऽन्वितः ..
अजेयः सर्वभूतानां साधूनां संमतस्तथा .. 57 ..
5.36.m: Endowed with the capacity to curse or bestow boons, possessed of fiery power, / he becomes unassailable by any creature, and esteemed by virtuous people.

5.36.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tacchrutvā sa munistasya piturmama vaco'khilam ..
tataścitreśvaraṃ pīṭhaṃ samāyāto'tha sanmuniḥ .. 58 ..
5.36.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा स मुनिस्तस्य पितुर्मम वचोऽखिलम् ..
ततश्चित्रेश्वरं पीठं समायातोऽथ सन्मुनिः .. 58 ..
5.36.m: Sūta said: / Having heard all that advice of his father, that sage, / that true sage, then arrived at the seat of Citreśvara.

5.36.s:
tatra saṃsādhayāmāsa sarvānmaṃtrānyathākramam ..
vidhinā śāstradṛṣṭena śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ.. 59 ..
5.36.d:
तत्र संसाधयामास सर्वान्मंत्रान्यथाक्रमम् ..
विधिना शास्त्रदृष्टेन श्रद्धया परया युतः.. 59 ..
5.36.m: There he mastered all the mantras in proper order, / according to the injunction seen in the scriptures, endowed with supreme faith.

5.36.s:
iti saṃsiddhamaṃtraḥ sa camatkārapuraṃ gataḥ ..
viprāṇāṃ prārthanārthāya bhūmikhaṃḍakṛte dvijāḥ .. 6.36.60 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahapurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṃḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye citreśvarīpīṭhamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma ṣaṭtriṃśattamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 36 ..
5.36.d:
इति संसिद्धमंत्रः स चमत्कारपुरं गतः ..
विप्राणां प्रार्थनार्थाय भूमिखंडकृते द्विजाः .. 6.36.60 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महपुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखंडे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये चित्रेश्वरीपीठमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम षट्त्रिंशत्तमोऽध्यायः .. 36 ..
5.36.m:
Thus, having mastered the mantras, he went to Camatkārapura / in order to petition the brahmins for a piece of land, O brahmins.
Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of the Sacred Seat of Citreśvarī', in the Glory of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the sixth section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.37.s:
.. sūta uvāca ..
athāpaśyatsa viprāṇāṃ vṛndaṃ vṛndārakopamam..
saṃniviṣṭaṃ dharāpṛṣṭhe līlābhāji dvijottamāḥ.....
eke vedavidastatra vedavyākhyānatatparāḥ..
parasparaṃ susaṃkruddhā vivadaṃti jigīṣavaḥ .. 2 ..
5.37.d:
.. सूत उवाच ..
अथापश्यत्स विप्राणां वृन्दं वृन्दारकोपमम्..
संनिविष्टं धरापृष्ठे लीलाभाजि द्विजोत्तमाः.....
एके वेदविदस्तत्र वेदव्याख्यानतत्पराः..
परस्परं सुसंक्रुद्धा विवदंति जिगीषवः .. 2 ..
5.37.m: Sūta said: / Then he saw an assembly of brahmins resembling the gods, / seated on the ground full of charm, O best of brahmins: / some, knowers of the Veda, intent on expounding the Veda, / were intensely angry with one another, disputing in their desire for victory;

5.37.s:
yajñavidyāvido'nye'pi yajñākhyānaparāyaṇāḥ ..
tatra viprāḥ pradṛśyaṃte śataśo brahmavādinaḥ .. 3 ..
5.37.d:
यज्ञविद्याविदोऽन्येऽपि यज्ञाख्यानपरायणाः ..
तत्र विप्राः प्रदृश्यंते शतशो ब्रह्मवादिनः .. 3 ..
5.37.m: others, knowers of sacrificial lore, were dedicated to explaining sacrifices; / there brahmins speaking on Brahman were seen by the hundreds;

5.37.s:
anye brāhmaṇaśārdūlā vedāṃgeṣu vicakṣaṇāḥ ..
pravadaṃti ca saṃdehānvṛndānāmagrataḥ sthitāḥ .. 4 ..
5.37.d:
अन्ये ब्राह्मणशार्दूला वेदांगेषु विचक्षणाः ..
प्रवदंति च संदेहान्वृन्दानामग्रतः स्थिताः .. 4 ..
5.37.m: other tigers among brahmins, skilled in the Vedāṅgas, / standing before assemblies, were expressing their doubts;

5.37.s:
vedābhyāsaparāścānye tāranādena sarvaśaḥ ..
nādayaṃto diśāṃ cakraṃ tatra samyagdvijottamāḥ .. 5 ..
5.37.d:
वेदाभ्यासपराश्चान्ये तारनादेन सर्वशः ..
नादयंतो दिशां चक्रं तत्र सम्यग्द्विजोत्तमाः .. 5 ..
5.37.m: others, intent on the study of the Veda with a loud voice, / properly filled the circle of the cardinal points with sound everywhere there, O best of brahmins;

5.37.s:
anye kautūhalāviṣṭāḥ saṃcarānviṣamānmithaḥ ..
papracchurjahasuścānye jñātvā mārgapravartinam .. 6 ..
5.37.d:
अन्ये कौतूहलाविष्टाः संचरान्विषमान्मिथः ..
पप्रच्छुर्जहसुश्चान्ये ज्ञात्वा मार्गप्रवर्तिनम् .. 6 ..
5.37.m: others, seized with curiosity, questioned one another on difficult passages, / while others laughed upon identifying one straying from the path;

5.37.s:
smṛtivādaparāścānye tathānye śrutipāṭhakāḥ ..
saṃdehānsmṛtijānanye pṛcchaṃti ca parasparam .. 7 ..
5.37.d:
स्मृतिवादपराश्चान्ये तथान्ये श्रुतिपाठकाः ..
संदेहान्स्मृतिजानन्ये पृच्छंति च परस्परम् .. 7 ..
5.37.m: others were devoted to discussions on the Smṛti, and others were reciters of the Śruti; / others questioned one another about doubts arising from the Smṛti;

5.37.s:
kīrtayaṃti tathā cānye purāṇaṃ brāhmaṇottamāḥ ..
vṛddhānāṃ puratastatra sabhāmadhye vyavasthitāḥ .. 8 ..
5.37.d:
कीर्तयंति तथा चान्ये पुराणं ब्राह्मणोत्तमाः ..
वृद्धानां पुरतस्तत्र सभामध्ये व्यवस्थिताः .. 8 ..
5.37.m: and other excellent brahmins recited the Purāṇa / in front of the elders, seated in the midst of the assembly there.

5.37.s:
atha tānsa munirdṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇānsaṃśitavratān ..
abhivādya tataḥ prāha sādaraṃ vinayānvitaḥ .. 9 ..
5.37.d:
अथ तान्स मुनिर्दृष्ट्वा ब्राह्मणान्संशितव्रतान् ..
अभिवाद्य ततः प्राह सादरं विनयान्वितः .. 9 ..
5.37.m: Then, having seen those brahmins of strict vows / and greeted them, that sage spoke with respect and humility:

5.37.s:
mama buddhiḥ samutpannā śambhorāyatanaṃ prati ..
kartuṃ brāhmaṇaśārdūlāstasmātsthānaṃ pradarśyatām .. 6.37.10 ..
5.37.d:
मम बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना शम्भोरायतनं प्रति ..
कर्तुं ब्राह्मणशार्दूलास्तस्मात्स्थानं प्रदर्श्यताम् .. 6.37.10 ..
5.37.m: "The desire has arisen in my mind to build a temple to Śambhu, / O tigers among brahmins; therefore, let a site be indicated.

5.37.s:
tavāhaṃ devadevasya śambhoḥ prāsādamuttamam ..
vidhāyārādhayiṣyāmi tameva vṛṣabhadhvajam .. 11 ..
5.37.d:
तवाहं देवदेवस्य शम्भोः प्रासादमुत्तमम् ..
विधायाराधयिष्यामि तमेव वृषभध्वजम् .. 11 ..
5.37.m: Having constructed an excellent temple to that Śambhu, the god of gods, / I shall worship him alone whose banner bears the bull."

5.37.s:
sa evaṃ jalpamāno'pi muhurmuhurataṃdritaḥ ..
na teṣāmuttaraṃ lebhe śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham .. 12 ..
5.37.d:
स एवं जल्पमानोऽपि मुहुर्मुहुरतंद्रितः ..
न तेषामुत्तरं लेभे शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम् .. 12 ..
5.37.m: Although he spoke thus repeatedly and unweariedly, / he received no answer from them, whether good or bad.

5.37.s:
tataḥ kopaparītātmā samunistāndvijottamān ..
śaśāpa tāraśabdena yathā śṛṇvaṃti kṛtsnaśaḥ .. 13 ..
5.37.d:
ततः कोपपरीतात्मा समुनिस्तान्द्विजोत्तमान् ..
शशाप तारशब्देन यथा शृण्वंति कृत्स्नशः .. 13 ..
5.37.m: Then, his mind seized by anger, that sage / cursed those excellent brahmins in a loud voice so that all could hear completely:

5.37.s:
.. durvāsā uvāca .. ..
vidyāmado dhanamadastṛtīyo'bhijanodbhavaḥ ..
ete madāvaliptānāmeta eva satāṃ damāḥ .. 14 ..
5.37.d:
.. दुर्वासा उवाच .. ..
विद्यामदो धनमदस्तृतीयोऽभिजनोद्भवः ..
एते मदावलिप्तानामेत एव सतां दमाः .. 14 ..
5.37.m: Durvāsas said: / "Arrogance born of learning, arrogance born of wealth, and a third born of high birth: / these belong to those blinded by pride; these very things are the self-restraint of the good.

5.37.s:
tatra ye'pi hi yuṣmākaṃ madā eva vyavasthitāḥ ..
yatastato'nvaye'pyevaṃ bhaviṣyati madānvitāḥ .. 15 ..
5.37.d:
तत्र येऽपि हि युष्माकं मदा एव व्यवस्थिताः ..
यतस्ततोऽन्वयेऽप्येवं भविष्यति मदान्विताः .. 15 ..
5.37.m: Since these very haughtinesses are established among you, / therefore, even in your lineage, they shall be filled with pride.

5.37.s:
sadā sauhṛdanirmuktāḥ pitaro'pi sutaiḥ saha ..
bhaviṣyaṃti pure hyasminkiṃ punarbāṃdhavādayaḥ .. 16 ..
5.37.d:
सदा सौहृदनिर्मुक्ताः पितरोऽपि सुतैः सह ..
भविष्यंति पुरे ह्यस्मिन्किं पुनर्बांधवादयः .. 16 ..
5.37.m: Always bereft of affection, even fathers with their sons / shall live in this city, to say nothing of kinsmen and others!"

5.37.s:
evamuktvā sa viprendro nivṛttastadanantaram ..
apamānaṃ paraṃ prāpya brāhmaṇānāṃ dvijottamāḥ .. 17 ..
5.37.d:
एवमुक्त्वा स विप्रेन्द्रो निवृत्तस्तदनन्तरम् ..
अपमानं परं प्राप्य ब्राह्मणानां द्विजोत्तमाः .. 17 ..
5.37.m: Having spoken thus, that foremost among the twice-born then turned back, / having met with supreme disrespect from the brahmins, O best of brahmins.

5.37.s:
atha tanmadhyago vipra āsīdvṛddhatamaḥ sudhīḥ ..
suśīla iti vikhyāto vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ .. 18 ..
5.37.d:
अथ तन्मध्यगो विप्र आसीद्वृद्धतमः सुधीः ..
सुशील इति विख्यातो वेदवेदांगपारगः .. 18 ..
5.37.m: Now, among them was an elder brahmin of wise intellect, / renowned by the name Suśīla, who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

5.37.s:
sa dṛṣṭvā taṃ muniṃ kruddhaṃ gacchaṃtamapamānitam ..
satvaraṃ prayayau pṛṣṭhe tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti ca bruvan.. 19 ..
5.37.d:
स दृष्ट्वा तं मुनिं क्रुद्धं गच्छंतमपमानितम् ..
सत्वरं प्रययौ पृष्ठे तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति च ब्रुवन्.. 19 ..
5.37.m: Seeing that sage departing angry and insulted, / he quickly went after him, calling out, "Stop! Stop!"

5.37.s:
athāsādya gataṃ dūraṃ praṇipatya muniṃ ca saḥ ..
provāca kṣamyatāṃ vipra viprāṇāṃ vacanānmama .. 6.37.20 ..
5.37.d:
अथासाद्य गतं दूरं प्रणिपत्य मुनिं च सः ..
प्रोवाच क्षम्यतां विप्र विप्राणां वचनान्मम .. 6.37.20 ..
5.37.m: Then, having approached the sage who had gone far, and bowing down to him, / he said, "O brahmin, forgive the brahmins at my word.

5.37.s:
etaiḥ svādhyāyasaṃpannairna śrutaṃ vacanaṃ tava ..
nottaraṃ tena saṃdattaṃ satyametadbravīmyaham .. 21 ..
5.37.d:
एतैः स्वाध्यायसंपन्नैर्न श्रुतं वचनं तव ..
नोत्तरं तेन संदत्तं सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीम्यहम् .. 21 ..
5.37.m: Absorbed in their own Vedic study, your word was not heard by them; / on that account no reply was given; I speak the truth.

5.37.s:
tasmādbhūmirmayā dattā śaṃbhuharmyakṛte tava ..
asminsthāne dvijaśreṣṭha prāsādaṃ kartumarhasi .. 22 ..
5.37.d:
तस्माद्भूमिर्मया दत्ता शंभुहर्म्यकृते तव ..
अस्मिन्स्थाने द्विजश्रेष्ठ प्रासादं कर्तुमर्हसि .. 22 ..
5.37.m: Therefore, land is given by me to you for a temple of Śambhu; / in this place, O best of brahmins, you ought to build a temple."

5.37.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā durvāsā harṣasaṃyutaḥ ..
kṣitidānodbhavāṃ cakre svasti brāhmaṇasattamāḥ ..
prāsādaṃ nirmame paścāttasya vākye vyavasthitaḥ .. 23 ..
5.37.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दुर्वासा हर्षसंयुतः ..
क्षितिदानोद्भवां चक्रे स्वस्ति ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ..
प्रासादं निर्ममे पश्चात्तस्य वाक्ये व्यवस्थितः .. 23 ..
5.37.m: Hearing his word, Durvāsas was filled with joy; / he pronounced a blessing arising from the gift of land, O best of brahmins, / and afterwards, abiding by his word, he constructed a temple.

5.37.s:
atha te brāhmaṇā jñātvā suśīlena vasundharā ..
devatāyatanārthāya dattā tasmai tapasvine .. 24 ..
5.37.d:
अथ ते ब्राह्मणा ज्ञात्वा सुशीलेन वसुन्धरा ..
देवतायतनार्थाय दत्ता तस्मै तपस्विने .. 24 ..
5.37.m: Then, those brahmins learned that land had been given by Suśīla / to that ascetic for the purpose of a temple to the deity.

5.37.s: sarve kopasamāyuktāḥ suśīlaṃ prati te dvijāḥ .. 25 ..
5.37.d: सर्वे कोपसमायुक्ताः सुशीलं प्रति ते द्विजाः .. 25 ..
5.37.m: All those brahmins were filled with anger toward Suśīla.

5.37.s:
tataḥ procuḥ samāsādya yena śaptā durātmanā ..
vayaṃ tasmai tvayā dattā prāsādārthaṃ vasundharā .. 26 ..
5.37.d:
ततः प्रोचुः समासाद्य येन शप्ता दुरात्मना ..
वयं तस्मै त्वया दत्ता प्रासादार्थं वसुन्धरा .. 26 ..
5.37.m: Then, approaching him, they said: "Land has been given by you for a temple / to that wicked-minded one by whom we were cursed!

5.37.s:
tasmāttvamapi cāsmākaṃ bāhya eva bhaviṣyasi ..
suśīlo'pi hi duḥśīlo nāmnā saṃkīrtyase budhaiḥ .. 27 ..
5.37.d:
तस्मात्त्वमपि चास्माकं बाह्य एव भविष्यसि ..
सुशीलोऽपि हि दुःशीलो नाम्ना संकीर्त्यसे बुधैः .. 27 ..
5.37.m: Therefore you, too, shall become an outcast among us; / and though named Suśīla ('virtuous'), you will be called Duḥśīla ('ill-natured') by the wise!

5.37.s:
eṣo'pi tāpaso duṣṭo yaḥ karoti śivālayam ...
naiva tasya bhavetsiddhiścāpi varṣaśatairapi .. 28 ..
5.37.d:
एषोऽपि तापसो दुष्टो यः करोति शिवालयम् ...
नैव तस्य भवेत्सिद्धिश्चापि वर्षशतैरपि .. 28 ..
5.37.m: As for this wicked ascetic who is building a dwelling for Śiva, / no accomplishment shall arise for him, even in a hundred years!

5.37.s:
tathā kīrtikṛtāṃ loke kīrtanaṃ kriyate naraiḥ ..
tataḥ saṃpaśyatāṃ cāsya kīrtirnāsya tu durmateḥ .. .. 29 ..
5.37.d:
तथा कीर्तिकृतां लोके कीर्तनं क्रियते नरैः ..
ततः संपश्यतां चास्य कीर्तिर्नास्य तु दुर्मतेः .. .. 29 ..
5.37.m: Likewise, in this world, praise is uttered by men for temple-builders; / therefore, as all look on, there shall be no fame for this wicked-minded one!"

5.37.s:
eṣa duḥśīlasaṃjño vai tava nāmnā bhaviṣyati ..
prāsādo nāmamātreṇa na saṃpūrṇaḥ kadācana .. 6.37.30 ..
5.37.d:
एष दुःशीलसंज्ञो वै तव नाम्ना भविष्यति ..
प्रासादो नाममात्रेण न संपूर्णः कदाचन .. 6.37.30 ..
5.37.m: "This temple will indeed be known as Duḥśīla after your name. / It will exist in name only, never completed.

5.37.s:
yasmātsauhṛdanirmuktāḥ kṛtāstena vayaṃ dvijāḥ ..
madaistribhiḥ samāyuktāḥ sarvānvayasamanvitāḥ .. 31 ..
5.37.d:
यस्मात्सौहृदनिर्मुक्ताः कृतास्तेन वयं द्विजाः ..
मदैस्त्रिभिः समायुक्ताः सर्वान्वयसमन्विताः .. 31 ..
5.37.m: Because of him, we twice-born who are possessed of the three prides, / along with our entire lineages, have been bereft of friendliness;

5.37.s:
tasmādeṣo'pi pāpātmā bhaviṣyati sa kopabhāk ..
taptaṃ taptaṃ tapo yena saṃprayāsyati saṃkṣayam.. 32 ..
5.37.d:
तस्मादेषोऽपि पापात्मा भविष्यति स कोपभाक् ..
तप्तं तप्तं तपो येन संप्रयास्यति संक्षयम्.. 32 ..
5.37.m: therefore this sinful man too shall become prone to anger, / by which whatever tapas he has performed will go to ruin."

5.37.s:
evamuktvātha te viprāḥ kopasaṃraktalocanāḥ ..
duḥśīlaṃ saṃparityajya praviṣṭāḥ svapure tataḥ .. 33 ..
5.37.d:
एवमुक्त्वाथ ते विप्राः कोपसंरक्तलोचनाः ..
दुःशीलं संपरित्यज्य प्रविष्टाः स्वपुरे ततः .. 33 ..
5.37.m: Having spoken thus, those brahmins with eyes reddened by wrath, / having completely abandoned Duḥśīla, then entered their own city.

5.37.s:
duḥśīlo'pi bahiścakre gṛhaṃ tasya purasya ca ..
devaśarmā yathāpūrvaṃ saṃtyaktaḥ puravāsibhiḥ .. 34 ..
5.37.d:
दुःशीलोऽपि बहिश्चक्रे गृहं तस्य पुरस्य च ..
देवशर्मा यथापूर्वं संत्यक्तः पुरवासिभिः .. 34 ..
5.37.m: Duḥśīla also built his house outside that city, / just as Devaśarman was previously cast out by the city dwellers.

5.37.s:
tasyānvaye'pi ye jātāste bāhyāḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ ..
bāhyāḥ kriyāsu sarvāsu sarveṣāṃ puravāsinām .. 35 ..
5.37.d:
तस्यान्वयेऽपि ये जातास्ते बाह्याः संप्रकीर्तिताः ..
बाह्याः क्रियासु सर्वासु सर्वेषां पुरवासिनाम् .. 35 ..
5.37.m: Those who were born in his lineage are declared to be 'outsiders', / excluded from all religious rites of all the city dwellers.

5.37.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ teṣu dvijeṃdreṣu śāpaṃ dattvā gateṣu ca ..
durvāsāḥ prāha duḥśīlaṃ kopasaṃraktalo canaḥ .. 36 ..
5.37.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं तेषु द्विजेंद्रेषु शापं दत्त्वा गतेषु च ..
दुर्वासाः प्राह दुःशीलं कोपसंरक्तलो चनः .. 36 ..
5.37.m: Sūta said: / When those lords of twice-born had departed after uttering the curse, / Durvāsas, his eyes reddened with wrath, said to Duḥśīla:

5.37.s:
mama siddhiṃ gatā maṃtrāḥ samarthāḥ śatrusaṃkṣaye ..
ātharvaṇāstathā cānye vedatrayasamudbhavāḥ .. 37 ..
5.37.d:
मम सिद्धिं गता मंत्राः समर्थाः शत्रुसंक्षये ..
आथर्वणास्तथा चान्ये वेदत्रयसमुद्भवाः .. 37 ..
5.37.m: "My mantras have achieved perfection, capable of destroying enemies— / those of the Atharvaveda, and others originating from the three Vedas.

5.37.s:
tasmādetatpuraṃ kṛtsnaṃ paśupakṣi samanvitam ..
nāśamadya nayiṣyāmi yathā śatrorhi duṣṭakaḥ .. 38 ..
5.37.d:
तस्मादेतत्पुरं कृत्स्नं पशुपक्षि समन्वितम् ..
नाशमद्य नयिष्यामि यथा शत्रोर्हि दुष्टकः .. 38 ..
5.37.m: Therefore today I will lead this entire city, together with its beasts and birds, / to destruction, just as a wicked man destroys his enemy."

5.37.s:
.. duḥśīla uvāca .. ..
naitadyuktaṃ naraśreṣṭha tava kartuṃ kathaṃcana ...
brāhmaṇānāṃ kṛte karma brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ .. 39 ..
5.37.d:
.. दुःशील उवाच .. ..
नैतद्युक्तं नरश्रेष्ठ तव कर्तुं कथंचन ...
ब्राह्मणानां कृते कर्म ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः .. 39 ..
5.37.m: Duḥśīla said: / "It is not proper for you, best of men, in any way to do this / deed toward brahmins, especially as a brahmin yourself.

5.37.s:
nighnaṃto vā śapaṃto vā vadaṃto vāpi niṣṭhuram ..
pūjanīyāḥ sadā viprā divyām̐llokānabhīpsubhiḥ .. 6.37.40 ..
5.37.d:
निघ्नंतो वा शपंतो वा वदंतो वापि निष्ठुरम् ..
पूजनीयाः सदा विप्रा दिव्याम्̐ल्लोकानभीप्सुभिः .. 6.37.40 ..
5.37.m: Whether striking, cursing, or speaking harshly, / brahmins must always be honoured by those desiring divine worlds.

5.37.s:
brāhmaṇairnirjitairmene ya ātmānaṃ jayānvitam ..
tāmisrādiṣu ghoreṣu narakeṣu sa pacyate .. 41 ..
5.37.d:
ब्राह्मणैर्निर्जितैर्मेने य आत्मानं जयान्वितम् ..
तामिस्रादिषु घोरेषु नरकेषु स पच्यते .. 41 ..
5.37.m: He who considers himself victorious over defeated brahmins / cooks in terrible hells such as Tāmisra.

5.37.s:
ātmanaśca parābhūtiṃ tasmādviprātsaheta vai ..
ya icchedvasatiṃ svarge śāśvatīṃ dvijasattama .. 42 ..
5.37.d:
आत्मनश्च पराभूतिं तस्माद्विप्रात्सहेत वै ..
य इच्छेद्वसतिं स्वर्गे शाश्वतीं द्विजसत्तम .. 42 ..
5.37.m: Therefore one should endure defeat of oneself by a brahmin, / if one desires an eternal dwelling in heaven, O best of the twice-born.

5.37.s:
eteṣāṃ brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ kṣetre siddhiṃ samāgatāḥ ..
maṃtrāste tatkathaṃ nāśaṃ tvameteṣāṃ kariṣyasi .. 43 ..
5.37.d:
एतेषां ब्राह्मणेंद्राणां क्षेत्रे सिद्धिं समागताः ..
मंत्रास्ते तत्कथं नाशं त्वमेतेषां करिष्यसि .. 43 ..
5.37.m: Your mantras attained perfection in the kṣetra of these lords of brahmins; / so how can you bring about their destruction?

5.37.s:
brahmaghne ca surāpe ca caure bhagnavate tathā ..
niṣkṛtirvihitā sadbhiḥ kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ .. .. 44 ..
5.37.d:
ब्रह्मघ्ने च सुरापे च चौरे भग्नवते तथा ..
निष्कृतिर्विहिता सद्भिः कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः .. .. 44 ..
5.37.m: For the slayer of a brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the thief, and the breaker of vows, / expiation is prescribed by the virtuous, but for the ungrateful there is no expiation.

5.37.s:
tasmātkopo na kartavyaḥ kṣetre cātra vyavasthitaiḥ ..
kṣamāṃ kuru muniśreṣṭha kṛpāṃ kṛtvā mamopari ..45 ..
5.37.d:
तस्मात्कोपो न कर्तव्यः क्षेत्रे चात्र व्यवस्थितैः ..
क्षमां कुरु मुनिश्रेष्ठ कृपां कृत्वा ममोपरि ..45 ..
5.37.m: Therefore anger should not be felt by those dwelling in this kṣetra; / show patience, O best of sages, having mercy on me."

5.37.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
sa tatheti pratijñāya tatra kṛtvāvasattapaḥ ..
prāptaśca paramāṃ siddhiṃ durlabhāṃ tridaśairapi .. 46 ..
5.37.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय तत्र कृत्वावसत्तपः ..
प्राप्तश्च परमां सिद्धिं दुर्लभां त्रिदशैरपि .. 46 ..
5.37.m: Sūta said: / Assenting with 'So be it', he performed tapas dwelling there, / and attained the highest perfection, difficult even for the thirty [gods] to reach.

5.37.s:
duḥśīlākhyaḥ kṣitau so'pi prāsādaḥ khyāti māgataḥ ..
yasya saṃdarśanādeva naraḥ pāpātpramucyate .. 47 ..
5.37.d:
दुःशीलाख्यः क्षितौ सोऽपि प्रासादः ख्याति मागतः ..
यस्य संदर्शनादेव नरः पापात्प्रमुच्यते .. 47 ..
5.37.m: That temple also became famous on earth by the name Duḥśīla, / merely by the sight of which a man is freed from sin.

5.37.s:
tasya madhyagataṃ liṃgaṃ śuklāṣṭamyāṃ sadā naraḥ ..
yaḥ paśyati kṣaṇaṃ dhyātvā narakaṃ sa na paśyati .. 48 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇe ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye duḥśīlākhyaprāsādotpatti varṇanaṃnāma saptatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 37 .. .. cha ..
5.37.d:
तस्य मध्यगतं लिंगं शुक्लाष्टम्यां सदा नरः ..
यः पश्यति क्षणं ध्यात्वा नरकं स न पश्यति .. 48 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराणे एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये दुःशीलाख्यप्रासादोत्पत्ति वर्णनंनाम सप्तत्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 37 .. .. छ ..
5.37.m:
A man who meditates for a moment on the liṅga within it / and sees it on the eighth day of the bright fortnight never sees hell.
Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, named 'Description of the Origin of the Temple Called Duḥśīla', in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.38.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tatraiva sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ dhundhumāreṇa bhūbhujā ..
sarvaratnamayaṃ kṛtvā prāsādaṃ sumanoharam .. 1 ..
5.38.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तत्रैव स्थापितं लिंगं धुन्धुमारेण भूभुजा ..
सर्वरत्नमयं कृत्वा प्रासादं सुमनोहरम् .. 1 ..
5.38.m: Sūta said: / Right there a liṅga was installed by King Dhundhumāra, / after he made a very charming temple made of all kinds of gems.

5.38.s:
tatra kṛtvā''śramaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tapastepe sudāruṇam ..
yatprabhāvādayaṃ devastasmim̐lliṅge vyavasthitaḥ .. 2 ..
5.38.d:
तत्र कृत्वा'ऽश्रमं श्रेष्ठं तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम् ..
यत्प्रभावादयं देवस्तस्मिम्̐ल्लिङ्गे व्यवस्थितः .. 2 ..
5.38.m: Establishing an excellent hermitage there, he performed terrible tapas, / by whose power this god took up his abode in that liṅga.

5.38.s:
tasya saṃnihitā vāpī kṛtā tena mahātmanā ..
sunirmalajalāpūrṇā sarvatīrthopamā śubhā .. 3 ..
5.38.d:
तस्य संनिहिता वापी कृता तेन महात्मना ..
सुनिर्मलजलापूर्णा सर्वतीर्थोपमा शुभा .. 3 ..
5.38.m: Close to it a stepwell was constructed by that great soul, / filled with very pure water, auspicious and equal to all sacred fords.

5.38.s:
dhundhumāreśvaraṃ paśyettatra snātvā narottamaḥ ..
na sa paśyati durgāṇi narakāṇi yamālaye .. 4 ..
5.38.d:
धुन्धुमारेश्वरं पश्येत्तत्र स्नात्वा नरोत्तमः ..
न स पश्यति दुर्गाणि नरकाणि यमालये .. 4 ..
5.38.m: Having bathed there, the best of men should behold Dhundhumāreśvara; / he will not behold the impassable hells in Yama's abode.

5.38.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
dhuṃdhumāro mahīpālaḥ kasminvaṃśe babhūva saḥ ..
kasminkāle tapastaptaṃ tenātra sumahātmanā .. 5 ..
5.38.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
धुंधुमारो महीपालः कस्मिन्वंशे बभूव सः ..
कस्मिन्काले तपस्तप्तं तेनात्र सुमहात्मना .. 5 ..
5.38.m: The ṛṣis said: / In which lineage was King Dhundhumāra born? / At what time was tapas performed here by that very great soul?

5.38.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
sūryavaṃśasamudbhūto bṛhadaśvasuto balī ..
khyātaḥ kuvalayāśveti dhaṃdhumārastathaiva saḥ .. 6 ..
5.38.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
सूर्यवंशसमुद्भूतो बृहदश्वसुतो बली ..
ख्यातः कुवलयाश्वेति धंधुमारस्तथैव सः .. 6 ..
5.38.m: Sūta said: / Born in the Solar dynasty was the mighty son of Bṛhadaśva, / known as Kuvalayāśva and likewise as Dhundhumāra.

5.38.s:
tena dhundhurmahādaityo nihato marujāṃgale ..
dhundhumāraḥ smṛtastena vikhyāto bhuvanatraye .. 7 ..
5.38.d:
तेन धुन्धुर्महादैत्यो निहतो मरुजांगले ..
धुन्धुमारः स्मृतस्तेन विख्यातो भुवनत्रये .. 7 ..
5.38.m: By him the great Daitya Dhundhu was slain in the desert waste; / therefore he is remembered as Dhundhumāra, renowned across the three worlds.

5.38.s:
camatkārapuraṃ kṣetraṃ sa gatvā pāvanaṃ mahat ..
tapastepe vayoṃ'te ca dhyāyamāno maheśvaram .. 8 ..
5.38.d:
चमत्कारपुरं क्षेत्रं स गत्वा पावनं महत् ..
तपस्तेपे वयोंऽते च ध्यायमानो महेश्वरम् .. 8 ..
5.38.m: Having gone to the great and purifying kṣetra of Camatkārapura, / he performed tapas at the end of his life, meditating upon Maheśvara.

5.38.s:
saṃsthāpya sumahalliṃgaṃ prāsāde ratnamaṃḍite ..
balipūjopahārādyaiḥ puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ .. 9 ..
5.38.d:
संस्थाप्य सुमहल्लिंगं प्रासादे रत्नमंडिते ..
बलिपूजोपहाराद्यैः पुष्पधूपानुलेपनैः .. 9 ..
5.38.m: Having installed a very great liṅga in a gem-adorned temple, / [he worshipped] with offerings, oblations, presents, flowers, incense, and unguents.

5.38.s:
tatastasya mahādevaḥ svayameva maheśvaraḥ ..
pratyakṣo'bhūdvṛṣārūḍho gauryā saha tathā gaṇaiḥ .. 6.38.10 ..
5.38.d:
ततस्तस्य महादेवः स्वयमेव महेश्वरः ..
प्रत्यक्षोऽभूद्वृषारूढो गौर्या सह तथा गणैः .. 6.38.10 ..
5.38.m: Then Mahādeva himself, Maheśvara, / mounted on the bull, became visible to him along with Gaurī and his gaṇas.

5.38.s:
uvāca varado'smīti prārthayasva yathepsitam ..
sarvaṃ te'haṃ pradāsyāmi yadyapi syātsudurlabham .. 11 .. ..
5.38.d:
उवाच वरदोऽस्मीति प्रार्थयस्व यथेप्सितम् ..
सर्वं तेऽहं प्रदास्यामि यद्यपि स्यात्सुदुर्लभम् .. 11 .. ..
5.38.m: He said: "I am a granter of boons; ask whatever you desire; / I will give you everything, even though it be very difficult to attain."

5.38.s:
dhundhumāra uvāca .. ..
yadi deyo varo'smākaṃ tvayā sarvasureśvara ..
saṃnidhānaṃ prakartavyaṃ liṃge'sminvṛṣabhadhvaja .. 12 ..
5.38.d:
धुन्धुमार उवाच .. ..
यदि देयो वरोऽस्माकं त्वया सर्वसुरेश्वर ..
संनिधानं प्रकर्तव्यं लिंगेऽस्मिन्वृषभध्वज .. 12 ..
5.38.m: Dhundhumāra said: / "If a boon is to be given to me by you, O Lord of all gods, / your presence should be established in this liṅga, O bull-bannered Lord!"

5.38.s:
.. śrībhagavānuvāca .. ..
caitre śuklacaturdaśyāṃ sāṃnidhyaṃ nṛpasattama ..
ahaṃ sadā kariṣyāmi gauryā sārdhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 13 ..
5.38.d:
.. श्रीभगवानुवाच .. ..
चैत्रे शुक्लचतुर्दश्यां सांनिध्यं नृपसत्तम ..
अहं सदा करिष्यामि गौर्या सार्धं न संशयः .. 13 ..
5.38.m: The Blessed Lord said: / "On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, O best of kings, / I will always abide here in presence together with Gaurī, without a doubt.

5.38.s:
tatra vāpyāṃ naraḥ snātvā yo māṃ saṃpūjayiṣyati ..
liṃge'sminsaṃsthitaṃ bhūpa mama lokaṃ sa yāsyati .. 14 ..
5.38.d:
तत्र वाप्यां नरः स्नात्वा यो मां संपूजयिष्यति ..
लिंगेऽस्मिन्संस्थितं भूप मम लोकं स यास्यति .. 14 ..
5.38.m: A man who, having bathed in that stepwell, worships me / residing in this liṅga, O king, will go to my realm."

5.38.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamuktvā sa bhagavāṃstataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ ..
so'pi rājā prahṛṣṭā tmā sthitastatraiva muktibhāk .. 15 ..
5.38.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा स भगवांस्ततश्चादर्शनं गतः ..
सोऽपि राजा प्रहृष्टा त्मा स्थितस्तत्रैव मुक्तिभाक् .. 15 ..
5.38.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord then vanished from sight. / That king too, his soul delighted, remained right there, attaining liberation.

5.38.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye dhundhumāreśvaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭātriṃśo adhyāyaḥ .. 38 .. .. cha ..
5.38.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये धुन्धुमारेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामाष्टात्रिंशो अध्यायः .. 38 .. .. छ ..
5.38.m: Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of Dhundhumāreśvara', in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.39.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tasyaivottaradigbhāge dhundhumāreśvarasya ca ..
yayātinā nareṃdreṇa sthāpitaṃ liṃgamuttamam .. 1 ..
5.39.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तस्यैवोत्तरदिग्भागे धुन्धुमारेश्वरस्य च ..
ययातिना नरेंद्रेण स्थापितं लिंगमुत्तमम् .. 1 ..
5.39.m: Sūta said: / In the northern region of that very Dhundhumāreśvara, / an excellent liṅga was installed by King Yayāti,

5.39.s:
devayānyā tathānyacca tathā śarmiṣṭhayā dvijāḥ ..
bhāryayā bhūpatestasya sarvakāmaphalapradam .. 2 ..
5.39.d:
देवयान्या तथान्यच्च तथा शर्मिष्ठया द्विजाः ..
भार्यया भूपतेस्तस्य सर्वकामफलप्रदम् .. 2 ..
5.39.m: and another by Devayānī, and also by Śarmiṣṭhā, O twice-born, / the wives of that king, bestowing the fruit of all desires.

5.39.s:
sa yadā sarvabhogānāṃ tṛptiṃ prāpto dvijottamāḥ ..
tadā putrasya rājyaṃ svaṃ vapuścaiva nyavedayat ..3..
5.39.d:
स यदा सर्वभोगानां तृप्तिं प्राप्तो द्विजोत्तमाः ..
तदा पुत्रस्य राज्यं स्वं वपुश्चैव न्यवेदयत् ..3..
5.39.m: When he had reached satiety with all pleasures, O best of the twice-born, / he then offered his kingdom and his own body to his son.

5.39.s:
jarāmādāya tadgātrādbhāryābhyāṃ sahitastadā ..
papraccha vinayopeto mārkaṃḍaṃ munisattamam .. 4 ..
5.39.d:
जरामादाय तद्गात्राद्भार्याभ्यां सहितस्तदा ..
पप्रच्छ विनयोपेतो मार्कंडं मुनिसत्तमम् .. 4 ..
5.39.m: Taking back the old age from his [son's] body, accompanied by his two wives, / he then, endowed with humility, questioned Mārkaṇḍa, best of sages.

5.39.s:
bhagavansarvatīrthānāṃ kṣetrāṇāṃ ca vadasva me ..
yatpradhānaṃ pavitraṃ yattadasmākaṃ prakīrtaya .. 5 .. ..
5.39.d:
भगवन्सर्वतीर्थानां क्षेत्राणां च वदस्व मे ..
यत्प्रधानं पवित्रं यत्तदस्माकं प्रकीर्तय .. 5 .. ..
5.39.m: "O venerable one, tell me of all sacred fords and sacred fields! / Proclaim to us that which is foremost and holy!"

5.39.s:
.. śrīmārkaṃḍeya uvāca .. ..
kṣetrāṇāmiha sarveṣāṃ tīrthaiḥ sarvairalaṃkṛtam ..
camatkārapuraṃ kṣetraṃ sāṃprataṃ pratibhāti naḥ .. 6 ..
5.39.d:
.. श्रीमार्कंडेय उवाच .. ..
क्षेत्राणामिह सर्वेषां तीर्थैः सर्वैरलंकृतम् ..
चमत्कारपुरं क्षेत्रं सांप्रतं प्रतिभाति नः .. 6 ..
5.39.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / "Among all sacred fields here, adorned with all sacred fords, / the sacred field Camatkārapura now shines forth to us,

5.39.s:
yatra viṣṇupadī gaṃgā jaṃtūnāṃ pāpanāśinī ..
svayaṃ sthitā nṛpaśreṣṭha tathā devā harādayaḥ .. 7 ..
5.39.d:
यत्र विष्णुपदी गंगा जंतूनां पापनाशिनी ..
स्वयं स्थिता नृपश्रेष्ठ तथा देवा हरादयः .. 7 ..
5.39.m: where the Gaṅgā that flows from Viṣṇu's foot, destroyer of the sins of living beings, / is personally present, O best of kings, and likewise the gods beginning with Hara,

5.39.s:
tathānyāni ca tīrthāni yāni saṃti dharātale ..
teṣāṃ yatra ca sāṃnidhyaṃ sarvadā nṛpasattama .. 8 ..
5.39.d:
तथान्यानि च तीर्थानि यानि संति धरातले ..
तेषां यत्र च सांनिध्यं सर्वदा नृपसत्तम .. 8 ..
5.39.m: and whatever other sacred fords exist on the surface of the earth, / whose presence is always there, O best of kings,

5.39.s:
śilā yatra dvipañcāśaddhastānāṃ parisaṃkhyayā ..
pitāmahena nirmuktā pramodāya dvijanmanām .. 9 ..
5.39.d:
शिला यत्र द्विपञ्चाशद्धस्तानां परिसंख्यया ..
पितामहेन निर्मुक्ता प्रमोदाय द्विजन्मनाम् .. 9 ..
5.39.m: where a stone measuring fifty-two cubits / was cast down by the Grandfather for the delight of the twice-born.

5.39.s:
yadanyatra śubhaṃ karma varṣeṇaikena sidhyati ..
tattatra divasenāpi siddhiṃ yāti kṣitīśvara .. 6.39.10 ..
5.39.d:
यदन्यत्र शुभं कर्म वर्षेणैकेन सिध्यति ..
तत्तत्र दिवसेनापि सिद्धिं याति क्षितीश्वर .. 6.39.10 ..
5.39.m: An auspicious rite which succeeds elsewhere in one year / attains success there in even a single day, O lord of the earth.

5.39.s:
tasmāttatra drutaṃ gatvā tapaḥ kuru mahīpate ..
yena prāpsyasi cittasthām̐llokānbhāryāsamanvitaḥ .. 11 ..
5.39.d:
तस्मात्तत्र द्रुतं गत्वा तपः कुरु महीपते ..
येन प्राप्स्यसि चित्तस्थाम्̐ल्लोकान्भार्यासमन्वितः .. 11 ..
5.39.m: Therefore, go there quickly and perform austerity, O king of the earth, / whereby, accompanied by your wives, you will attain the worlds desired in your heart."

5.39.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa rājā nahuṣātmajaḥ ..
camatkārapure kṣetre bhāryābhyāṃ sahito yayau .. 12 ..
5.39.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा स राजा नहुषात्मजः ..
चमत्कारपुरे क्षेत्रे भार्याभ्यां सहितो ययौ .. 12 ..
5.39.m: Hearing his words, that king, the son of Nahuṣa, / went with his two wives to the sacred field of Camatkārapura.

5.39.s:
tataḥ saṃsthāpya talliṃgaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ ..
samyagārādhayāmāsa śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ .. 13 ..
5.39.d:
ततः संस्थाप्य तल्लिंगं देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ..
सम्यगाराधयामास श्रद्धया परया युतः .. 13 ..
5.39.m: Then, having installed that liṅga of the god of gods, the trident-bearer, / he worshipped it properly, endowed with supreme faith.

5.39.s:
tatastasya prabhāvena bhāryābhyāṃ sahito nṛpaḥ ..
vimānavaramārūḍho jagāma tridivālayam .. 14 ..
5.39.d:
ततस्तस्य प्रभावेन भार्याभ्यां सहितो नृपः ..
विमानवरमारूढो जगाम त्रिदिवालयम् .. 14 ..
5.39.m: Then, through its power, the king, accompanied by his two wives, / mounted an excellent aerial chariot and went to the abode of heaven,

5.39.s:
kinnarairgīyamānaśca stūyamānaśca cāraṇaiḥ ..
sparddhamānaḥ samaṃ devairdvādaśārkasamaprabhaḥ .. 15 ..
5.39.d:
किन्नरैर्गीयमानश्च स्तूयमानश्च चारणैः ..
स्पर्द्धमानः समं देवैर्द्वादशार्कसमप्रभः .. 15 ..
5.39.m: being sung of by kinnaras and praised by cāraṇas, / rivaling the gods, resplendent as twelve suns.

5.39.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye yayātīśvaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmaikonacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ.. .. 39 .. .. cha ..
5.39.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये ययातीश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामैकोनचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः.. .. 39 .. .. छ ..
5.39.m: Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, titled 'Description of the Māhātmya of Yayātīśvara', in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] in the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.40.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
yadeṣā bhavatā proktā brāhmī tatra mahāśilā ..
mokṣadā sarvajaṃtūnāṃ tathā pātakanāśinī .. 1 ..
5.40.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
यदेषा भवता प्रोक्ता ब्राह्मी तत्र महाशिला ..
मोक्षदा सर्वजंतूनां तथा पातकनाशिनी .. 1 ..
5.40.m: The seers said: / "Regarding this great stone of Brahmā spoken of by you there, / which grants liberation to all living beings and destroys sins,

5.40.s:
sā kathaṃ sthāpitā tatra kiṃprabhāvā ca sūtaja ..
etanno brūhi niḥśeṣaṃ na hi tṛpyāmahe vayam .. 2 ..
5.40.d:
सा कथं स्थापिता तत्र किंप्रभावा च सूतज ..
एतन्नो ब्रूहि निःशेषं न हि तृप्यामहे वयम् .. 2 ..
5.40.m: how was it established there, and what is its power, O son of Sūta? / Tell us all this completely, for we are not satiated."

5.40.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
brahmalokaniviṣṭasya brahmaṇo' vyaktajanmanaḥ ..
purā'bhūnmahatī cintā tīrthayātrāsamudbhavā .. 3 ..
5.40.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
ब्रह्मलोकनिविष्टस्य ब्रह्मणो' व्यक्तजन्मनः ..
पुराऽभून्महती चिन्ता तीर्थयात्रासमुद्भवा .. 3 ..
5.40.m: Sūta said: / "Formerly, a great concern arose for Brahmā of unmanifest birth, / residing in the world of Brahmā, originating from a pilgrimage to sacred fords:

5.40.s:
sarveṣāmeva devānāṃ saṃti tīrthāni bhūtale ..
muktvā māṃ tanmayā kāryaṃ tīrthamekaṃ dharātale .. 4 ..
5.40.d:
सर्वेषामेव देवानां संति तीर्थानि भूतले ..
मुक्त्वा मां तन्मया कार्यं तीर्थमेकं धरातले .. 4 ..
5.40.m: 'All the gods indeed have sacred fords on the surface of the earth, / except for me; therefore, I must establish a sacred ford on the earth's surface,

5.40.s:
yatra trikālamāsādya karma saṃdhyāsamudbhavam ..
martyalokaṃ samāsādya karomi tadanaṃtaram .. 5 ..
5.40.d:
यत्र त्रिकालमासाद्य कर्म संध्यासमुद्भवम् ..
मर्त्यलोकं समासाद्य करोमि तदनंतरम् .. 5 ..
5.40.m: where, having arrived at the three junctures of the day, reaching the mortal world, / I may then perform the rites arising from the twilight devotions,

5.40.s:
tathānyadapi yatkiñcitkarma dharmyaṃ hitāvaham ..
tatkaromi yathānye'pi cakrurdevāḥ śivādayaḥ .. 6 ..
5.40.d:
तथान्यदपि यत्किञ्चित्कर्म धर्म्यं हितावहम् ..
तत्करोमि यथान्येऽपि चक्रुर्देवाः शिवादयः .. 6 ..
5.40.m: and whatever other righteous, beneficial rite there is, / I may perform that, just as the other gods, Śiva and the rest, have done.

5.40.s:
na svarge'sti hi kṛtyānāmadhikāro'tra kaścana ..
śubhānāṃ karmaṇāmeva kevalaṃ bhujyate phalam .. 7 ..
5.40.d:
न स्वर्गेऽस्ति हि कृत्यानामधिकारोऽत्र कश्चन ..
शुभानां कर्मणामेव केवलं भुज्यते फलम् .. 7 ..
5.40.m: For in heaven there is no eligibility for actions whatsoever; / only the fruit of auspicious deeds is enjoyed here.

5.40.s:
tasmādyatra dharāpṛṣṭhe śileyaṃ nipatiṣyati ..
trisaṃdhyaṃ tatra gantavyamanuṣṭhānārthameva hi .. 8 ..
5.40.d:
तस्माद्यत्र धरापृष्ठे शिलेयं निपतिष्यति ..
त्रिसंध्यं तत्र गन्तव्यमनुष्ठानार्थमेव हि .. 8 ..
5.40.m: Therefore, wherever on the surface of the earth this stone shall fall, / there I must go at the three twilight junctures, solely for the performance of rites.'"

5.40.s:
evamuktvā suvistīrṇāṃ śilāṃ tāmā sanodbhavām ..
pracikṣepa dharāpṛṣṭhaṃ samuddiśya pitāmahaḥ .. 9 ..
5.40.d:
एवमुक्त्वा सुविस्तीर्णां शिलां तामा सनोद्भवाम् ..
प्रचिक्षेप धरापृष्ठं समुद्दिश्य पितामहः .. 9 ..
5.40.m: Having spoken thus, the Grandfather hurled toward the earth's surface / that very expansive stone originating from his seat.

5.40.s:
atha sā patitā bhūmau sarvaratnamayī śilā ..
camatkārapure kṣetre sarvakṣetramahodaye .. 6.40.10 ...
5.40.d:
अथ सा पतिता भूमौ सर्वरत्नमयी शिला ..
चमत्कारपुरे क्षेत्रे सर्वक्षेत्रमहोदये .. 6.40.10 ...
5.40.m: Then that stone, made of all kinds of jewels, fell upon the earth / in the sacred field of Camatkārapura, the source of supreme prosperity among all sacred fields.

5.40.s:
tata āgatya lokeśaḥ svayameva dharātalam ..
tatkṣetraṃ vīkṣayāmāsa vyāptaṃ tīrthaiḥ samantataḥ .. 11 ..
5.40.d:
तत आगत्य लोकेशः स्वयमेव धरातलम् ..
तत्क्षेत्रं वीक्षयामास व्याप्तं तीर्थैः समन्ततः .. 11 ..
5.40.m: Then the lord of the world, having personally come to the surface of the earth, / looked upon that sacred field filled on all sides with sacred fords.

5.40.s:
tataḥ puṇyatame deśe dṛṣṭvā tāṃ samupasthitām ..
śilāmānaṃdamāpannaḥ provāca tadanantaram .. 12 ..
aho dhanyatamo matto nānyo'sti bhuvanatraye ..
sarvatīrthamaye kṣetre yato jātātra saṃsthitiḥ ...3..
5.40.d:
ततः पुण्यतमे देशे दृष्ट्वा तां समुपस्थिताम् ..
शिलामानंदमापन्नः प्रोवाच तदनन्तरम् .. 12 ..
अहो धन्यतमो मत्तो नान्योऽस्ति भुवनत्रये ..
सर्वतीर्थमये क्षेत्रे यतो जातात्र संस्थितिः ...3..
5.40.m:
Then, seeing that stone positioned in the most sacred place, / he was filled with joy and spoke thereafter:
"Ah, there is none more fortunate than me in the three worlds, / since my presence has come to be here in a sacred field consisting of all sacred fords!

5.40.s:
salilena vinā yasmānna kriyā saṃpravartate ..
tasmādatra mayā kāryaḥ śucitoyo mahāhradaḥ .. 14 ..
5.40.d:
सलिलेन विना यस्मान्न क्रिया संप्रवर्तते ..
तस्मादत्र मया कार्यः शुचितोयो महाह्रदः .. 14 ..
5.40.m: Since no ritual activity proceeds without water, / therefore a great pool of pure water must be made here by me."

5.40.s:
tataḥ saṃciṃtayāmāsa svasutāṃ ca sarasvatīm ..
jana saṃsparśabhītyā ca pātālatalavāhinīm .. 15 ..
5.40.d:
ततः संचिंतयामास स्वसुतां च सरस्वतीम् ..
जन संस्पर्शभीत्या च पातालतलवाहिनीम् .. 15 ..
5.40.m: Then he thought of his daughter Sarasvatī, / who flows in the realm of Pātāla out of fear of the touch of people.

5.40.s:
atha bhūmitalaṃ bhittvā prādurbhūtā mahānadī ..
tāṃ śilāmamalaistoyaiḥ kṣālayantī samaṃtataḥ .. 16 ..
atha mūrtimatī bhūtvā provāca prapitāmaham ..
kimarthaṃ saṃsmṛtā devamamādeśaḥ pradīyatām...7..
5.40.d:
अथ भूमितलं भित्त्वा प्रादुर्भूता महानदी ..
तां शिलाममलैस्तोयैः क्षालयन्ती समंततः .. 16 ..
अथ मूर्तिमती भूत्वा प्रोवाच प्रपितामहम् ..
किमर्थं संस्मृता देवममादेशः प्रदीयताम्...7..
5.40.m:
Then, bursting through the surface of the earth, the great river appeared, / washing that stone on all sides with pure waters.
Then, assuming an embodied form, she spoke to the great-grandfather: / "For what purpose have I been remembered, O god? Let your command be given!"

5.40.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
tvayātraiva sadā stheyaṃ śilāyāṃ mama saṃnidhau ..
saṃdhyātraye'pi tvattoyairyena kṛtyaṃ karomyaham .. 18 ..
5.40.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
त्वयात्रैव सदा स्थेयं शिलायां मम संनिधौ ..
संध्यात्रयेऽपि त्वत्तोयैर्येन कृत्यं करोम्यहम् .. 18 ..
5.40.m: Brahmā said: / "You must always remain right here upon the stone in my presence, / so that with your waters I may perform rites at all three twilight junctures.

5.40.s:
tathā ye mānavāḥ snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti jale tava ..
te yāsyaṃti parāṃ siddhiṃ durlabhāṃ devā mānuṣaiḥ .. 19 ..
5.40.d:
तथा ये मानवाः स्नानं करिष्यंति जले तव ..
ते यास्यंति परां सिद्धिं दुर्लभां देवा मानुषैः .. 19 ..
5.40.m: Likewise, the mortals who take a ritual ablution in your water / shall attain the supreme perfection difficult to obtain even by gods and humans."

5.40.s:
.. sarasvatyuvāca .. ..
ahaṃ kanyā suraśreṣṭha pātālatalavāhinī ..
janasparśabhayādbhītā nāgacchāmi mahītale .. 6.40.20 ..
5.40.d:
.. सरस्वत्युवाच .. ..
अहं कन्या सुरश्रेष्ठ पातालतलवाहिनी ..
जनस्पर्शभयाद्भीता नागच्छामि महीतले .. 6.40.20 ..
5.40.m: Sarasvatī said: / "I am an unmarried maiden, O best of gods, flowing in the realm of Pātāla; / terrified of the fear of human touch, I will not come to the earth's surface.

5.40.s:
tavādeśo'nyathā naiva mayā kāryaḥ kathaṃcana ..
evaṃ matvā suraśreṣṭha yadyuktaṃ tatsamācara .. 21 ..
5.40.d:
तवादेशोऽन्यथा नैव मया कार्यः कथंचन ..
एवं मत्वा सुरश्रेष्ठ यद्युक्तं तत्समाचर .. 21 ..
5.40.m: Yet your command must by no means be disobeyed by me. / Considering this, O best of gods, do whatever is fitting."

5.40.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
tavārthe kalpayiṣyāmi sthāne'traiva mahāhradam ..
agamyaṃ sarvamartyānāṃ tatra tvaṃ sthātumarhasi .. 22 ..
5.40.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
तवार्थे कल्पयिष्यामि स्थानेऽत्रैव महाह्रदम् ..
अगम्यं सर्वमर्त्यानां तत्र त्वं स्थातुमर्हसि .. 22 ..
5.40.m: Brahmā said: / "For your sake I shall fashion a great pool right in this place, / inaccessible to all mortals; you should dwell there."

5.40.s:
evamuktvā sa deveśaścakhāna ca mahāhradam ..
tataḥ sarasvatī tatra svasthānamakaro datha .. 23 ..
5.40.d:
एवमुक्त्वा स देवेशश्चखान च महाह्रदम् ..
ततः सरस्वती तत्र स्वस्थानमकरो दथ .. 23 ..
5.40.m: Having spoken thus, the lord of gods dug a great pool. / Then Sarasvatī took up her abode there.

5.40.s:
tato dṛṣṭiviṣānsarpānādideśa pitāmahaḥ ..
yuṣmābhiḥ sarvadā stheyaṃ hradesmiñchāsanānmama .. 24 ..
5.40.d:
ततो दृष्टिविषान्सर्पानादिदेश पितामहः ..
युष्माभिः सर्वदा स्थेयं ह्रदेस्मिञ्छासनान्मम .. 24 ..
5.40.m: Then the Grandfather commanded serpents whose glance is venomous: / "By my order, you must always abide in this pool.

5.40.s:
yathā sarasvatīṃ martyā na spṛśaṃti kathaṃcana ..
bhavadbhiḥ sarvathā kāryaṃ tathā pannagasattamāḥ .. 25 ..
5.40.d:
यथा सरस्वतीं मर्त्या न स्पृशंति कथंचन ..
भवद्भिः सर्वथा कार्यं तथा पन्नगसत्तमाः .. 25 ..
5.40.m: You must act in every way, O best of serpents, / so that mortals do not touch Sarasvatī by any means."

5.40.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ brahmā vyavasthāpya tatra kṣetre sarasvatīm ..
tāṃ ca citraśilāṃ madhye brahmalokaṃ jagāma ha .. 26 ..
5.40.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं ब्रह्मा व्यवस्थाप्य तत्र क्षेत्रे सरस्वतीम् ..
तां च चित्रशिलां मध्ये ब्रह्मलोकं जगाम ह .. 26 ..
5.40.m: Sūta said: / Having thus established Sarasvatī in that sacred field, / and that wondrous stone in the middle, Brahmā indeed went to the world of Brahmā.

5.40.s:
atha maṃkaṇakonāma maharṣiḥ saṃśitavrataḥ ..
kṣetre tatra samāyāto viṣavidyāvicakṣaṇaḥ .. 27 ..
5.40.d:
अथ मंकणकोनाम महर्षिः संशितव्रतः ..
क्षेत्रे तत्र समायातो विषविद्याविचक्षणः .. 27 ..
5.40.m: Then a great seer named Maṅkaṇaka, strict in his vows / and expert in the science of poisons, arrived at that sacred field.

5.40.s:
sakramādbhramamāṇastu tasminsarpābhirakṣite ..
taṃ muniṃ veṣṭayāmāsurbabandhuścaiva pāśakaiḥ .. 28 ..
5.40.d:
सक्रमाद्भ्रममाणस्तु तस्मिन्सर्पाभिरक्षिते ..
तं मुनिं वेष्टयामासुर्बबन्धुश्चैव पाशकैः .. 28 ..
5.40.m: While he was wandering about in order in that [pool] guarded by serpents, / they encircled that sage and bound him with their coils.

5.40.s:
so'pi vidyābalātsarpānnirviṣāṃstāṃścakāraha ..
tatra snātvā śucirbhūtvā kṛtvā ca pitṛtarpaṇam ..
niṣkrāṃtaḥ salilāttasmātkṛtakṛtyo mudānvitaḥ .. 29 ..
5.40.d:
सोऽपि विद्याबलात्सर्पान्निर्विषांस्तांश्चकारह ..
तत्र स्नात्वा शुचिर्भूत्वा कृत्वा च पितृतर्पणम् ..
निष्क्रांतः सलिलात्तस्मात्कृतकृत्यो मुदान्वितः .. 29 ..
5.40.m: He too, by the power of his science, rendered those serpents venomless. / Having bathed there, become pure, and offered libations to the ancestors, / he emerged from that water, having accomplished his purpose and filled with joy.

5.40.s:
tataścakre muniryāvatsamyakkuśaparigraham ..
darbhāgreṇāsya hastāgraṃ pāṭitaṃ tāvadeva hi .. 6.40.30 ..
5.40.d:
ततश्चक्रे मुनिर्यावत्सम्यक्कुशपरिग्रहम् ..
दर्भाग्रेणास्य हस्ताग्रं पाटितं तावदेव हि .. 6.40.30 ..
5.40.m: Then, as soon as the sage properly gathered the kuśa grass, / the tip of his hand was pierced by the tip of a darbha blade. 6.40.30

5.40.s:
atha tasmātkṣatājjātastasya śākaraso mahān ..
taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa viśeṣeṇa harṣito vismayānvitaḥ .. 31 ..
5.40.d:
अथ तस्मात्क्षताज्जातस्तस्य शाकरसो महान् ..
तं दृष्ट्वा स विशेषेण हर्षितो विस्मयान्वितः .. 31 ..
5.40.m: Then, from that wound, an abundance of plant sap flowed out. / Seeing that, he became especially joyous and filled with wonder. 31

5.40.s:
siddho'hamiti vijñāya nṛtyaṃ cakre tataḥ param ..
brāhmīṃ śilāṃ samāruhya ānaṃdāśrupariplutaḥ .. 32 ..
5.40.d:
सिद्धोऽहमिति विज्ञाय नृत्यं चक्रे ततः परम् ..
ब्राह्मीं शिलां समारुह्य आनंदाश्रुपरिप्लुतः .. 32 ..
5.40.m: Realising, 'I have achieved perfection,' he then began to dance; / climbing onto the rock sacred to Brahmā, he was overwhelmed with tears of joy. 32

5.40.s:
athaivaṃ nṛtyamānasya munestasya mahātmanaḥ ..
lāsyaṃ cakre tataḥ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam .. 33 ..
5.40.d:
अथैवं नृत्यमानस्य मुनेस्तस्य महात्मनः ..
लास्यं चक्रे ततः सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजंगमम् .. 33 ..
5.40.m: Now, as that great-souled sage was dancing in this manner, / the entire world, both immovable and moving, began to dance. 33

5.40.s:
camatkārapuraṃ kṛtsnaṃ bhagnaṃ naṣṭā dvijottamāḥ ..
prāsādairdhvaṃsitaistatra hāhākāro mahānabhūt ..34..
5.40.d:
चमत्कारपुरं कृत्स्नं भग्नं नष्टा द्विजोत्तमाः ..
प्रासादैर्ध्वंसितैस्तत्र हाहाकारो महानभूत् ..34..
5.40.m: The whole of Camatkārapura was broken; the best of brahmins fled; / as palaces collapsed there, a great cry of despair arose. 34

5.40.s:
]tato devagaṇāḥ sarve taddṛṣṭvā tasya ceṣṭitam..
lāsyasya vāraṇārthāya procurvṛṣabhavāhanam.. 35 ..
5.40.d:
]ततो देवगणाः सर्वे तद्दृष्ट्वा तस्य चेष्टितम्..
लास्यस्य वारणार्थाय प्रोचुर्वृषभवाहनम्.. 35 ..
5.40.m: Then all the hosts of gods, seeing his actions, / spoke to the bull-vehicled [Śiva] to stop his dance: 35
